title: Fund Accounting (Alternatives) Associate 2
description:
Who are we looking for?   
 
 You!  As part of our current operations in Ireland we have a number of roles at  graduate and entry level available within our Fund Accounting Group. 
 
 What we can offer you?   
We are the largest financial administrator in Ireland, servicing global market leading clients across a variety of product types including ETFS, CCFs, Multi Manager funds, Fund of Funds, Alternative UCITS, Private Equity and Real Estate Funds. With us, you have the opportunity to develop your career in many different directions within the funds industry. 
 We offer flexibility to blend working from home or office, excellent benefits package, strong personal and career development programmes to support your career journey and much more.  Keep reading to find out more.  
 
 Why this role is important to us: 
Fund Accounting is at the core of our asset servicing solutions for our clients allowing State Street to give asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. 
 
This is a team providing a crucial operational service for clients worldwide, and you will work with a range of internal teams across the globe to service a wide array of prominent clients across multiple fund types. 
 
 Roles Available and What You Will Be Responsible For: 
 
 Fund Accounting – NAV calculation   
 
Be part of a new team with great opportunities for career growth. The role will involve the processing and review of accounting activity. The team take responsibility for the accuracy of the NAV (Net Asset Value) per share published to the marketplace and liaise with other supporting departments to ensure the standards are kept high. This is an exciting time to join as the team is establishing a large footprint in Ireland. 
 
 Fund Accounting – NAV Oversight   
 
With responsibility for a portfolio of clients the team oversees client deliverables on a daily basis. This includes the publication of the NAV along with any supporting information and queries our clients have on the funds valuation. 
  
 What We Value:  
 
These skills will help you succeed in this role. 
 Team skills – demonstrated ability to work with people at different levels. 
 Excellent communication skills – verbal and written.
 Attention to detail and accuracy.
 Ability to meet key deliverables within stated timeframes. 
 Proactive approach. 
 
 Experience/Qualifications: 

 A primary degree is all we ask, but Finance or Accountancy knowledge will provide a great start for you 
 Experience working with Microsoft Office.
 
 About State Street 
 Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

 We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.

Work mode:
Onsite
Onsite Location(s):
Clonmel, Ireland
Diversity - Innovation - Caring - Global Collaboration - Winning Spirit - High Performance
At Boston Scientific, we’ll give you the opportunity to harness all that’s within you by working in teams of diverse and high-performing employees, tackling some of the most important health industry challenges. With access to the latest tools, information and training, we’ll help you in advancing your skills and career. Here, you’ll be supported in progressing – whatever your ambitions.
Advancing possibilities for a brighter tomorrow
Boston Scientific is seeking a highly motivated Graduate Deployment Analytics Analyst on a defined-term (23months) basis to join our Clonmel team .
Job Purpose:
Start your career where your ideas, curiosity and technical skills can make a meaningful difference. As a Graduate Engineer/Analyst at Boston Scientific, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues, contribute to innovative medical technologies and build hands-on experience in a collaborative environment.
Provide deployment intelligence through analytics, reporting automation, readiness insights and AI-enabled decision support.
This is an opportunity to apply what you learned during your studies, develop your technical and problem-solving capabilities and gain valuable experience while contributing to technologies designed to improve patients' lives.
Key Responsibilities:
Deployment Analytics
Develop deployment readiness dashboards using Power BI or other visualization tools.
Analyze deployment metrics and trends.
Support executive reporting and the preparation of PowerPoint presentations.
Risk and Readiness Insights
Analyze readiness progression.
Support the product owner in identifying major deployment challenges and developing technical solutions.
Create deployment performance scorecards.
Reporting Automation
Develop Power BI dashboards.
Create automated reporting processes.
Support key performance indicator standardization.
Validate AI-generated reports.
Education & Experience:
Hons Bachelor Degree (Level 8) in engineering or science is essential.
Graduated within the past two years or currently in the final year of university.
Relevant work experience or completion of a co-op program, ideally within or knowledge of industrial engineering and supply chain analytics.
Eligibility to work in Ireland.
Strong communication and teamwork skills, with the initiative to contribute in a collaborative environment.
Strong systems aptitude and an interest in developing technical skills, interest in information systems.
Enthusiastic, proactive approach to learning and problem-solving.
Interest in medical technology, manufacturing, product development or continuous improvement.
Strong analytics, data science and statistical skills.
What we can offer you
Competitive Benefits – we offer market leading benefits including performance-related bonus, pension contribution, onsite gym, onsite parking, subsidised canteen, organised social groups and healthcare.
A Career with Meaningful Purpose   – opportunity to transform the lives of patients worldwide.
Our Culture   - our work is guided by core values that define our culture and empower our employees.
Career Development   – our highly engaged leaders will empower you to grow and will invest in your potential. You can also broaden your skills through personal development courses.
Opportunity to Innovate   – we encourage you to fulfil your true creative potential by speaking up with your ideas and solutions to problems that matter.
Work-Life Balance   – we have created a culture that acknowledges, respects and supports your life and work choices.
Corporate Social Responsibility   – we are dedicated to progressing business practices in areas important to our communities. Our onsite charity events have raised over €1.5 million for worthy causes in the past ten years.
Boston Scientific Ireland Graduate Programme cosing date is 22nd November 2026.
As a leader in medical science for more than 40 years, we are committed to solving the challenges that matter most – united by a deep caring for human life. Our mission to advance science for life is about transforming lives through innovative medical solutions that improve patient lives, create value for our customers, and support our employees and the communities in which we operate. Now more than ever, we have a responsibility to apply those values to everything we do – as a global business and as a global corporate citizen.
So, choosing a career with Boston Scientific isn’t just business, it’s personal. And if you’re a natural problem-solver with the imagination, determination, and spirit to make a meaningful difference to people worldwide, we encourage you to apply and look forward to connecting with you!

title: Associate, Fund Accounting – Private Debt
description:
We are global private markets specialists delivering tailored investment solutions, advisory services, and impactful, data driven insights to the world’s investors. Leveraging the power of our platform and our peerless intelligence across sectors, strategies, and geographies, we help identify the advantages and the answers our clients need to succeed.

Position Overview

The Associate of StepStone Private Debt – Fund Accounting in Dublin will be responsible for performing shadow accounting of StepStone funds, will oversee all activities related to a fund on a daily basis and will coordinate and reconcile with the fund administrators. The Associate will be in contact with professionals across the company and will work closely with team members in other StepStone offices and Departments on a regular basis.

 

Essential Job Functions:

  • Perform a Final Review before release of NAV valuations of private debt funds and fund of funds (Shadow accounting)
  • In-dept review of complex management and performance fees calculation
  • Review and maintain all fund holdings for inclusion in both NAVs and periodic Investor reporting
  • Continuous review of controls in place with the objective of mitigating risk both internally and externally
  • Monitor and review foreign currency hedging activities within the portfolio and the effects of FX Neutralisation within the NAV
  • Budget and track fund’s fees and expenses periodically
  • Track and monitor subscriptions / redemptions, capital calls, withdrawals, dividends, etc. are applied at the appropriate period.
  • Collect and reconcile data from and between Investment Advisor, Investment Manager and Fund Administrator; filing and input into the proprietary database
  • Ensure quality and integrity of the data inputs through reasonability checks
  • Assist with development of junior staff
  • Assist in client reports production for a variety of our portfolios and ensuring quality and timliness thereof; internal as well as external coordination regarding the content of the individual reports
  • Perform other duties as requested or as responsibilities dictate
  • Continuously work towards improving the overall process through efficiencies and collaboration
  • Review and perform monthly IRR checks to ensure these are within expectation and highlight areas where this is not achieved with the relevant internal teams
  • Actively be involved in the Onboarding and Offboarding of Funds from inception to liquidation

 Education and/or Work Experience Requirements:

  • 4-6 years in a comparable role
  • Bachelor degree in finance, Accounting or mathematical-related subject

 Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Demonstrates commitment, accuracy and attention to detail, even in a high-volume, fast-paced environment
  • Highly motivated with a passion for the industry
  • Knowledge of the private debt- / private equity- or hedge-fund sectors
  • Experience in audit, fund accounting and/or custody in one of the above sectors
  • Passion for fast-paced learning, especially in a technology-enabled environment
  • Good analytical skills with a flair for processes as well as good IT skills
  • Takes initiative and ownership of responsibilities assigned
  • Ability to prioritize activities while working on multiple projects and achieve target deadlines
  • Strong interpersonal, collaborative and Investor servicing skills
  • Promote and demonstrate a positive, team‐oriented attitude
  • Effective communication skills and strong problem solving skills
  • Highly proficient in using Excel, Word, and other Microsoft office programs
  • Experience with FX hedging and complex fee calculation models

 Other Attributes:

  • Experience with Investran a plus
  • Possess an accreditation like an ACCA, ACA, CFA, CPA, CIA, or CAIA
  • Passion for fast-paced learning, especially in a technology-enabled environment
  • Strong analytical skills with a flair for processes as well as good IT skills

title: Commercial Finance: Data Analytics & Reporting Co-Op
description:
Work Flexibility: Onsite 
 
 This role will be based in one of our Cork sites.
 
 Throughout the placement, you will be an integral part of Stryker’s 2027 Cooperative cohort.
 
 The North Europe Commercial Finance team supports Stryker’s commercial operations across six countries (Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Sweden, Finland & Norway), working closely with sales leadership, business units and the wider EMEA Finance organisation. The team supports a business with more than $350M in annual revenue and provides insight to help drive sustainable growth, profitability and cash flow.
 
 This placement sits at the intersection of Finance and Commercial Operations. The successful candidate will gain hands-on exposure to regional performance management, business partnering, planning and forecasting, and digital reporting. You will be given meaningful ownership, supported by experienced finance colleagues, and encouraged to improve how information is delivered to decision-makers.
 
 For this undergraduate placement, we’re looking for someone who brings both a strong interest in Finance and a passion for Digitalisation. The ideal candidate will be excited to apply their analytical and technical skills to improve reporting capabilities and unlock business insights.
 
 Tasks and responsibilities may include: 
 Digital reporting and process improvement: Using Excel, Power BI, Co Pilot and other approved analytics tools to automate recurring work, improve data quality, reduce manual effort and create intuitive dashboards or visualisations for commercial stakeholders.

 Ad hoc decision support: Contribute to short-cycle analytical projects, including market or portfolio reviews, investment proposals, scenario modelling and other emerging business questions across North Europe.

 Controls and data governance: Apply disciplined review, documentation and version-control practices. Help ensure analyses are traceable, assumptions are clearly stated and sensitive information is handled appropriately.

 Month-end and management reporting: Support selected month-end activities relevant to commercial finance, including reporting checks, accrual support, management-account review and preparation of clear performance commentary.

 Variance and trend analysis: Compare actual results with budget, forecast and prior periods. Work with finance colleagues and commercial partners to understand movements and document the commercial story behind the numbers.

 Forecasting and budgeting: Support monthly forecasts, annual budget activities and longer-range planning. Assist with data collection, model updates, reasonableness checks, consolidation and preparation of management materials.

 
 What you will learn: 
 How a regional commercial finance team supports growth and profitability in a multi-country healthcare business.

 How to move from financial data to clear, actionable insight for commercial decision-makers.

 How forecasting, budgeting, month-end reporting and performance reviews connect across the business cycle.

 How to communicate financial analysis confidently to both finance and non-finance stakeholders.

 How digital tools and strong process design can improve the speed, quality and consistency of finance support.

 
 What you will need: 
 A strong interest in commercial finance, business performance and digitalisation.

 Confidence working with numbers, with a careful and structured approach to analysis and data quality.

 High proficiency in Excel and a keen interest in developing Power BI, automation, AI or broader analytics skills.

 Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain analysis in a simple and practical way.

 Curiosity, initiative and a willingness to ask thoughtful questions and take ownership.

 An organised, collaborative and adaptable approach in a fast-paced, international environment.

 
 To be eligible: 
 Enrolled at an Irish or Northern Irish university for the duration of the cooperative placement.

 Available for either 6, 9 or 12 months – exact duration and start date to be discussed with your Talent Acquisition Business Partner at Stryker.

 
 What we can offer: 
 Attractive salary & vacation entitlement

 Experience our inclusive, people-first culture . You will be paired with mentors and have access to leaders who support your growth, give constructive feedback, and help build confidence. 

 Flexible working hours

 Sports & Social  clubs and DE&I  Employee Resource Groups  and the opportunity to  connect with other co-ops 

 The opportunity to contribute to real-world projects that make a difference in improving healthcare and patients’ lives. In Stryker, you will be given responsibilities that truly matter.

 
 Next steps: 
 Once you have applied to one of our co-op opportunities, our dedicated University Recruiting Business Partners will take some time to look through your application and ensure you meet the criteria in relation to the specific position.

 Should all requirements be met, and you are happy to proceed, in September, successful candidates will be invited to a final round business interview with the hiring team.

 If successful through the final round business interview, you will receive your offer shortly after.

 Please note, individual recruitment timelines may vary – please keep in contact with your University Recruiting Business Partner and your university placement coordinator for specific timelines and updates.

   
  
 Ireland: €30,000 EUR Annual
   
  
 If you’d like to learn more about the compensation associated with this opportunity, your recruiter will be happy to walk you through the details as you progress through the hiring process.
  
   
Travel Percentage: None

title: 2027 Advisory Graduate Programme – Dublin
description:
Graduate Programme 2027 - Build your future in Advisory  
 Advisory work is rarely confined to one discipline. Our clients come to us with complex, connected challenges, and our teams bring together commercial, financial, digital, risk and transformation expertise to help solve them. We work with organisations at every stage of their business journey, from growth and transformation to transactions, risk management, technology adoption, financial reporting and operational improvement.  
 That means graduates can build transferable skills from the outset, while still indicating where their interests and strengths may best fit across Advisory.
 Applying to Advisory 
 You will submit one application to the Advisory Graduate Programme and select your choice of capability preference. This helps us understand where your interests lie while allowing us to consider your skills, strengths and aspirations.
 Capability Preferences 
 Transactions – Deal Advisory, M&A, Restructuring & Recovery, Valuations, Transaction Support and Aviation Advisory
 Management Consulting – Strategy, Transformation Excellence, Change Programs, Workforce Management
 AI, Data & Technology – Data Governance and Responsible AI, Analytics, System Strategy & Implementation
 Accounting – Financial Reporting, statutory reporting, transaction accounting and finance transformation
 Cyber & Risk – Cyber, AML, Internal Audit, IT Risk, Regulatory Compliance
 Quants and Actuarial – Quantitative Risk Advisory, Insurance & Actuarial
 Transactions 
 Help clients make confident decisions during some of the most important moments in their business journey.
 Support financial and commercial due diligence engagements
 Assist with mergers, acquisitions, disposals and fundraising projects
 Contribute to business valuations and financial modelling
 Support restructuring and recovery assignments
 Analyse financial and operational performance
 Prepare reports, presentations and client deliverables
 Support aviation-related advisory and finance projects
 This pathway may suit graduates who enjoy commercial analysis, finance, problem-solving and fast-paced project environments
  
 Management Consulting 
  
 Help organisations turn strategy into action and deliver meaningful change.
 Support business transformation and change programmes
 Participate in stakeholder workshops and client engagements
 Conduct business research and structured analysis
 Assist with programme and project management
 Identify opportunities for process and operating-model improvement
 Develop presentations, reports and recommendations
 Support organisational and workforce transformation initiatives
 This pathway may suit graduates who enjoy problem-solving, communication, storytelling, collaboration and working across industries.
  
 AI, Data & Technology 
  
 Help organisations use technology, data and AI to create better business outcomes.
 Support data analytics, reporting and insight initiatives
 Assist in developing dashboards and management information solutions
 Work with Power BI and Microsoft technologies
 Support data governance and data-quality programmes
 Contribute to responsible AI-enabled business transformation
 Assist with digital and technology-enabled process improvement
 Translate business needs into practical technology and data solutions
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in data, analytics, technology, engineering, innovation and business problem-solving. Technical qualifications are welcomed, but curiosity and willingness to learn are also important.
 Accounting  
  
 Help organisations navigate complex financial reporting, accounting and finance-transformation challenges.
 Support accounting and financial-reporting assignments
 Assist clients with statutory reporting matters
 Help prepare and review financial statements
 Conduct accounting and regulatory research
 Support finance-transformation initiatives
 Assist with the implementation of new accounting standards
 Contribute to transaction-related accounting projects
 Analyse financial information and business performance
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in accounting, finance, reporting and commercial problem-solving.
 Cyber & Risk 
  
 Help organisations manage uncertainty, strengthen governance and build resilience.
 Support internal-audit and assurance engagements
 Assist with enterprise risk-management projects
 Participate in risk assessments and control reviews
 Support governance, compliance and regulatory initiatives
 Analyse business, operational and risk information
 Contribute to cyber-risk and operational-resilience programmes
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in risk, investigation, technology, governance, regulation and how organisations operate.
 Quants & Actuarial  
  
 Help organisations understand complex financial, insurance and risk challenges through data, modelling and actuarial insight.
 Develop quantitative solutions to complex risk measurement questions
 Contribute to actuarial and insurance advisory engagements
 Analyse business, financial and risk data.
 Prepare reports, presentations and recommendations for clients.
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in mathematics, statistics, actuarial science, finance, insurance, regulation and solving complex problems through quantitative analysis.
 As a graduate within Advisory, you will benefit from 
 Exposure to diverse client projects across industries
 Structured learning and career-development opportunities 
 Dedicated coaching, mentoring and peer support
 Professional qualification support where relevant
 Early responsibility and client interaction
 Opportunities to collaborate across Advisory and the wider firm
 Access to national and international colleagues and expertise
 Who We're Looking For 
  
 We are looking for curious, ambitious and collaborative graduates from a wide variety of academic backgrounds. Successful candidates will demonstrate:
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
 Clear written and verbal communication
 Intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn

title: Business Analyst

 At Davy, it’s the unique talents of all our people that have been the foundations of our success for 100 years. As we continue to grow, so do you. Because you are not just part of our team – you are a key player in shaping our future. 
 At Davy, you are the difference.  
 Established in 1926, the Davy Group sits at the heart of wealth and capital in Ireland, providing a broad range of services to high-net-worth individuals, self-directed investors, small-to-medium enterprises, credit unions, corporations, and domestic & international institutional investors. 
 Our culture is shaped around three values, which are at the heart of everything we do: client success, one Davy, and building a proud legacy. Sharing the same goals, we work together to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients. As part of a team of over 900, you will be encouraged to learn and to grow, both professionally and personally. 
 About the role 
 An exciting opportunity has opened up in Commercial Team / Davy Private Clients. In the role, the successful candidate will:
 
 Reporting & Performance Analysis 
 Produce and maintain regular management reports and dashboards.
 Monitor and analyse key business metrics, trends and performance indicators.
 Identify opportunities, risks and emerging trends through data analysis.
 Support the delivery of business performance reporting to management and key stakeholders.
 Develop reporting solutions that improve visibility, consistency and decision-making.
 Business Analysis & Decision Support 
 Conduct forecasting, trend analysis and scenario modelling to support business planning.
 Analyse business performance and provide actionable insights and recommendations.
 Assist management in evaluating business opportunities and areas for improvement.
 Support budgeting, forecasting and planning activities through analytical input.
 Translate data into meaningful management information and business intelligence.
 Performance Management Support 
 Support the production and ongoing development of performance scorecards and reporting frameworks.
 Assist in tracking performance against agreed objectives and key metrics.
 Provide analytical support to managers and business stakeholders.
 Ensure performance data is accurate, timely and actionable.
 Contribute to the continuous improvement of performance measurement processes.
 Data Management & Governance 
 Support data quality improvement initiatives across business systems and processes.
 Assist in maintaining data integrity, consistency and governance standards.
 Identify data issues and work with stakeholders to implement corrective actions.
 Contribute to the development and enhancement of reporting and data management processes.
 Support business readiness activities associated with system and technology initiatives.
 Stakeholder Engagement 
 Build strong working relationships across business functions.
 Act as a key liaison between operational teams and support functions in relation to reporting and analysis requirements.
 Gather and document business requirements for reporting and analytical needs.
 Present findings, insights and recommendations in a clear and concise manner.
 Support projects and initiatives that require analytical expertise and business insight.
 Requirements

 Essential 
 Third-level qualification in Business, Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Data Analytics, Information Systems or a related discipline.

 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex data sets.
 Experience producing management information, performance reporting and business insights.
 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
 Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
 Strong organisational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities.

title: Associate Consultant, Transfer Agency (Dealing Team)
description:
About Northern Trust 

 As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. 

 Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. 

 With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. 

 Role / Department 
 The Associate Consultant role operates within a dedicated Dealing Team in the Transfer Agency Department. The role provides experienced technical and operational support across day-to-day dealing activities, taking increased ownership for assigned clients, operational deliverables, issue resolution and the effective application of established processes and controls.
 Reporting to the Dealing Manager, the Associate Consultant acts as a key point of support for the wider team, assisting with complex operational queries, workflow coordination and the development of less experienced partners. The role works closely with the Consultant and Dealing Manager to support consistent service delivery, operational quality and the timely escalation and resolution of issues.
 The Transfer Agency Department provides fund administration services to multiple Fund Management companies, delivering the full range of shareholder servicing functions including Dealing, Registration, Finance and Investor Services. The department operates across multiple locations and provides partners with opportunities to develop their knowledge, experience and careers.
  
 Key Responsibilities 
 The key responsibilities of the role include: 
 Take ownership of assigned clients and support the effective delivery of day-to-day TA Dealing activities, ensuring agreed service requirements and deadlines are met.
 Provide experienced operational and technical support to the Dealing team, assisting with the investigation and resolution of more complex processing queries and exceptions.
 Act as an escalation point for operational queries from junior team members and offshore partners, escalating material or higher-risk matters to the Consultant or Dealing Manager as appropriate.
 Support the day-to-day oversight of processing quality, accuracy and timeliness, including activities performed by offshore TA Dealing teams.
 Monitor workflow queues and operational priorities, identifying outstanding items, potential issues and capacity concerns and escalating where appropriate.
 Prepare and review accurate and timely client and operational reporting, including prediction, cash and register reporting.
 Ensure assigned client and operational deliverables are completed accurately and within agreed timeframes.
 Maintain accurate and up-to-date procedures, checklists and supporting documentation, identifying areas requiring clarification or improvement.
 Complete applicable data-protection checks and ensure external communications are issued in accordance with TA policies, procedures and control requirements.
 Support the identification, investigation and escalation of operational risks, errors and control issues, contributing to timely resolution and appropriate follow-up.
 Provide day-to-day guidance and knowledge sharing to less experienced partners, supporting cross-training and the development of technical knowledge within the team.
 Support process reviews and continuous-improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing operational quality, efficiency and the client or investor experience.
 Contribute to projects, client onboarding, system or process changes and other business initiatives within the scope of the role.
 Work collaboratively with other Transfer Agency functions, including New Business, Investor Services, Registration and Finance, as well as relevant internal stakeholders.
 Respond to client and investor queries accurately and within agreed service expectations.
 Maintain a strong understanding of assigned dealing processes and relevant systems and apply that knowledge to support effective operational delivery.
 Comply with applicable regulatory requirements and internal Northern Trust policies, procedures and control standards.
  
 Skills / Qualifications 
 The successful candidate will benefit from having: 
  
 Relevant experience within Transfer Agency, Fund Administration or Financial Services, preferably within a Dealing environment.
 Strong working knowledge of Transfer Agency operations and a good understanding of the end-to-end dealing process.
 Ability to investigate and resolve operational queries and exceptions, applying sound judgement and escalating appropriately when required.
 Good understanding of operational risk, controls and escalation requirements.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess information and identify appropriate actions.
 Experience taking ownership of client or operational deliverables and working effectively to agreed deadlines.
 Strong accuracy and attention to detail, with a focus on maintaining high standards of operational quality.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with clients, colleagues and internal stakeholders.
 Experience supporting, coaching or sharing technical knowledge with less experienced team members.
 Strong planning, organisation and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
 A collaborative approach and the ability to build effective working relationships across teams and functional areas.
 Good PC skills, including Microsoft Word and Excel, with the ability to learn relevant business systems and dealing platforms.
 Knowledge of the fund administration and relevant regulatory environment.
 A flexible, professional and proactive approach to changing business and client requirements.
 Ability to work independently within defined responsibilities while contributing effectively as part of the wider team.am.
  

 Work Authorization 

 Applicants must have the right to work in Ireland at the time of application and for the duration of employment.

 Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide employment permit sponsorship for this role. This includes Critical Skills Employment Permits, General Employment Permits, Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permits, Stamp 1G permissions, and other employment permits under Irish immigration frameworks.

 Working with Us 

 As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve. 

 Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities. 

 Reasonable Accommodation 

 Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com , or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.

title: 2027 Advisory Graduate Programme – Cork
description:
Graduate Programme 2027 - Build your future in Advisory  
 Advisory work is rarely confined to one discipline. Our clients come to us with complex, connected challenges, and our teams bring together commercial, financial, digital, risk and transformation expertise to help solve them. We work with organisations at every stage of their business journey, from growth and transformation to transactions, risk management, technology adoption, financial reporting and operational improvement.    
 That means graduates can build transferable skills from the outset, while still indicating where their interests and strengths may best fit across Advisory. 
 Applying to Advisory 
 You will submit one application to the Advisory Graduate Programme and select up to three capability preferences. This helps us understand where your interests lie while allowing us to consider your skills, strengths and aspirations across the breadth of Advisory. 
 Capability Preferences: 
 Transactions –  Deal Advisory, M&A, Restructuring & Recovery, Valuations, Transaction Support and Aviation Advisory 
 Management Consulting – Strategy, Transformation Excellence, Change Programs, Workforce Management 
 AI, Data & Technology –  Data Governance and Responsible AI, Analytics, System Strategy & Implementation 
 Accounting – Financial Reporting, statutory reporting, transaction accounting and finance transformation 
 Cyber & Risk – Cyber, AML, Internal Audit, IT Risk, Regulatory Compliance 
 Quants and Actuarial –  Quantitative Risk Advisory, Insurance & Actuarial 
  
 Transactions 
 Help clients make confident decisions during some of the most important moments in their business journey. 
 Support financial and commercial due diligence engagements 
 Assist with mergers, acquisitions, disposals and fundraising projects 
 Contribute to business valuations and financial modelling 
 Support restructuring and recovery assignments 
 Analyse financial and operational performance 
 Prepare reports, presentations and client deliverables 
 Support aviation-related advisory and finance projects 
 This pathway may suit graduates who enjoy commercial analysis, finance, problem-solving and fast-paced project environments 
   Management Consulting 
  
 Help organisations turn strategy into action and deliver meaningful change . 
 Support business transformation and change programmes 
 Participate in stakeholder workshops and client engagements 
 Conduct business research and structured analysis 
 Assist with programme and project management 
 Identify opportunities for process and operating-model improvement 
 Develop presentations, reports and recommendations 
 Support organisational and workforce transformation initiatives 
 This pathway may suit graduates who enjoy problem-solving, communication, storytelling, collaboration and working across industries. 
   
 AI, Data & Technology 
 Help organisations use technology, data and AI to create better business outcomes. 
 Support data analytics, reporting and insight initiatives 
 Assist in developing dashboards and management information solutions 
 Work with Power BI and Microsoft technologies 
 Support data governance and data-quality programmes 
 Contribute to responsible AI-enabled business transformation 
 Assist with digital and technology-enabled process improvement 
 Translate business needs into practical technology and data solutions 
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in data, analytics, technology, engineering, innovation and business problem-solving. Technical qualifications are welcomed, but curiosity and willingness to learn are also important. 
 Accounting   
 Help organisations navigate complex financial reporting, accounting and finance-transformation challenges. 
 Support accounting and financial-reporting assignments 
 Assist clients with statutory reporting matters 
 Help prepare and review financial statements 
 Conduct accounting and regulatory research 
 Support finance-transformation initiatives 
 Assist with the implementation of new accounting standards 
 Contribute to transaction-related accounting projects 
 Analyse financial information and business performance 
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in accounting, finance, reporting and commercial problem-solving. 
 Cyber & Risk 
 Help organisations manage uncertainty, strengthen governance and build resilience. 
 Support internal-audit and assurance engagements 
 Assist with enterprise risk-management projects 
 Participate in risk assessments and control reviews 
 Support governance, compliance and regulatory initiatives 
 Analyse business, operational and risk information 
 Contribute to cyber-risk and operational-resilience programmes 
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in risk, investigation, technology, governance, regulation and how organisations operate. 
 Quants & Actuarial   
 Help organisations understand complex financial, insurance and risk challenges through data, modelling and actuarial insight. 
 Develop quantitative solutions to complex risk measurement questions 
 Contribute to actuarial and insurance advisory engagements 
 Analyse business, financial and risk data. 
 Prepare reports, presentations and recommendations for clients. 
 This pathway may suit graduates interested in mathematics, statistics, actuarial science, finance, insurance, regulation and solving complex problems through quantitative analysis . 
 As a graduate within Advisory, you will benefit from: 
 Exposure to diverse client projects across industries 
 Structured learning and career-development opportunities   
 Dedicated coaching, mentoring and peer support 
 Professional qualification support where relevant 
 Early responsibility and client interaction 
 Opportunities to collaborate across Advisory and the wider firm 
 Access to national and international colleagues and expertise 
 Who We're Looking For 
 We are looking for curious, ambitious and collaborative graduates from a wide variety of academic backgrounds. Successful candidates will demonstrate: 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills 
 Clear written and verbal communication 
 Intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn 
 Commercial awareness and sound judgement 
 Attention to detail and commitment to quality 
 Ability to work effectively within teams 
 Adaptability and resilience 
 A genuine interest in helping organisations solve complex challenges 
   
 It would also be helpful if you have 
 Experience gained through an internship, part-time role, volunteering, university society or team-based project. Candidates should be on track to achieve a minimum 2.1 degree classification and possess strong IT skills and a desire to develop as a trusted business advisor. 
 Join Us 
 We welcome applications from a broad range of disciplines. Depending on the capability preference, relevant backgrounds may include business, commerce, economics, accounting, finance, law, psychology, computer science, data science, information systems, mathematics, statistics, physics and engineering. Degree title alone will not determine placement. 
 Our graduate experience is designed to support both breadth and depth. Some graduates may gain exposure across different teams, industries and client challenges before deciding where to specialise; others may begin developing deeper expertise in a particular capability, sector or service line from an early stage. 
 Whichever path you choose, you will be supported within a collaborative Advisory environment, with opportunities to learn, grow and contribute across a wide range of client engagements and programmes.   
 Location and working arrangement:  Cork office, primarily office-based. 
 Application and selection process 
 Apply through link - complete our application form and upload your current CV.  
 Closing date Thursday 22 October 2026.  
 Selection process early November 2026. Start date Q4 2027.

title: Associate, Private Credit Fund Accounting, PFS - Dublin
description:
About this role 
 
 
 Associate, Fund Accounting (Private Credit) 
 
 Company Description 
 HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.
 
 HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”).Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).
 
 The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets.This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally, offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.
 
 Department Description 
 The Fund Accounting team’s primary responsibility is the books and records of the funds.  This responsibility includes oversight, review and reconciliation of the books and records with internal teams including Middle Office, Cash Management, and Asset Management / Valuation as well as with external, third-party fund administrators.  This responsibility includes NAV calculation and review, management and performance fees, expense review and management and capital calls and distributions.  In addition to the core books and records, Fund Accounting works closely with Legal on fund setup and operation, with Product Specialist and Investor Relations on ongoing and ad hoc analysis and with Management Company Accounting on AUM, performance and fee reporting and revenue recognition. 
 
 Position Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         
BlackRock’s Private Financing Solutions division (“PFS”) is currently hiring for an Associate level individual on the Fund Accounting team to support BLK Private Credit Funds. Private Credit is a strategic focus for the firm and this position will be part of a core accounting team in Dublin, Ireland. The position offers significant growth opportunities both organically as the firm expands our product offerings, as well as opportunities to be involved in ongoing platform-wide projects.
 
 The Fund Accounting Associate performs an integral role within the Fund Accounting team and is responsible for review and reconciliation of the funds’ books and records, liaising with both internal departments and external third-party fund administrators.  The Fund Accounting Associate will be involved in the closing of the books including NAV review and reconciliation and partners’ capital statement review among other responsibilities.  Additionally, the Fund Accounting Associate will be involved in fund setup and operation and ad hoc internal and investor requests.
 
 Responsibilities                                                                                                                                                                                 
 Specific responsibilities will include but not be limited to the following:
 Monthly and quarterly closing of the funds’ books with fund administrators
 Preparation and review of partners’ capital statements
 Preparation and review of capital call and distribution calculations and notices
 Review of fund expenses for accuracy and coordination of accruals and payments
 Calculation and review of monthly investor return and NAV estimates
 Preparation and review of quarterly and annual GAAP or IFRS financial statements
 Oversee regulatory compliance with SEC, NFA, and other regulations for the relevant products
 Ad hoc reporting and projects
 
 Candidate Profile 
 Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting or Finance
 5+ years of combined experience in a Fund Accounting role, and/or public accounting role supporting clients within the financial services industry (preferably within Private Credit, Public Credit, Private Equity or Hedge Funds)
 Big four public accounting experience preferred
 Chartered Accountant (or equivalent) preferred
 Strong verbal and written communication skills.
 Positive attitude and willingness to continuously learn.
 Self-motivated with the ability to work in a fast-paced environment with minimal supervision.
 Ability to consistently be attentive to detail while meeting critical deadlines and handling multiple tasks simultaneously.
 Strong organizational skills.
 Thorough knowledge of internal controls
 Ability to work with large volumes of data and maintain high levels of accuracy
 
 


The salary range for Dublin is Euro 75,000 - Euro 95,000 Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy and your total compensation may vary based on role, location, and firm, department and individual performance. 
 
 Our benefits 
 
 To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.
 
 
 Our hybrid work model 
 
 BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.
 
 
Guidance on AI use for candidates 

 At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance  on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.

 About BlackRock 

 At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being.  Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.

 This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.

 To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com . We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn , Instagram , YouTube , X , and TikTok .

 BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.  We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected characteristics at law.

As part of our team, you can explore what motivates and energizes your career goals: partnering with our customers, our communities, and each other.

 Job Description Custody Operations Specialist (Settlements) 

 Our Investment Services businesses continues to be a powerful growth engine for U.S. Bank. It services 600 client relationships across our Global Corporate Trust, Global Custody, Global Fund Services and Depositary business units. 

 Our Global Custody business within Investment Services comprises of Custody, Trade Services, Cash Processing, FX, Asset Servicing, Client Services and Settlements teams. We are currently looking to hire a permanent Custody Operations Specialist for our Settlements team in Dublin. The role is dynamic and fast-paced and provides great exposure, dealing with 90+ Global and US Domestic markets. 

 Key Responsibilities: 
 Monitoring of trade activity to settlement status, investigating root causes of failed settlement. 
 Manually settling trades within internal books and records system.

 Supports internal operational teams with knowledge of trade activity, failed trades, payments, cash and overdraft situations. 
 Maintains high levels of client service with both internal and external clients. 
 Support 100+ global markets and 60+ currencies 
 Involvement in upcoming group projects.

 Maintain and support the investigation of our daily Recons in line with Regulatory Rules. 
 
 Basic Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience / transferrable skills 
 
 Preferred Skills/Experience 
 2-4 years industry experience. 
 Settlement and SWIFT experience desired, but not essential. 
 Able to work under strict multi-currency deadlines. 
 Ability to perform multiple tasks concurrently and meet established deadlines in a dynamic work environment. 
 Strong attention to detail. 
 Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills. 
 Ability to be organised, multitask, and meet deadlines in a dynamic work environment. 
 Effective interpersonal and communication skills, verbal, and written communication. 
 Passionate about client service and delivery. 
 Proficient IT skills, using a variety of software packages including Microsoft Office applications. 
 
 Location expectations

 U.S. Bank is committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation practices in line with local regulatory and legal requirements. Our total rewards approach is designed to attract, retain, and support top talent while ensuring equal pay for work of equal value.
  
 We offer a market-competitive compensation package that includes:
 Clearly defined salary ranges aligned with industry benchmarks and internal equity standards.

 Performance-based incentives for eligible employees (as defined by relevant plan rules), awarded through transparent, objective criteria that recognize both individual and company performance.

 Inclusive equitable benefits that are accessible to all employees and focused around our 3 main pillars of financial wellbeing, health & wellness).

 Continuous development opportunities including training, education support, and career progression pathways based on inclusive and transparent criteria.

 Employee recognition programs that celebrate achievements and milestones for all.

  
 We regularly review our compensation and benefits to ensure they remain competitive, inclusive, and responsive to employee needs and market trends. Further details of the compensation package will be provided upon application.
 
 We encourage candidates to explore the full value of our offer, including monetary and non-monetary benefits, at Employee benefits and development | U.S. Bank | Elavon .
   
 Closing Date

 We aim to provide timely updates throughout the process and encourage early applications to ensure consideration.

About Citco: 
 The market leader. The premier provider. The best in the business. At Citco, we’ve been the front-runner in our field since our incorporation in 1948 led to the evolution of the asset servicing sector itself. This pioneering spirit continues to guide us today as we innovate and expand, push beyond the boundaries of our industry, and shape its future. From working exclusively with hedge funds to serving all alternatives, corporations and private clients, our organization has grown immensely across asset classes and geographies. For us, this progress is a pattern that we’ll only maintain as we move forward, always prioritizing our performance. So for those who want to play at the top of their game and be at the vanguard of their space, we say: Welcome to Citco.
 About the Team & Business Line:

Goodbody Wealth Management Graduate Programme
Start date: September 2027
About Goodbody
For more than 150 years, Goodbody has helped clients make informed financial decisions and move forward with confidence. Today, we are an intelligence-led capital, investment and wealth platform with global reach, connecting insight, expertise and opportunity to deliver exceptional outcomes for businesses, individuals and institutions.
With more than 400 employees across Dublin, London, Cork and Galway, we combine deep expertise with a collaborative culture that enables our people to grow and succeed. Guided by our values and recognised through multiple employer and workplace culture awards, we are committed to creating an inclusive environment where ambition is supported, development is encouraged and careers can flourish.
Wealth Management Graduate Programme
This is an exciting opportunity for ambitious graduates and early career talent who are curious about investments, financial planning and building trusted client relationships. Joining our Wealth Management Graduate Programme in Dublin, you will learn how Goodbody supports clients in achieving their financial goals while gaining practical exposure to one of Ireland’s leading investment-led financial services firms.
As part of the programme, you will build a strong foundation in wealth management through hands-on experience across areas such as Wealth Advisory, Investment Solutions, Client Solutions and Financial Planning. You will work alongside experienced Wealth Executives, Senior Wealth Executives and internal specialists, gaining exposure to client service, portfolio oversight, investment markets, financial planning-led advice and the standards expected in a regulated environment.
What you will experience
You will work alongside experienced investment professionals, gaining hands-on exposure to financial markets, investment management and the delivery of exceptional client outcomes. Through structured training, practical experience and ongoing support, you will develop the technical knowledge, commercial awareness and professional skills needed to build a successful career in wealth management. During the programme, you will:
Develop a strong understanding of investment markets, portfolio management, financial planning and the wealth-management industry, supporting clients at different stages of their financial journey.
Learn how to prepare client meeting materials, investment reviews and portfolio analysis, building the attention to detail, commercial judgement and technical expertise required in a highly regulated environment.
Gain practical experience supporting client relationships, responding to client requests, coordinating account activity and ensuring agreed actions are delivered efficiently and professionally.
Work closely with investment advisors, financial planners and specialist teams to understand how tailored wealth-management solutions are designed and delivered.
Gain exposure to a broad range of client situations, helping you understand how investment, tax, estate and succession-planning considerations come together to support long-term financial wellbeing.
Contribute to research projects, market analysis and business initiatives that support the continued evolution of Goodbody's wealth-management offering.
Build confidence communicating with clients, colleagues and professional advisers, developing the interpersonal and relationship-management skills that are essential to long-term success.
Take increasing responsibility for your work as your experience grows, receiving coaching, mentoring and regular feedback to support your professional development.
You will have access to on-the-job learning, regular feedback, a dedicated buddy, networking opportunities and support for relevant professional development. Y ou will also be placed on an educational pathway via the Institute of Bankers (IOB) that enables you to become a qualified Wealth Advisor at the end of the programme.
We know that early career candidates may not have extensive industry experience. What matters most is your curiosity, motivation, willingness to learn and interest in helping clients make confident financial decisions. If you meet most of the criteria and are excited by the opportunity to build a career in Wealth Management, we encourage you to apply.
About you: what we are looking for
We're interested in talented graduates from a wide range of academic backgrounds. While some candidates may have studied finance, economics or business, others may have discovered an interest in financial services through further study, work experience or personal interest.
A curious and enthusiastic mindset with genuine interest for building a career in wealth management.
A client-focused mindset, with the ability to build positive relationships and communicate clearly and professionally.
Strong analytical skills, attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with information, data and documentation.
A collaborative approach, with enthusiasm for working as part of a team and learning from experienced colleagues.
A proactive and resilient attitude, with the confidence to ask questions, take ownership and manage competing priorities.
Good digital capability, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and a willingness to learn new systems.
An interest in completing relevant professional qualifications, such as QFA, APA, CFP or stockbroking qualifications, with support from Goodbody where appropriate.
Why start your career with Goodbody Wealth Management?
Join one of Ireland's leading wealth managers, working with clients whose needs span investments, financial planning, retirement planning and intergenerational wealth transfer.
Benefit from a graduate programme that combines hands-on experience with structured learning, helping you develop both professionally and personally from the outset of your career.
Receive ongoing coaching, mentoring and support from experienced colleagues who are invested in your success and committed to helping you reach your potential.
Build a strong foundation for a long-term career in financial services, with opportunities to deepen your expertise, pursue professional qualifications and explore different career paths within the business.
Be part of a collaborative and inclusive culture where teamwork, integrity and a shared commitment to exceptional client service are at the heart of everything we do.
Work in an environment that values curiosity, initiative and continuous improvement, where your ideas and contributions are encouraged from day one.
Applications are expected to close on the  25th  October 2026 however, we encourage candidates to apply early as the programme may close sooner if demand is high.
Candidates must be fully authorised to work in Ireland or hold a valid work permit for the full duration of the programme (23 months commencing September 2027).

title: Financial Analyst Intern 2027
description:
There’s a universe of opportunity at Amazon. 
 
At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. From the moment you join, you’re part of something big: building products or services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact. You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless opportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the world. Ready to start your adventure?

What’s in it for you?
An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Finance teams are the strategy drivers to any organization. This role gives you the opportunity to be a part of making business decisions at scale, in a multinational company that still retains is Day One Customer Obsessed start up culture. By being involved in performance metrics, data analysis and financial models, you’ll identify where we can drive better efficiency and productivity to continue reducing costs for our customers while continuously improving our products’ selection.

Key job responsibilities
During your internship you will tackle real-world business challenges, while developing your analytical expertise. As an intern, you will own projects that directly impact our business operations honing your financial acumen and quantitative skills. This hands-on experience will provide you with valuable exposure to corporate finance, data analysis, empower you to build Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions working together with like-minded customer obsessed finance professions. You will be part of strategic decision-making learning from your peers and leaders. You will gain practical insights into financial planning, analysis, and reporting while contributing to initiatives that drive business growth and enhance customer value. This opportunity is ideal for driven individuals looking to launch their careers in finance or broader business. Where is better to learn about innovating at scale than a company that has multinational resources but remains startup at its heart. 

Key Responsibilities:
• Analyze financial data and trends to drive cost optimization and operational efficiency 
• Develop financial reports, forecasts, and KPI dashboards to support strategic decision-making 
• Perform financial assessments that inform business solutions and enhance customer value 
• Implement process automation and data quality improvements 
• Collaborate with stakeholders across teams while building your professional network

A day in the life
Your paid 6-month internship includes: 

• Mentorship: we care about your career aspirations and strive to assign projects based on your interests. You can learn and be curious with access to unlimited virtual trainings on project management, personal brand, communication skills and many more.
• Extra perks for Amazonians such as: exclusive Amazon.ie discount; Gym membership discount; Beta testing on new Amazon products; Free mental health, legal, and financial support for you and your family.
• Get involved: we have with over 13 Amazon Affinity Groups you can join and become an ally to a cause close to your heart (sustainability, diversity, LGBTQ+, mental and/or physical disabilities, local community initiatives, etc.) 
• Taking ownership of your career: because when you succeed, we all win. A successful internship, could lead to a full-time (graduate role) after finishing your university studies.

About the team
• Intern Community: Join a network of fellow interns, where you'll build lasting connections through collaborative projects and social events. Engage with like-minded individuals in specialized interest groups, from sustainability to innovation, expanding your professional network and perspective.
• Amazon Community: Immerse yourself in Amazon's diverse workplace culture, collaborating with professionals across various roles and experience levels to gain invaluable insights and mentorship opportunities.
• Support: Benefit from comprehensive program support, including dedicated mentorship, regular office hours, and IT and HR assistance, ensuring you have the resources needed to succeed.
• Learning Sessions: Accelerate your professional development through exclusive training sessions, access to Amazon's learning platforms, and direct interaction with industry experts, preparing you for future career success.
• Opportunities: Excel in your internship to unlock potential pathways to full-time graduate roles or extended internship programs. Enjoy competitive compensation, relocation assistance, and comprehensive employee benefits while working hard, having fun and making history. 

Every day will be filled with developing new skills and achieving personal growth. Interested? Submitting your application takes less than 10 minutes and cover letters are not required. You will just need to attach your CV and answer a questionnaire. Selected candidates will be invited to an online assessment. If successful, you’ll attend to two rounds of virtual interviews, which take place on the same day. Interviews consist of behavioural questions and a case study, focusing on our Leadership Principles. The entire recruitment process typically takes 3 to 4 weeks. Do note that the selection process and timelines are subject to change, and vary with role and location.

EMEA Student Programs Team
- Currently in your penultimate or final year and working towards a university degree with an anticipated graduation date after the completion of your internship.
- Relevant studies in Economics, Finance, or an Applied Science major (e.g., Engineering, Mathematics, or similar disciplines).
- Available to commence an internship between January and September 2027. Yes, our start dates are flexible! You should then be available for 6 months, full time (40h/week). Internship length is subject to availability.
- Fluent written and verbal communication in English (Level - C1 or higher).
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Excel (e.g. macros, pivots, lookups, VBA).
- You must have the right to work in the country of employment.
- You will be based in Dublin for the duration of the internship. A relocation package may be offered, subject to an eligibility criterion.
- Strong analytical skills and ability to work with large datasets, presenting actionable data-driven insights.
- Excellent communication and teamwork skills, working effectively with others, driving your solutions to Deliver Results.
- Demonstrated curiosity, proactivity, and willingness to take on challenges in an ambiguous, fast-paced environment.
- Data visualization skills, such as proficiency in Tableau, QlikView, PowerPivot, or MicroStrategy, Amazon Quick Sight.
- Oracle, VBA and MySQL/SQL knowledge.
- Basic knowledge of and interest in AI.

We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build. Protecting your privacy and the security of your data is a longstanding top priority for Amazon. Please consult our Privacy Notice ( https://www.amazon.jobs/en/privacy_page ) to know more about how we collect, use and transfer the personal data of our candidates.

title: Business Analyst
description:
About Northern Trust 

 As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. 

 Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. 

 With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. 

 Summary 
The Business Analyst will support the Global Threat Technology within Security Operations by documenting requirements, coordinating operational deliverables, improving reporting processes, and helping convert Security Operations data into actionable management insights. The role will partner with CsIRT, SORT, OSM, GRC, and technology stakeholders to improve clarity, consistency, and execution across Security Operations.

 Key responsibilities 
• Gather, document, and validate business requirements for SecOps metrics, dashboards, workflow improvements, and governance routines.
• Support OSM reporting packages, KPI / KRI tracking, action item follow-up, and recurring management updates.
• Maintain process documentation, meeting artifacts, intake trackers, and evidence packages for audit, exam, and leadership requests.
• Partner with technical teams to translate operational needs into clear user stories, acceptance criteria, and implementation-ready requirements.
• Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, improve data quality, and reduce manual reporting effort across Security Operations.
• Coordinate across stakeholders to track dependencies, risks, decisions, and deliverables through completion.

 Qualifications 
• Experience as a business analyst, operations analyst, project analyst, or similar role in technology, cybersecurity, risk, or financial services.
• Strong written communication skills with the ability to summarize complex operational information for management audiences.
• Working knowledge of requirements documentation, process mapping, KPI / metrics reporting, and stakeholder coordination.
• Familiarity with cybersecurity operations, incident response, threat management, audit / regulatory requests, or control environments preferred.
• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 tools; experience with Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Power BI, Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar tools preferred.
• Highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple workstreams in a fast-paced operational environment.

 Work Authorization 

 Applicants must have the right to work in Ireland at the time of application and for the duration of employment.

 Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide employment permit sponsorship for this role. This includes Critical Skills Employment Permits, General Employment Permits, Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permits, Stamp 1G permissions, and other employment permits under Irish immigration frameworks.

 Working with Us 

 As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve. 

 Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities. 

 Reasonable Accommodation 

 Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com , or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.
