title: Abbott Ireland Operations Professional Development Programme (OPDP) - Ireland
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Abbott in Ireland 
 Abbott has maintained a strong presence in Ireland since 1946 and celebrates its 80th anniversary in the country in 2026. The company supports the Irish healthcare sector with a broad portfolio spanning diagnostics, diabetes care, medical devices and nutritional products. Today, Abbott employs more than 6,500 people across ten sites located in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford and Sligo.
 
 About Abbott 
 Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.
 
 We currently have a number of open positions on our OPDP Program in Ireland.
 
 Our Operations Professional Development Program (OPDP) is an entry-level, three-year rotation program designed to offer hands-on experience while promoting personal and professional growth. As a participant from Ireland, you will begin the program and first two rotations in Ireland, then you will complete your final-year rotation outside of Europe.    
 
 Upon completion, PDP participants graduate into their full-time position, continuing to grow their career and contributing as an Abbott professional using the foundation of skills, experience and network developed during their time in the program. 
 
 As an OPDP participant you will:   
 Be a regular full-time employee of Abbott and qualify for the same competitive salary and benefits as other Abbott employees.  
 Assume full responsibility and contribute as a functional operation professional. 
 Rotate through three challenging, demanding, and diverse 12-month assignments. 
 Develop a well-rounded skill set through assignments in the established learning tracks (see below) for the program. 
 Relocate to various sites around Ireland to experience assignment diversity and operations
 Work within multiple business units during your rotational program at Abbott. 
 Have the opportunity to explore possible crossover assignments within other Operation Programs (i.e. Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Operational Excellence). 
 Be paired with a mentor to assist in the development of your operations career. 
 Create a personalized growth plan to serve as a step-by-step guide towards the experiences, knowledge, and resources necessary to achieve your career goals 
 Obtain training customized to support your individual growth and development. 
 Report to the department manager in each assignment who will oversee your day-to-day responsibilities.  
 
 OPDP rotation overview:   
 The first two assignments are based in Ireland and involve working across functional areas such as: Technical, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, Project Management and Engineering
 The first rotation is known as a technical rotation, while the second rotation focuses on Leading a Team
 The third rotation is based outside of Europe and focuses heavily on Operational Excellence
 No assignment is repeated; each is with a different Assignment Manager 
 OPDP participants starting the program on 05 July 2027 will complete a three-year program with the final international (overseas) rotation ending in June 2030
 
   Requirements:   
 Bachelor’s Degree/MSc engineering  (Automation / Mechanical / Electrical / Automation) Biotechnology, Pharmacy, Food Science, Supply Chain (Business Studies with major/minor Supply Chain) or related disciplines (grade 2:1 or higher) 
 Tracking to or have a minimum of 2.1 Grade in your undergraduate course with a track record of outstanding co-curricular activities
 Interest in pursuing a career in Operations – Production, Engineering, Quality Assurance, etc. 
 Geographically mobile and willing to complete a one-year assignment outside of Europe
 Unrestricted authorization to work in Ireland
 Fluent level of English for written and verbal business communication.
 
 Key Skills 
 Ambition for Leadership
 Capacity to apply skills and knowledge to address operational challenges and add value to the business. 
 Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills. 
 Strong interpersonal, leadership & communication skills. 
 Eager to learn and has the flexibility and willingness to work on different projects. 
 Previous work experience in internship or co-op work experience would be an advantage 
 
 
 The closing date for applications is  Friday, 08 October 2026 . However, interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis from the launch of the program. We strongly encourage students to apply as early as possible to avoid missing out on these exciting opportunities.
 #earlycareers
 
      
 The base pay for this position is 
N/A In specific locations, the pay range may vary from the range posted. 
      
 JOB FAMILY: Engineering      
 DIVISION: CHR Corporate Human Resources         
 LOCATION: Ireland > Sligo : Carbury Point, Finisklin Industrial & Technology Park, Sligo      
 ADDITIONAL LOCATIONS: Ireland > Clonmel : Cashel Road, Ireland > Cootehill : Dromore West, Ireland > Donegal Town : R267, Ireland > Galway : Parkmore East Business Park, Ireland > Kilkenny : Kilkenny Business and Technology Park, Ireland > Longford : Lisnamuck, Ireland > Sligo : Finisklin Road      
 WORK SHIFT: Standard      
 TRAVEL: Yes, 50 % of the Time      
 MEDICAL SURVEILLANCE: Yes      
 SIGNIFICANT WORK ACTIVITIES: Not Applicable

title: WorldLink Network Operations Analyst
description:
Excited to grow your career? 
 We value our talented employees, and whenever possible strive to help one of our associates grow professionally before recruiting new talent to our open positions. If you think the open position, you see is right for you, we encourage you to apply!
 Our people make all the difference in our success.
 ------------------------------------------------------
 Business Overview: 
 WorldLink is Citi’s primary cross-currency payments capability, enabling clients to efficiently and seamlessly make payments from their primary functional currency account(s) to beneficiaries in over 135 currencies. WorldLink facilitates cross-border payments and is coupled with an embedded FX capability.
 Leveraging Citi’s in-country expertise, Worldlink Payment Services, helps the client to improve operational efficiency and offering a choice of payment methods, such as Funds Transfers, ACH, Cheques, Instant Payments, Wallets & Card payments.
 WorldLink addresses key client challenges and objectives including navigating local country regulations and payment requirements, efficiently managing beneficiaries, managing FX exposure, increasing efficiency, automated processes and achieving centralization and control.
 Role Overview: 
 The Network Operations team is responsible for the management of WorldLink’s global partners. Network Operations are key point of contact for Product, Service and Operations staff across the globe for questions related to the Cross Border Payments Solutions and our network.
 This successful candidate will be required to work independently, with internal teams and external partners across multiple cross functional families by driving results and process improvements/efficiencies, whilst having the ability to be completely adaptable to changing business requirements and deliverables is essential.
 
 What you’ll do: 
 
 Leadership & People Management: 
 Demonstrated experience in coaching, mentoring, and identifying skill gaps within a team
 Drive a high-performance culture through regular feedback, training, and manage career development plans
 Manage workload allocation, prioritization, and succession planning
 
 Query Management & Oversight: 
 Exhibits strong knowledge and expertise in the products, payment offerings and capabilities
 Manage, review and respond to queries, timely escalation of key issues to the senior manager, manage client expectations by providing updates & timelines for resolution/completion
 Considered an SME across the Business with regards to Products supported - is considered the person who can answer most questions and will support teams to provide solutions to their problems
 
 Stakeholder Management: 
 Develops strong relationships within management across the Business along with all stakeholders at Citi
 Responsible for escalation management including presenting cohesive client satisfaction updates to senior management
 Comfortable investigating root-cause of any issues, client dis-satisfaction etc and escalating to the senior management
 Engage proactively with internal stakeholders (e.g., product teams, technical support, sales) to address operational challenges and improve service delivery
 Support business initiatives including product/currency expansion; confirming capacity for new business and defining processing capabilities
 
 Risk & Control: 
 Appropriately assess risk when decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets
 Driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behaviour, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency
 Continuously Identify process improvement opportunities and communicating to management for consideration
 
 What we’ll need from you: 
 Experience in payments, FX or other related functions in the financial services industry
 Track record leading projects
 Strong analytical skills to evaluate complex issues, activities and processes
 Excellent communication skills: ability to engage and inspire across stakeholder groups
 Exceptional command in Microsoft Office suite, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word
 
 Education: 
 Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, or a related field
 
 What we can offer you: 
 
 By joining Citi Dublin, you will not only be part of a business casual workplace with a hybrid working model (up to 2 days working at home per week), but also receive a competitive base salary (which is annually reviewed) and enjoy a whole host of additional benefits that support you (and your family) to be well, live well and save well. Discover more here. 
 
 Alongside these benefits Citi is committed to ensuring our workplace is where everyone feels comfortable coming to work as their whole self every day.  We want the best talent around the world to be energised to join us, motivated to stay, and empowered to thrive. 
 
 Sounds like Citi has everything you need? Then apply to discover the true extent of your capabilities.

As an Internal Audit Graduate, you'll gain exposure to a diverse range of business areas and work with colleagues across the organisation, helping to ensure AIB continues to operate in a safe, effective and sustainable way.
At AIB, we know that starting your career is a big step. That's why we've created a graduate programme that gives you meaningful work, plenty of support and opportunities to develop both professionally and personally.
Over 3.5 years, you'll build valuable experience, complete professional qualifications and develop the confidence, technical expertise and commercial awareness needed for a successful career.
No two days will be the same!
Why join our graduate programme?
Internal Audit offers a unique opportunity to see how AIB manages risk, strengthens controls and supports effective governance across the organisation.
You'll gain insight into a wide range of business functions while working alongside experienced professionals who are invested in helping you succeed.
Along the way, you'll also have opportunities to:
Pursue globally recognised professional qualifications such as ACCA and Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), with financial support, study leave and mentoring
Build your professional network
Attend development events
Connect with senior leaders across the organisation
Learn from graduates who have already completed the programme
Explore different career paths within AIB
This is more than a graduate programme. It's an opportunity to gain a professional qualification, develop highly transferable skills and build a strong foundation for a successful career.
What You’ll Do
Group Internal Audit provides independent assurance to the Board and senior management on the effectiveness of governance, risk management and internal controls across AIB.
As the third line of defence, Internal Audit plays a critical role in helping the organisation operate effectively and deliver positive outcomes for customers, colleagues and stakeholders.
By helping identify opportunities for improvement, strengthening controls and supporting effective risk management, you'll contribute to the long-term resilience and success of AIB.
One of the greatest benefits of Internal Audit is the breadth of exposure available throughout the programme.
You may gain insight into:
Retail Banking
Capital Markets
Wealth
Technology
Risk
Finance
Operations
Corporate Functions
Sustainability and Strategic Transformation initiatives
Few graduate programmes offer such a comprehensive view of how a bank operates.
What's in it for you?
Our 3.5-year training contract is designed to provide extensive practical experience while supporting you through your professional qualification journey and helping you develop deep expertise across multiple business areas.
Alongside valuable experience and development opportunities, you'll enjoy:
21 Days annual leave & 2 additional volunteer days
Additional AIB Bank Holidays – Good Friday & the day after St. Stephens Day
Hybrid working, 3 days in office & 2 working from home
Rotations across different teams
Dedicated graduate development programme
Professional qualifications supported by AIB
Access to senior leaders and mentoring
Internal networking events
Real project ownership from day one
Strong emphasis on wellbeing & work-life balance
Structured learning & development programme
Defined Contribution Pension Scheme
Vhi Healthcare scheme
Variable remuneration scheme
We are with you every step of the way
Starting your first professional role can feel daunting, but we'll support you every step of the way.
Every graduate is assigned a dedicated People Leader who will support your development, help you navigate challenges and encourage you to get the most from your experience.
You'll also become part of a vibrant graduate community, joining fellow Internal Audit graduates as well as graduates from previous intakes. Whether through learning, networking or social events, you'll build relationships that last well beyond the programme.
We also offer access to a wide range of support networks and initiatives, including our Employee Assistance Programme and Mentor Her programme.
Entry Requirements:
Achieved or expected to achieve a minimum 2.1 Honours Degree (or equivalent for universities outside of Ireland) is a prerequisite for those joining the AIB graduate programme.
Candidates must be fully authorised to work in Ireland or hold a valid work permit for the full duration of the 3.5 year contract (September 2027 – March 2031)
If you are not sure about your suitability based on any aspects of the role advertised, we encourage you to please contact our Future Talent Programmes team at Grads@aib.ie for a conversation.
AIB is an equal opportunities employer, and we pride ourselves on being the first bank in Ireland to receive the Investors in Diversity Gold Standard accreditation from the Irish Centre for Diversity. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees. Should you have a reasonable accommodation request please email the Talent Acquisition team at  Grads@aib.ie
Apply today and start shaping your future with AIB.
Applications are expected to close on the 26 th October 2026 however, we encourage candidates to apply early as the programme may close sooner if demand is high.
Eligibility and Equal Opportunities
Applicants must be resident in the Republic of Ireland and be fully authorised to work, or hold a valid work permit, for the full duration of the programme. Any offer of employment will be conditional upon satisfactory evidence of the right to work in the Republic of Ireland.
AIB is an equal opportunities employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates and are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process.

title: 2027 Summer Intern - Funds & Operations Analyst, EMEA
description:
PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns.
 
 Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking.  We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients.
 
 
 Internship positions are located in Dublin, Ireland 
 
 You’re eligible to apply if you: 
 Are an undergraduate currently pursuing a degree with an expected graduation date of December 2027 – June 2028

 Have a minimum 2:1 from an accredited university

 Are business proficient in English

 
 You’ll excel as a Client Operations Analyst if you: 
 Can collaborate and contribute to operations-related projects that enhance communications, optimize and automate reports, and create operational efficiency

 Are entrepreneurial, proactive about problem-solving, and enjoy working with data and technology

 Exhibit the following skills sets: being process minded, organized, client driven, and detail oriented while utilizing strong presentation skills

 Have a strong interest in operations and the financial markets, macroeconomics, and investment finance

 Are able to articulate ideas and strategies clearly, both verbally and in writing

 Demonstrate a commitment to quality and attention to detail, ensuring that work is delivered completely, accurately and on time

 Are personable, with the ability to develop client relationships into strategic partnerships

 Are ethical, collaborative, organized, flexible, high energy, self-starter, accountable, humble

 Are great at using Excel, along with having some programming skills (recommended SQL and/or Python) 

 Have undertaken finance/capital markets coursework (recommended)

 Have demonstrated curiosity and experience in using new emerging technologies and AI tools in your work or school projects to solve problems and drive better outcomes   

 
 See yourself as a Client Operations Analyst: 

You’ll serve as a central operational liaison that focuses on the reporting process and inquiries to help create a better client experience utilizing modern tools and technology.
 You’ll work cross-functionally to understand client needs, translate them into meaningful plans, and execute accordingly to mitigate risk and build efficiency.
 
 The PIMCO Internship Experience: 
 The PIMCO Internship is a 10-week program that runs from early June to mid-August, with the expectation that you will be available for the full duration of the program  

 During Week 1, you’ll participate in PIMCO Fundamentals Training, providing you with the skills, knowledge, and relationships that will prepare you for success

 Alongside your colleagues, participate in PIMCO's Global Month of Volunteering , developed to heighten the impact of our employees' worldwide volunteer efforts

 Join us for a variety of cross-divisional education, networking & social events!

 Your supervisor, peer mentor, senior leaders and team offer guidance and mentorship throughout the summer

 You will gain hands-on experience with AI-powered tools from day one, with training and resources that help build future ready skills and make an impact from the start

 You’ll receive feedback at mid- and end-of-summer as part of a formal review process to keep you on the path to meeting your summer goals

 As a PIMCO intern, you’ll receive competitive compensation, along with a transition bonus to help with relocation to one of our office locations

 
 Want to learn more? Hear about The PIMCO Internship Experience from past interns & search for live virtual recruiting events !
 
 How you should apply: 
 
 We review applications on a rolling basis and encourage you to apply by submitting your resume as soon as you are ready. 
 
 What to expect during the interview process: 
 After we receive your application, we'll conduct an initial resume & cover letter review. We'll send status updates throughout the process.

 If you are selected to move forward, you will be invited to complete a one-way video interview and assessment, giving you the opportunity to showcase your interests, skills, and personality as part of the next stage of the process.

 Once you complete the assessment, you will have a final round of live interviews with us via video conference. These interviews typically include both behavioral and technical questions.

 
 Applications for the internship program are reviewed in phases. Candidates are strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible to be considered in the initial review. Later applications received may still be considered; however, due to the high volume of interest, we cannot guarantee that all applications will be reviewed.

PIMCO is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive, cognitively diverse environment.
 
 For more information on PIMCO and Career Opportunities, please visit https://www.pimco.com/us/en/about-us/careers/students/internships 
 
 
 

 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Statement 
 PIMCO recruits and hires qualified candidates without regard to race, national origin, ancestry, religion (including religious dress and grooming practices), sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender (including gender identity and expression), age, military or veteran status, disability (physical or mental), any factor prohibited by law, and as such affirms in policy and practice to support and promote the concept of equal employment opportunity and affirmative action, in accordance with all applicable federal, state, provincial and municipal laws. The company also prohibits discrimination on other basis such as medical condition, or marital status under applicable laws. 
 
 Applicants with Disabilities 
 PIMCO is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. We provide reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities, including veterans, in job application procedures. If you have any difficulty using our online system due to a disability and you would like to request an accommodation, you may contact us at 949-720-7744 and leave a message. This is a dedicated line designed exclusively to assist job seekers with disabilities to apply online. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

title: Deal Onboarding Analyst - Global Corporate Trust
description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions, enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed in the right ways, all more confidently and more often—that’s what we call the courage to thrive.   We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.
  
 As a wholly owned subsidiary of U.S. Bank, Elavon is committed to building the platforms and ecosystems that help over 1.5 million customers around the world to achieve their financial goals—no matter what they need. From transaction processing to customer service, to driving innovation and launching new products, we’re building a range of tailored payment solutions powered by the latest technology. As part of our team, you can explore what motivates and energizes your career goals: partnering with our customers, our communities, and each other.
  
 We actively uphold transparent and fair hiring practices that support individual opportunity, inclusive culture, and career mobility across all levels of our organisation.
 
 We offer meaningful opportunities for growth, a culture of inclusion, and a strong commitment to transparency and integrity in everything we do.
 
 
 
 Job Description Deal Onboarding Analyst - Global Corporate Trust 

 The Deal Onboarding Management (DOM) team sits within the Data Management & Control Group and are responsible for a variety of tasks including but not exclusive to the setup of deals across a variety of systems and platforms, providing client access to statements, deal audit follow up’s and raising of quarterly fees for multiple products. This team works closely with internal/external teams gathering information to support the deal setup. The team sets up deals as per the target operating model and is responsible for flagging issues. DOM will be involved from the deal incept, supporting testing across the various platforms, gathering of tax documentation and billing, to name a few of the further tasks.
  
 Essential Functions: 
 Structured Finance Deal Account Set Up - Ensuring that accounts are accurately set up following the target operating model for account set up in a timely fashion. Escalating any issues arising from this to Relationship Management in a time sensitive manner.
 Deal Onboarding – Set up of deals across various systems, gathering of tax documentation, fee and extracting data from various sources.  
 Queries & Escalations – Acting as escalation contact for business line queries and requests between the business line and client correspondents.
 Participate in Bank projects and UAT testing as required.
 Escalating of issues in a timely manner to management
 Change Management – continuous looking for improvements, efficiencies and enhanced controls in DMC processes.
 Ability to work on own initiative to 100% accuracy. 
 Understanding of regulations and risks attached to the role and when to escalate to avoid potential issues.
  
 Desired Experience & Qualities: 
 Experience of data set up within a banking / financial services environment.
 Effective interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills
 Understanding of the importance of timely and correct escalation
 Ability to create, implement and adhere to controls
 Working knowledge of Corporate Trust and its products
 Attention to detail and an inquisitive nature
 Takes ownership and works to tight deadlines without compromising on quality
 Flexible and adaptable
  
 Preferred Skills/Experience: 
 Bachelor's degree in finance, or equivalent work experience
 Three to five years of experience in trust and securities operational functions
 Good knowledge of trust and securities operational functions, systems, procedures, products and services
 Good knowledge and understanding of legal, regulatory and accounting principles which directly affect Wealth Management & Securities Services business lines and clients
 
 Location expectations  
 This role requires working from a U.S. Bank location three (3) or more days per week.
  
 
 Accessibility 
 We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment experience. If you need adjustments at any stage of the application or hiring process, please contact your recruiter for guidance and support. 
 
 Total Rewards 
 U.S. Bank is committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation practices in line with local regulatory and legal requirements. Our total rewards approach is designed to attract, retain, and support top talent while ensuring equal pay for work of equal value.
  
 We offer a market-competitive compensation package that includes:
 Clearly defined salary ranges aligned with industry benchmarks and internal equity standards.

 Performance-based incentives for eligible employees (as defined by relevant plan rules), awarded through transparent, objective criteria that recognize both individual and company performance.

 Inclusive equitable benefits that are accessible to all employees and focused around our 3 main pillars of financial wellbeing, health & wellness).

 Continuous development opportunities including training, education support, and career progression pathways based on inclusive and transparent criteria.

 Employee recognition programs that celebrate achievements and milestones for all.

  
 We regularly review our compensation and benefits to ensure they remain competitive, inclusive, and responsive to employee needs and market trends. Further details of the compensation package will be provided upon application.
 
 We encourage candidates to explore the full value of our offer, including monetary and non-monetary benefits, at Employee benefits and development | U.S. Bank | Elavon .
   
 Closing Date 
 Posting may be closed earlier due to high volume of applicants.
  
 We aim to provide timely updates throughout the process and encourage early applications to ensure consideration.

Diversity - Innovation - Caring - Global Collaboration - Winning Spirit - High Performance
At Boston Scientific, we’ll give you the opportunity to harness all that’s within you by working in teams of diverse and high-performing employees, tackling some of the most important health industry challenges. With access to the latest tools, information and training, we’ll help you in advancing your skills and career. Here, you’ll be supported in progressing – whatever your ambitions.
Advancing possibilities for a brighter tomorrow
Boston Scientific is seeking a highly motivated Graduate Knowledge Operations Analyst   on a defined-term (23months) basis to join our Clonmel team .
Job Purpose:
Start your career where your ideas, curiosity and technical skills can make a meaningful difference. As a Graduate Engineer at Boston Scientific, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues, contribute to innovative medical technologies and build hands-on experience in a collaborative environment.
Create a knowledge library using a Power application by structuring, tagging and connecting information, including documentation, procedures, process maps and business change impacts, to a specific business hierarchy.
This is an opportunity to apply what you learned during your studies, develop your technical and problem-solving capabilities and gain valuable experience while contributing to technologies designed to improve patients' lives.
Key Responsibilities:
Knowledge Management
Work with business partners to identify and locate knowledge items for the library.
Organize information, including features, process maps and training materials.
Establish relationships between connected knowledge items and the business hierarchy.
Maintain repository governance standards.
Metadata and Taxonomy Management
Apply classification and tagging standards.
Improve document discoverability through numbering, labeling or AI tools.
Ensure consistent naming conventions.
Support knowledge governance processes.
AI Enablement
Identify content quality issues.
Support AI search optimization.
Validate knowledge retrieval outputs.
Recommend repository improvements.
Education & Experience:
Hons Bachelor Degree (Level 8) in engineering or science is essential.
Graduated within the past two years or currently in the final year of university.
Relevant work experience or completion of a co-op program, ideally within or knowledge of information systems/business administration.
Eligibility to work in Ireland.
Strong communication and teamwork skills, with the initiative to contribute in a collaborative environment.
Strong systems aptitude and an interest in developing technical skills.
Enthusiastic, proactive approach to learning and problem-solving.
Interest in medical technology, manufacturing, product development or continuous improvement.
Strong knowledge management, library science and data analytics skills.
What we can offer you
Competitive Benefits – we offer market leading benefits including performance-related bonus, pension contribution, onsite gym, onsite parking, subsidised canteen, organised social groups and healthcare.
A Career with Meaningful Purpose   – opportunity to transform the lives of patients worldwide.
Our Culture   - our work is guided by core values that define our culture and empower our employees.
Career Development   – our highly engaged leaders will empower you to grow and will invest in your potential. You can also broaden your skills through personal development courses.
Opportunity to Innovate   – we encourage you to fulfil your true creative potential by speaking up with your ideas and solutions to problems that matter.
Work-Life Balance   – we have created a culture that acknowledges, respects and supports your life and work choices.
Corporate Social Responsibility   – we are dedicated to progressing business practices in areas important to our communities. Our onsite charity events have raised over €1.5 million for worthy causes in the past ten years.

title: Group HR Administrator
description:
Group HR Administrator
About the role
Reporting directly to the Senior Group HR Generalist, Monument Re is looking to hire a Group HR Administrator. This position will play a vital role in supporting our Group HR function to deliver our priorities and plans across the jurisdictions in which we operate. This position will require the successful candidate to support payroll and HR processes with a strong focus on reporting and analysis to help drive valuable business insights. This role offers an excellent opportunity for growth and development within the wider HR function. This role will be based in Dublin and is an 11-month Fixed Term Contract.
Responsibilities
Coordinate and prepare monthly payroll data for Ireland, the UK and Bermuda, liaising with payroll providers and internal stakeholders to support accurate and timely payroll processing.
Administer a range of payroll-related activities, including pension administration, benefit deductions, salary changes, and employee payroll queries.
Maintain and update employee records on our HR system, ensuring data accuracy
Supporting the preparation of monthly and quarterly HR KPI reports.
Monitor and respond to queries received through the HR Operations inbox, escalating issues where required and ensuring timely follow-up.
Provide administrative support to the Group HR Team, including drafting letters, preparing documentation, references and responding to ad hoc requests.
Support the delivery of an effective onboarding process for new joiners, coordinating documentation, inductions, and employee communications.
Coordinate learning and development activities, including training administration, scheduling, logistics management, and communication with participants.

Ready to start your career at AIB?
If you're curious, ambitious and looking for a role where you can learn, grow and make a real impact from day one, our Legal & Corporate Affairs Graduate Programme could be the perfect fit.
At AIB, we know that starting your career is a big step. That's why we've created a graduate programme that gives you meaningful work, plenty of support and opportunities to develop both professionally and personally.
Over 23 months, you'll rotate across different teams, gain exposure to exciting projects and develop the skills, experience and confidence needed to build a successful career.
No two days will be the same!
Why join our graduate programme?
As part of the programme, you'll get the opportunity to experience different areas across Legal & Corporate Affairs, working with a range of teams and colleagues.
You'll learn on the job, contribute to real business initiatives and work alongside experienced professionals who are invested in helping you succeed.
Along the way, you'll also have opportunities to:
Build your professional network
Attend development events
Connect with senior leaders across the organisation
Learn from graduates who have already completed the programme
Explore different career paths within AIB
This is more than just a graduate role. It's an opportunity to discover what you're capable of.
What You’ll Do
Legal:
The Legal Function has responsibility and accountability for the provision of all legal services within the AIB Group. The objective of the Legal Function is to work collaboratively with the business and support units that we provide services to, and to ensure that our advice is pragmatic, commercial and customer focused. The Legal Function also plays a key role in controlling external legal spend to maximise value and avoid unnecessary external instructions. In addition, the Function has responsibility for Third Party Management and Supplier Relationship.
Corporate Affairs:
Sitting within the Corporate Affairs Function, the Corporate Governance and Company Secretarial teams   ensure a simple, efficient and compliant corporate governance structure is in place to support the AIB Group Board and Executive. The teams help the business, and our leaders achieve AIB's strategic objectives by advising on all aspects of corporate governance, acting as communicator, facilitator and advisor to the Chairman, the Group Board, the Boards of the main subsidiaries and the Executive Leadership Team, to enable effective engagement with shareholders and other relevant stakeholders.
What's in it for you?
Alongside valuable experience and development opportunities, you'll enjoy:
21 Days annual leave & 2 additional volunteer days
Additional AIB Bank Holidays – Good Friday & the day after St. Stephens Day
Hybrid working (depending on placement within relevant functions),
Rotations across different teams
Strong emphasis on wellbeing & work-life balance
Structured learning & development programme
Defined Contribution Pension Scheme
Vhi Healthcare scheme
Variable remuneration scheme
We are with you every step of the way
Starting your first professional role can feel daunting, but we'll be with you every step of the way.
Every graduate is assigned a dedicated People Leader who will support your development, help you navigate challenges and encourage you to get the most from your experience.
You'll also become part of a vibrant graduate community, joining fellow Enterprise Delivery graduates as well as graduates from previous intakes. Whether it's learning, networking or social events, you'll quickly build relationships that last well beyond the programme.
We also offer access to a wide range of support networks and initiatives, including our Employee Assistance Programme and Mentor Her programme.
Please click  here  for further information about AIB’s PACT – Our Commitment to You.

title: 2026 Graduate Programme - Fund Accounting 1
description:
ABOUT US: 
  
 As a world leading provider of integrated solutions for the alternative investment industry, Alter Domus (meaning “The Other House” in Latin) is proud to be home to 90% of the top 30 asset managers in the private markets, and more than 7,000 professionals across 24 jurisdictions.  
 With a deep understanding of what it takes to succeed in alternatives, we believe in being different - in what we do, in how we work and most importantly in how we enable and develop our people. Invest yourself in the alternative, and join an organization where you progress on merit, where you can speak openly with whoever you are speaking to, and where you will be supported along whichever path you choose to take.  
 Find out more about life at Alter Domus at careers.alterdomus.com   
  
 ABOUT THE PROGRAMME 
  
 The aim of Alter Domus’ Graduate Programme is to create a graduate experience that develops individuals’ professional and technical skills, fosters engagement and understanding with the wider business and provides an opportunity for accelerated career growth with Alter Domus.  
 Our Graduate Programme commences in September each year - unless you would like to start earlier. A key part of our Graduate Programme is the facilitation of 12 month rotations across the key areas of our business, namely Private Debt, Private Equity, Real Estate and Fund of Funds. 
  
 WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING: 
  
 Taking care of the day-to-day operations of the funds and following up with third parties, including investors and fund managers. 
 Undergoing an interactive onboarding & training program designed to quickly and effectively give new joiners the industry skills and contexts needed. 
 You will take part in the setup of funds, and implementing complex international real estate structures as part of restructuring plans, mergers and acquisitions. 
 Preparing the funds’ periodic Net Asset Value calculation and year-end financial statements, management of the audit, and reviewing other fund related reports. 
 Reviewing tax returns and tax balances and maintaining relevant contacts with the tax authorities. 
 Taking an active part in the initial setup of any new funds take-on and liaising with independent tax specialists, lawyers, and notaries as part of the set up process. 
  
 WHAT YOU WILL LEARN: 
  
 Expertise per sub-asset class: All teams specialise in a given asset class (Private Equity, Real Estate, Debt, Fund Of Funds) 
 End-to-end processing by an integrated team of generalists with full knowledge and control over the full process rather than functionalization of the teams. 
 Expert Pools support the delivery teams on specific topics: Consolidation, Liquidations, Tax Compliance, Transfer Pricing, Investor Customer Due Diligence (CDD). 
  
 YOUR PROFILE: 
  
 You should be working towards a 2.1 degree (or above) in areas such as Finance, Accounting, Business or Economics 
 You are interested in accounting for investment products, particularly funds in the Real Estate, Private Equity or Private Debt industries, a relevant internship an advantage 
 You are interested in pursuing further professional development through the ACCA pathway 
 You enjoy communicating and collaborating within a team to help solved problems and generate results and you are reliable and organized. 
 WHAT WE OFFER 
  
 We are committed to supporting your development, advancing your career, and providing benefits that matter to you.  
 Our industry-leading Alter Domus Academy offers six learning zones for every stage of your career, with resources tailored to your ambitions and resources from LinkedIn Learning.  
  
 Grad benefits also include: 
  
 Support for ACCA accreditation including study leave  
 Flexible arrangements, generous holidays, plus an additional day off for your birthday and graduation! 
 Continuous mentoring along your career progression  
 Active sports, events and social committees across our offices  
 24/7 support available from our Employee Assistance Program  
 The opportunity to invest in our growth and success through our Employee Share Plan  
 Health Insurance 
 Pension Scheme 
  
 Equity in every sense of the word: 
  
 We are in the business of equity, in every sense of the word. For us, this means taking action to ensure every colleague has equal opportunity, valuing every voice and experience across our organisation, maintaining an inclusive culture where you can bring your whole self to work, and making Alter Domus a workplace where everyone feels they belong.  
  
 We celebrate our differences, and understand that our success relies on diverse perspectives and experiences, working towards shared goals and a common purpose. We take pride in creating a workplace where all our people are empowered to be truly invested in the alternative and bring their whole selves to work. 
  
 We are committed to ensuring a welcoming recruiting and onboarding process for everyone. Please contact our hiring team if you require any accommodations to make our recruitment process more accessible for you.  
  
 (Alter Domus Privacy notice can be reviewed via Alter Domus webpage: https://alterdomus.com/privacy-notice/ )

 #LI-NW1

title: Kepak Health and Safety Graduate Programme 2027 - Ireland
description:
Kepak Health & Safety Graduate Programme 2027 
 We are seeking to recruit for the 2027 Health and Safety Graduate Programme in our Kepak Cork site in Watergrasshill, Co. Cork
 
 Start date: 6th September 2027 
 Salary: €33,500 Year 1 and a potential increase of €1,500 at the start of Year 2 
 Duration: 2 Years 
 Check out our Graduate Hub on : https://www.kepak.com/careers/graduates/ 
 The Programme: 
 Our Health & Safety (H&S) Graduate programme is to help us to develop our H&S leaders of the future, and allows dynamic, motivated, hardworking, and passionate Graduates an opportunity to start their career with one of Ireland & UKs leading meat businesses. 
 You can expect: 
 To be fully immersed into our Culture from day 1, working alongside key industry experts and Kepak leaders
 Gain an in depth understanding of our brands and products, and our relationships with customers and consumers, and how they underpin our financial performance
 To learn key aspects of our business, whilst you develop your skills and knowledge
 The opportunity to develop personally and professionally through exposure to key projects, tasks and development activities that challenge you, all supported by a detailed learner journey and training plan
 A dedicated mentor and development program to support you both on the programme and into a role that best fits your skills
 Kepak is one of Europe’s leading food companies operating 12 manufacturing sites across 
 Ireland and the UK with sales offices in Europe, US and Asia. The group has a turnover of €1.5bn and employs over 4,500 people. Our company purpose “ Meat at our heart, innovation our driver and nutrition our future ” is underpinned by our values of “ Responsibility, Ambition, Passion for Food and Teamwork” . 
 
 ROLE LOCATION: 
 Kepak, Watergrasshill, Co. Cork
 Full time, On-site position 
 
 ROLE PURPOSE: 
 Reporting to the Site health and Safety Manager, the H&S Graduate will be responsible for the development and implementation of Health and Safety management systems within the Site and for ensuring that advice and support is available for all business Unit Managers in order for them to fulfil their own responsibilities.
 Liaising closely with Group H&S support services to ensure site management system is aligned with Group safety strategy.
 
 ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Policies and Procedures 
 Ongoing development and implementation of improved Health and Safety practices, policies and procedures on the site.    
 Enforce the effective operation of Safety and Health practices and policies in conjunction Business Unit Managers 
 Develop and budget with the Site Manager and Health and Safety Manager effective Training policies for implementation on the site. 
 
 Safety Personnel 
 Facilitate, support and advise the Site Risk Management teams. Chair the Site Safety meetings to update all business unit managers on developments at site level.
 Ensure all personnel are fully safety trained and competent for the role.
 
 Risk Assessment 
 Assist business unit Managers undertake Risk Assessments for all operations on site.
 Review Risk Assessments on a regular basis.
 Implement Internal Audit processes at site level and measure performance and action planning.
 
 Review and Assist 
 A written safety report will be presented each month to the site manager for discussion with the Site H&S team identifying areas of risk, concern and recommendations for implementation on site.
 
 Audits 
 Undertake regular unscheduled Safety audits on the site to ensure compliance with Group policy.
 Enforce policy by identifying breaches and reporting to the Site Manager and the Group Health and Safety Manager
 
 Liaison 
 Liaise with HSA and other outside agencies in relation to H&S matters including reporting, auditing and ensuring recommendations and guidelines are fully complied with.
 
 ROLE DELIVERABLES: 
 Meeting Reporting Deadlines %.
 KPI’s will be set out and reviewed by the Site Manager for each period defined (month / quarter / year) reflecting achievement of agreed objectives and initiatives.
 Requirements 
 Who are we looking for? 
 We are looking for hardworking and ambitious Graduates, who want to learn and grow in a challenging and fast paced environment, by performing real roles as part of your rotations. 
 You must be mobile and willing to travel throughout the programme to undertake development activities at any of our sites in the UK and Ireland.
 We will be looking for alignment with our Core Values:
 Responsibility – Ability to work on your own initiative and take accountability for your actions
 Ambition – You will have the willingness and confidence to challenge yourself to be the best you can be and be driven to succeed
 Passion for Food – this is at the heart of everything we do, you must be passionate about every aspect of our industry
 Teamwork – ability to build positive relationships quickly with people from all cultures and career stages is pivotal
 Strong communicator with well-developed interpersonal skills.
 Organized, energetic and self-motivated.
 Demonstrate the ability to work on your own initiative without immediate hands on support.
 Ability to identify continuous improvement initiatives and ability to challenge status quo.
 Strong IT sills and familiarity with Microsoft Office, Excel, Power Point and other common software tools.
 A high level of analytical, methodology and time management skills required.
 A high level of attention to detail and accuracy.
 Benefits 
 Employee Discount Scheme
 Service-Related Annual Leave
 Discounted Health Insurance
 Educational Assistance/ L&D
 Cycle to work scheme
 Employee assistance programme

title: Fab Supply Planning Analyst
description:
Job Details: 
 
 Job Description:  Role Overview 
 Intel Foundry is seeking a Planning Analyst, Fab Supply Planning to support planning operations for the Ireland manufacturing site. This role plays a critical part in enabling successful technology ramps, production readiness, and sustained high-volume manufacturing by integrating engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain requirements into executable supply plans.
 The successful candidate will leverage advanced analytics, business insight, and cross-functional collaboration to influence supply decisions, identify optimization opportunities, and drive alignment across Engineering, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain organizations. This individual must be a strong communicator, critical thinker, and problem solver who can translate complex data into actionable recommendations that improve factory performance, supply readiness, and customer outcomes.

 Key Responsibilities 

 • Production & Supply Planning: Develop and maintain production, supply, inventory, and capacity plans that support technology ramps, production readiness, customer commitments, and high-volume manufacturing objectives.
 • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain teams to ensure new process requirements, factory changes, and operational needs are effectively integrated into production plans and execution strategies.
 • Technology Ramp Support: Support the transition of new technologies and manufacturing capabilities into sustained high-volume production while balancing customer commitments, factory performance, and operational readiness.
 • Data Analysis & Optimization: Analyze demand, supply, inventory, capacity, cycle time, and factory performance data to identify risks, opportunities, and optimization strategies.
 • Supply Decision Support: Influence supply, capacity, and inventory decisions through data-driven analysis, scenario modeling, and actionable recommendations.
 • Risk Management: Identify supply risks, production constraints, engineering dependencies, and operational gaps while driving mitigation plans and resolution efforts.
 • Capacity Planning: Support capacity planning, bottleneck management, and supply optimization activities to maximize factory output and business performance.
 • Reporting & Insights: Develop reporting, dashboards, and business insights that improve visibility, planning accuracy, and decision quality.
 • Executive Communication: Translate complex operational data into concise, executive-ready recommendations and communications.
 • Problem Solving & Alignment: Lead cross-functional problem-solving efforts and drive alignment across organizations to ensure successful production ramps and manufacturing readiness.
 • Continuous Improvement: Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance planning processes, supply optimization, operational performance, and manufacturing execution.

 
 
 Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications 

 • Education: Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Engineering, Business, Data Analytics, or a related field.
 • Relevant Experience: Experience gained through internships, co-ops, academic projects, military service, or professional experience in supply chain, manufacturing, engineering, operations, analytics, or a related discipline.
 • Analytical Skills: Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving capabilities.
 • Technical Skills: Experience using analytical tools such as Excel, Power BI, SQL, Python, Tableau, or similar technologies.
 • Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence stakeholders through data-driven recommendations.

 Preferred Qualifications 

 • Planning Experience: Experience in supply planning, factory planning, manufacturing operations, engineering operations, or supply chain analytics.
 • Operational Knowledge: Understanding of capacity planning, inventory management, forecasting, production planning, and manufacturing operations.
 • Manufacturing Experience: Experience supporting technology ramps, manufacturing readiness, or high-volume manufacturing environments.
 • Industry Experience: Experience working within semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or technology industries.
 • Business Intelligence: Experience developing dashboards, business analytics, and executive-level presentations.
 • Stakeholder Management: Demonstrated ability to influence decisions and drive results in a cross-functional environment.
 • Systems Knowledge: Familiarity with ERP systems, planning platforms, and data visualization tools.
 
           
 
 
 Job Type: Experienced Hire 
 
 Shift: Shift 1 (Ireland) 
 
 Primary Location:  Ireland, Leixlip 
 
 Additional Locations: 
 
 
 
 Posting Statement: All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, religious creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military and veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender, gender expression, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by local law, regulation, or ordinance. Position of Trust N/A

title: Consultant, Fund Accounting
description:
About Northern Trust 

 As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. 

 Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. 

 With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. 

 Role 
 We are currently recruiting for a consultant within our growing Fund Accounting department. The consultant has responsibility for accurately reviewing and sign off on NAV calculations.  They are the subject matter expert on the team for all fund specific requirements. The consultant also leads the team in rolling out new system enhancements and procedures and collates and provides feedback from the fund accounting department to the relevant stakeholders. They may be an individual contributor or have one or two direct reports. This role will be attractive to candidates with prior fund accounting experience or relevant operational /accounting experience who want to progress their career in a ‘best in class’ environment 

 Principal Responsibilities 
 Responsible for co-coordinating systems testing in the team. 
 Mentors individuals and peers during projects and assignments. 
 Analytically and procedurally competent to represent the team on cross-function process or project deliverables. 
 Responsible for the rollout of new procedures within the team in consultation with BPA/Team leaders/NAV Managers. 
 Ability to provide input into long term strategy for department 
 Experience of representing businesses to current clients via presentations etc. 
 Instils a client service culture among staff and ensures that all clients receive a quality service. 
 Experience of designing and implementing development plans, training plans and succession plans for all levels of staff. 
 Identify tasks to be completed by the project team and ensure that they are completed in a timely and efficient manner.  
 Identify and delegate projects/assignments and tasks to individuals and peers. Maintain accountability for the projects/assignments. Provide progression feedback and recognition to the individuals and the project team. 
 
 Skills /Experience 
 Previous fund accounting experience or relevant operational experience preferred 
 Detailed Knowledge of Enterprise and related Fund Accounting applications preferred 
 Maintain an understanding of the industry and NT, in particular NT’s systems, infrastructure and process/data flows. 
 Experience with vendors an advantage (Bloomberg, Reuters etc) 
 Strong communication, first class presentation and internal and external client-servicing skills. 
 Evidence of successful negotiation skills 
 Understanding of how Fund Accounting systems link and interface with other systems and an appreciation of how to implement such interfaces. 
 Client service orientation 
 Good attention to detail 
 Demonstrates willingness to help others outside team 
 Good prioritisation and multi-tasking skills 
 Strong problem solving skills 
 Organises own workload and establishes priorities 
 Demonstrates good knowledge of standards and procedures required for own tasks 
 Excellent PC skills especially MS Excel 
 
 Work Authorization 

 Applicants must have the right to work in Ireland at the time of application and for the duration of employment.

 Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide employment permit sponsorship for this role. This includes Critical Skills Employment Permits, General Employment Permits, Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permits, Stamp 1G permissions, and other employment permits under Irish immigration frameworks.

 Working with Us 

 As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve. 

 Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities. 

 Reasonable Accommodation 

 Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com , or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.

title: Kepak Energy Usage Graduate Programme 2027 - Ireland
description:
Kepak Energy Usage Graduate Programme 2027 - Ireland We are seeking to recruit for the 2027 Energy Usage Graduate Programme across the following Kepak locations in Ireland:
 Clonee, Co.Meath 
 Ballymahon, Co.Longford 
 Watergrasshill, Co.Cork 
 Athleague,Co.Roscommon 
 Ballybay, Co.Monaghan 
 McCarrens, Cavan 
 
 Are you passionate about energy management and ready to learn? We’re looking for a Trainee Energy Efficient Manager/ Energy Graduate who is eager to grow and make a real impact in the field of sustainability. 
 This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to develop their skills and knowledge in energy management, while being supported with training and mentorship to build a successful career.
 In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience, manage energy efficiency projects, and help shape the future of energy management. We are looking for someone who is excited to learn, contribute, and grow in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
 Job Purpose: 
 To optimise energy resource management across our Midlands sites, helping us reduce consumption and improve sustainability through effective energy efficiency practices.
 What You’ll Do: 
 Lead the Charge: Play a key role in driving energy leadership, making efficiency a priority across our sites with support and guidance from senior team members.
 Create Impact: Develop and manage a 5-year energy plan aligned with our sustainability targets (Origin Green & SBTI).
 Water Stewardship Hero: Manage the company’s Water Stewardship Strategy and ensure sustainability is at the core of our operations.
 Energy Mapping: Develop and manage site-specific energy maps to optimise energy flow and consumption.
 System Optimisation: Learn to manage and optimise our Energy Management Systems (EMS) to drive energy efficiency improvements.
 Collaborate & Report: Lead weekly site energy management meetings, and represent our Midlands sites in monthly meetings.
 Continuous Improvement: Drive incremental improvements in energy consumption, always looking for ways to enhance sustainability practices.
 Project Delivery: Support the delivery of energy and water reduction projects with measurable results.
 What’s In It For You? 
 Career Development: You’ll receive plenty of training and mentorship to develop your skills and advance your career in energy management.
 Real Impact: Your work will contribute directly to our decarbonisation journey and a more sustainable future.
 Innovative Culture: Join a team that values forward-thinking ideas and approaches to energy challenges.
 Continuous Growth: We’ll support your ongoing learning and provide opportunities to expand your knowledge.
 This is more than just a job—it’s an exciting opportunity to grow your career while helping shape a sustainable future. Let’s build a sustainable tomorrow, today.
  
 What We’re Looking For: 
 We’re looking for someone who is innovative, driven, and ready to learn . If you’re passionate about energy efficiency and sustainability, and excited about a hands-on role that will help you grow professionally, this is the perfect opportunity for you. We want someone who thrives on collaboration, enjoys solving problems, and is motivated to make a positive impact on the environment.
 What You’ll Bring: 
 Analytical Mindset: You enjoy working with data and uncovering opportunities for improvement. 
 Communication Skills: You’re comfortable communicating clearly and confidently, whether in meetings or presentations.
 Project Management Enthusiast: You’re keen to learn how to manage multiple projects and deadlines effectively.
 Tech-Savvy: Strong computer and Excel skills will be key, and you’ll receive training on digital tools to optimise energy performance.
 Attention to Detail: You take pride in your work and ensure everything is completed with precision and care.
 Energy Interest: While you may not have all the technical expertise just yet, you have an eagerness to learn and a genuine interest in energy efficiency and sustainability.
 
 Start date: September 6th 2026
 Starting Salary - €33,500 with an up to €1,500 increase at the start of Year 2 to €35,000
 Read more about our programme and hear from some of our Graduates : https://www.kepak.com/careers/graduates/ 
 Requirements 
 Who are we looking for? 
 We are looking for hardworking and ambitious Graduates, who want to learn and grow in a challenging and fast paced environment, by performing real roles as part of your rotations. 
 You must be mobile and willing to travel throughout the programme to undertake development activities at any of our sites in the UK and Ireland.
 We will consider undergraduates from all disciplines and backgrounds.
 
 Knowledge and Skills 
 •Educational Background: Open to graduates from all disciplines. 
 •Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with people of different nationalities and backgrounds.
 
 Personal Attributes 
 •Driven and Ambitious: A desire to build a long-term career in the meat industry, with aspirations to become a manager in operations.
 •Eager to Learn: A proactive approach to learning, with a willingness to seek out information, ask questions, and absorb knowledge like a sponge.
 •Resilience: Comfortable working in a challenging environment, including exposure to abattoirs and carcass locations.
 
 We will be looking for alignment with our Core Values:
 Responsibility – Ability to work on your own initiative and take accountability for your actions
 Ambition – You will have the willingness and confidence to challenge yourself to be the best you can be and be driven to succeed
 Passion for Food – this is at the heart of everything we do, you must be passionate about every aspect of our industry
 Teamwork – ability to build positive relationships quickly with people from all cultures and career stages is pivotal
 Benefits 
 Employee Discount Scheme
 Service-Related Annual Leave
 Discounted Health Insurance
 Educational Assistance/ L&D
 Cycle to work scheme
 Employee assistance programme

Position Summary: The Finance Graduate role is a structured 12-month rotational programme within the Finance department in AstraZeneca Ireland.
 This is an entry-level role for graduates seeking to develop a career in Finance. The programme provides broad exposure to how Finance supports business performance, financial integrity, decision-making and compliance.
 Under the formal supervision of the Ireland CFO, and day-to-day guidance from the relevant rotation lead, the graduate will learn from experienced colleagues and contribute to defined activities across four areas: Distribution, Demand & Inventory Management (2 months); Finance Operations (2 months); Finance Business Partnering (4 months); and Financial Control & Reporting (4 months).
 The role is primarily focused on learning, development and capability building, while supporting the Finance team with day-to-day activities and improvement projects.
 
 Accountabilities: Complete the structured rotations in the agreed sequence and actively participate in learning, coaching and feedback sessions.
 Distribution, Demand & Inventory Management (2 months): support demand forecasts, inventory and wholesaler reporting, product-availability reviews, stock monitoring and cross-functional supply planning; gain exposure to distribution operations, returns and inventory risks.
 Finance Operations (2 months): support purchase-to-pay activities, purchase orders, invoices, vendor master data, healthcare professional and healthcare organisation payment processes, routine reconciliations and selected month-end activities. Support Transfer of Value (ToV) as a key part of the Finance Operations rotation, including data collection, quality review, reconciliation, preparation of reporting files, stakeholder follow-up and process guidance under supervision.
 Finance Business Partnering (4 months): support budgeting, forecasting, planning and monthly performance analysis; assist with cost reviews, business reporting and the identification of financial risks and opportunities; develop insights that support business decisions.
 Financial Control & Reporting (4 months): support month-end and year-end close, reconciliations, financial reporting, audit preparation, accounting activities, internal controls, compliance, risk management and supporting documentation.
 Collaborate with colleagues across Finance and other functions, maintaining accurate records and completing assigned activities to agreed quality standards and timelines.
 Contribute to Finance projects, process improvement and simplification initiatives.
 Participate in the company commitment to AI, Digital and Data excellence.
 
 
 Education, Qualifications, Skills and Experience: 
 Degree-level qualification in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business or a related discipline.
 Previous internship, placement or work experience in Finance, Accounting or Business.
 Experience analysing data and presenting findings.
