title: Graduate Program Associate - Manufacturing Technical Services
description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.
 
 Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.
 
 We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

 Job Description 
 
 Graduate Program Associate - Manufacturing Technical Services 
 2026 Intake, start date late November or early December 

 About Gilead: 
 Gilead Sciences, Inc. is a research-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops and commercialises innovative medicines in areas of unmet medical need.  With each new discovery and investigational drug candidate, we seek to improve the care of patients living with life-threatening diseases around the world.  Gilead’s therapeutic areas of focus include HIV/AIDS, liver diseases, cancer and inflammation, and serious respiratory and cardiovascular conditions.

 The Position 
 We have an opportunity for a Graduate to join our team for a 2 year programme, working within the Development and Technical Services function and rotating to key relevant areas as below.  Throughout this time, the successful candidate will be developed and mentored to aid your on the job learning. 

 The Development and Technical Services Department at our Manufacturing facility in Cork, support the introduction of new products to the site, the management of the lifecycle of products and supports the manufacture of Gilead products at third party manufacturing facilities.

 As a Graduate within our Development and Technical Services Department, you will have the opportunity to develop fundamental skills related to the manufacture of Oral Solid Dose Products including drug product formulation and process development, Quality by Design (QbD), oversight of GMP drug product manufacturing, global regulatory requirements and the application of operation excellence methodologies to problem solving and process improvement projects.

 The role offers potential development opportunities to the candidate in the following related functions: Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality Assurance and Validation.

 Key Responsibilities 
 The successful candidate will rotate into key areas, building responsibility and experience in the below:
 Supports the technical transfer of new products to site.
 Contributes to the completion of all technical support activities related to maintaining commercial product supplies.
 Contributes to and may lead complex processes across functions and interacts effectively with the other team members to ensure product meets regulatory, performance and cost requirements.
 Contributes to and may lead technical investigations of process deviations and assessment of their impact on product quality.
 Defines requirements for and reviews master batch records.
 Conducts non-routine analysis of raw materials, intermediates, and finished product samples.
 Troubleshoots instrumentation such as particle size analyzers or other measurement devices used in material characterization.
 Assists in the training of manufacturing technicians as needed.
 Applies knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs).
 Writes and executes SOPs, protocols and reports.
 Supports yield improvements on site.
 Supports qualification of new excipients and APIs to site.
 Identifies new technologies to support site requirements.
 
 Knowledge, Experience & Skills 
 A minimum 2.1 level 8 degree in a related area such as Science, Process, Chemical or Biopharmaceutical Engineering.
 Good problem solving and attention to detail.
 Highly adaptable and displaying good initiative.
 Strong communication, team player and ability to build effective relationships.
 Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
 
 Gilead Core Values 
 Integrity (Doing What’s Right)
 Teamwork (Working Together)
 Excellence (Being Your Best)
 Accountability (Taking Personnel Responsibility)
 Inclusion (Encouraging Diversity)
 

 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) It is the policy of Gilead Sciences, Inc. and its subsidiaries and affiliates (collectively "Gilead" or the "Company") to recruit select and employ the most qualified persons available for positions throughout the Company.  Except if otherwise provided by applicable law, all  employment actions relating to issues such as compensation, benefits, transfers, layoffs, returns from layoffs, company-sponsored training, education assistance, social and recreational programs are administered on a non-discriminatory basis (i.e. without regard to protected characteristics or prohibited grounds, which may include an individual’s gender, race, color, national origin, ancestry, religion, creed, physical or mental disability, marital status, sexual orientation, medical condition, veteran status, and age, unless such protection is prohibited by federal, state, municipal, provincial, local or other applicable laws).  Gilead also prohibits discrimination based on any other characteristics protected by applicable laws.

title: Graduate Programme, Audit - Dublin (Sept 2027)
description:
Why Start Your Career at S&W? 
 Starting your career is about more than just a job. It's about the people you learn from, the relationships you build and the experiences that shape you. Whether that's passing an exam, achieving a personal milestone or celebrating success with your colleagues, you'll be part of a team that's invested in your growth, celebrates your successes and supports you to be yourself.
 At S&W, you'll be given meaningful work from day one, while having the support, training and encouragement to help you succeed. You'll learn by doing, working alongside experienced colleagues, contributing to real projects and developing valuable professional skills from the start. As your confidence grows, so will your opportunities, with plenty of support along the way.
 As a growing accountancy and advisory firm, we offer a balance of opportunity and support. You'll learn from people at every level of the business, gain exposure to a variety of clients, industries and experiences, and develop the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to build a successful career.
 The Audit & Assurance Team at S&W 
 Our Audit & Assurance team works with a diverse range of clients, from entrepreneurial and family-owned businesses to charities, not-for-profit organisations and larger established businesses across a variety of industries.
 What sets Audit & Assurance at S&W apart is the breadth of experience you'll gain early in your career. You'll develop technical expertise, commercial awareness and a well-rounded understanding of how organisations operate, while working closely with experienced colleagues and gaining exposure to senior leaders and Partners. Together, this provides a strong foundation for a successful career in the profession.
 What Will You Be Doing? 
 As part of our Audit & Assurance team, you'll work alongside colleagues to deliver services to a variety of clients. You'll be involved in different stages of an engagement, gaining insight into how organisations operate and the role assurance plays in building confidence in financial reporting.
 Alongside your role, you'll study towards the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) or Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI) qualification. Through a combination of professional training and practical experience, you'll build a strong foundation in audit, accountancy and wider business advisory services. You'll be supported with funded training, dedicated study time and guidance from colleagues who have successfully completed the qualification themselves.
 Your work will include:
 Analysing financial information
 Testing processes and controls
 Building relationships with client teams
 Resolving audit and accountancy queries
 Supporting a range of audit and accountancy projects
 Whether you're based in one of our offices or working directly with clients, you'll contribute to meaningful work from day one while building the skills and confidence needed to become a trusted adviser.
 To Be Successful in This Role 
 You'll be someone who:
 Is curious, eager to learn and open to new challenges
 Enjoys working with others and building positive relationships
 Has a keen eye for detail and enjoys solving problems
 Is proactive and looks for ways to make a positive contribution
 Takes ownership of their development and is motivated to achieve their goals
 You'll also need to:
 Be committed to working towards the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) or Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI) qualification
 Have some accountancy experience, as part of your education or work experience
 Have obtained or be predicted a minimum 2:2 degree, in any discipline
 Minimum 400 Leaving Certificate points (or equivalent)
 Leaving Certificate O2 or H5 in Maths and English (or equivalent)
 Your Learning & Development 
 We'll support you throughout your qualification journey with a leading UK training provider, dedicated study time and practical experience that complements your learning. You'll join as part of a cohort and benefit from a support network that includes experienced colleagues, a buddy and our Learning & Development team, helping you make the most of the opportunities available to you.
 As a Colleague at S&W, You'll Have Access to Benefits That Include 
 Fully funded training towards professional qualifications
 Competitive salary
 Private medical insurance
 Life assurance
 Pension contribution
 Generous holiday package
 Option to purchase additional holiday
 Cycle to work scheme
 Season ticket loan
 Eye care support
 Shared parental leave
 Our Commitment to Inclusion 
 We are proud to value the differences that a diverse workforce brings, representative of society and our clients. At S&W we have a wide range of highly active employee resource groups and we’re delivering multiple diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives across the organisation. It is our commitment to provide a workspace where all colleagues, regardless of identity, background, or circumstance, feel respected as individuals and feel that they can achieve their full potential and work in a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment.

 Verifying and processing of loan lifecycle such as Interest, Paydowns, PIK, Drawdowns to agent notices.

 Reconciliations: 
 To review and resolve daily reconciliation breaks by liaising the client and NAV teams as required.

 Pricing:

 During the course of normal day to day operation, responsible for identifying any unusual or potentially suspicious transaction activity and must report and/or escalate in accordance with corporate policy and guidelines detailed in relevant operating procedures.

 Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Job Description:
IT Service Desk – L1 Engineer
Role and Responsibilities (Including, but not limited to)
Hungarian language proficiency is required
Act as a single point of contact for all modes of support such as phone calls, chat, web portal and emails from customers regarding their IT issues and queries
Basic and intermediate level of understanding related to Incident, Service Requests, Work Orders, Major Incidents, Change Request, Knowledge Articles, Knowledge Base, Problem Management, Problem Record and Priority/Severity types response/resolution timelines, CMDB, CIs etc.
Basic Active Directory knowledge. Creating user accounts, reset passwords, create groups etc.
1st and 2nd line support - troubleshooting of IT problems (in-house software to hardware, such as Laptops, PCs and Printers, IPhone, Exchange & Active Directory)
Provide basic troubleshooting and support for MS Office applications used (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Visio & Project)
Escalate unresolved calls to the appropriate support groups as per defined matrix and chase them until closure
Take ownership of user IT issues and follow up the status of problems with respective work groups on behalf of the end user
Communicate progress on Incidents and Service Requests in a timely manner back to the end user
To maintain a high-degree of customer service for all support queries and adhere to all ITIL & ITSM principles
Provide stats for the daily/weekly/monthly Service Desk report on call trends and other analysis
Publishing support documentation to assist staff with requests for information & provide staff training if required
Handling major incidents by coordinating with multiple teams
An ITIL qualification (ITIL V3 and Edition 4) is preferable, but not essential
Basic knowledge/awareness of Desktop Services, Networking, 0365, IT Security. MCP certification would be desirable
Demonstrated Experience
Excellent English communication skills (written and verbal) and telephone call handling etiquettes
2 to 4 years previous IT Service Desk experience required
Incident Management experience (Managing incidents including business expectations and communication)
Basic User & Security Group Active Directory administration
Strong knowledge of Microsoft based operating systems with emphasis on Windows 10 and Office 2010
Experience in using and troubleshooting Outlook (2010 and above) in a network environment (permissions, calendar sharing, delegation)
Minimum Education: Graduate in Engineering or Science
Behavioral Attributes
Strong communication skills, both verbal and written (English language)
Work well in team environments and be self-motivated/self-starter
Strong listening skills and ability to innovate and brainstorm around business ideas and needs
A self-motivated achiever who gains satisfaction from providing excellent customer service
Flexibility to support migration issues on the go, without supervision, deal with ambiguity, self-motivated and results driven in 24*7 environment
Able to derive results in an ambiguous setting and accomplish results in line with business needs

Job Description:
It’s never been a more exciting time to join Vistra.
At Vistra our purpose is progress. We believe that our clients have the power to change the world and to do great things for global progress, and we exist to remove the friction that comes from the complexity of global business – to help our clients achieve progress without friction.
But progress only happens when people come together and take action. And we’re absolutely committed to building a culture where our people can do just that.
We have an exciting opportunity for you to join our team as Facilities Administrator. Reporting to the Facilities Officer Channel Islands, this part-time, permanent position is based in Guernsey and offers local coverage, allowing you to make a significant impact on our local business and its growth.
Purpose of the Role:
Facilities is an organisational function which integrates people, place and process within the building environment with the purpose of improving the quality of life of people and the productivity of the core business.
Key Responsibilities:
Responsibilities are varied but typically include:
Providing front-of-house, visitor reception, hospitality, and customer service support, ensuring colleagues, visitors, and stakeholders receive a professional and welcoming experience.
Preparing meeting rooms for internal and external meetings, including room set-up and arranging refreshments when needed.
Supporting the handling of incoming and outgoing mail, courier deliveries, and distribution of correspondence.
Providing telephone coverage when required, including taking messages and directing calls appropriately.
Assisting with the booking and coordination of meeting rooms and office facilities.
Maintaining stationery, kitchen, and general office supplies.
Supporting the Facilities team with routine administrative tasks
When needed liaising with suppliers, contractors, couriers, and building management teams as directed.
Assisting with office housekeeping
Supporting office moves, workstation set-ups, equipment collections, and other ad hoc office activities as required.
Assisting with employee engagement, social, and office events when required.
Following Health & Safety procedures and reporting any issues or concerns to the appropriate person.
Undertaking any other reasonable duties required to support the smooth day-to-day running of the office.
Ad Hoc:
Providing general ad hoc administrative support to office-based teams.
Assisting with ad hoc document management, filing, archiving, and records retention activities.
Attributes and Technical Skills:
Adaptable and willingness to learn new skills
A committed professional team-player in providing quality support services
Able to balance multiple tasks/deliverables , seeking advice and/or guidance if required.
Able to respond to ad-hoc requests/unknown events
Able to resolve queries and find solutions timely.
Good communication and interpersonal skills
Obtain and maintain qualifications as required to fulfil role, incl Fire Marshall, First Aider, etc qualification
Good working knowledge of MS Excel, Word and Outlook
General ‘handyman’ type maintenance skills
Clean driving license
Relevant Experience:
Relevant experience in similar role

Accuracy and attention to detail

If you are excited about working with us, we encourage you to apply or have a confidential chat with one of our Talent Acquisition team members. Our goal is to make this a great place to work where all our people can thrive. We hope you join us on this exciting journey!

title: Middle Office Analyst/Associate
description:
PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns.
 
 Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking.  We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients.
 
 
 Position Description: 

 The candidate will be working in the Middle Office team in Dublin processing OTC and non-OTC trades encompassing Bond trades, FX, Derivatives Repos and Swaps with the aim being to provide support to the Portfolio Managers for any product traded. The primary responsibilities include regular contact with brokers to confirm trades, acting as escalation contact for settlement queries and monitoring the inhouse STP trade capture system. Thus, strong trade flow management ability and good settlement experience are vital. Furthermore, the Associate will be involved in interaction with the Dublin and the Newport Beach offices.

 Daily interaction with Portfolio Managers, Compliance, and Investment Operations.
 Monitor proprietary trade capture system: ensure accurate trade capture and completeness of tickets.
 Complete initial confirmation with the broker for trades executed in London office
 Trade floor support: run various daily trade-flow reports and any ad hoc reports requested by Portfolio Management team.
 Interaction with Back Office support functions: escalation contact for trade settlement. The back-office support is outsourced to State Street, daily contact through telephone and email. There is also direct contact with Brokers to resolve issues and support State Street as point of escalation.
 The team work on a weekly alternating shift pattern of 8.00am – 5.00pm, 9.30am – 6.30pm and 11.30am until close. On average the late shift is shorter, but a willingness to work later hours as required is essential for the role.
 
 Position Requirements: 
 Proven experience in a similar role within Asset Management or Investment Banking.
 Excellent attention to detail. Strong analytical ability is essential
 Strong verbal and written communication skills are vital to work within the firm’s demanding and focused environment.
 Capability to manage multiple tasks with tight time deadlines and possess strong problem-solving ability.
 Flexibility and ability to work under pressure with a fair degree of autonomy as well as in a team environment is essential. PIMCO works on a flat structure so ability to work with all levels of firm.
 Good working knowledge of MS Word, Excel, Access, MS Outlook and Bloomberg. Basic knowledge of other MS programs such as PowerPoint preferred. SQL and programming skills are a plus.
 Educated to degree level or equivalent is an advantage.
 Clear commitment to PIMCO’s culture, values and approach
 
 
 

 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Statement 
 PIMCO recruits and hires qualified candidates without regard to race, national origin, ancestry, religion (including religious dress and grooming practices), sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender (including gender identity and expression), age, military or veteran status, disability (physical or mental), any factor prohibited by law, and as such affirms in policy and practice to support and promote the concept of equal employment opportunity and affirmative action, in accordance with all applicable federal, state, provincial and municipal laws. The company also prohibits discrimination on other basis such as medical condition, or marital status under applicable laws. 
 
 Applicants with Disabilities 
 PIMCO is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. We provide reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities, including veterans, in job application procedures. If you have any difficulty using our online system due to a disability and you would like to request an accommodation, you may contact us at 949-720-7744 and leave a message. This is a dedicated line designed exclusively to assist job seekers with disabilities to apply online. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

title: Data analyst - AML
description:
About the team:

At SumUp, keeping our platform safe and compliant is critical to the trust of the millions of small businesses we serve around the world.

You’ll join our Global AML team at an exciting point in its growth. We’re expanding into new markets, evolving our AML capabilities, introducing AI-enabled controls, and navigating increasingly complex regulatory expectations.

As an AML Data Analyst, you’ll play a key role in turning AML data into actionable insights. Working closely with our global AML Operations and AML Governance teams, as well as colleagues across Engineering and Data, you’ll help us understand how our controls are performing, identify risks and gaps early, and make better decisions as our business scales.

This is a role where your analysis will go beyond reporting. The insights you generate will directly support how we monitor, improve, and strengthen our global AML framework.

 

What you’ll do:

  • Build and maintain AML dashboards, operational reports, and data packs used by AML Operations, AML Governance, and senior leadership
  • Design measurement frameworks that track AML operational KPIs, including case volumes, productivity, SLA adherence, and screening hit rates
  • Support AML teams by providing data extracts, analysis, trend identification, and root-cause analysis on AML control outputs and data quality issues
  • Run data validation and quality checks to keep AML data accurate and consistent across systems and regions
  • Support Transaction Monitoring and Sanctions/PEP screening through data analysis, requirements definition, and testing
  • Partner with Engineering and AML Operations to define data requirements and support automation projects
  • Build self-service analytics resources so AML Operations teams can explore data and find insights independently

 

You’ll be great for this role if you have:

  • Experience in data analytics, business intelligence, or a similar role within financial services, fintech, compliance, AML, or another regulated environment.
  • Strong SQL skills, including writing complex queries and building reliable datasets for reporting and analysis.
  • Practical experience with Python for data analysis and automation.
  • Experience working with a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to identify patterns, trends, root causes, and actionable insights from complex data.
  • The ability to translate technical analysis into clear recommendations and stories for non-technical stakeholders and senior leaders.
  • Experience working with data quality, validation, multiple data sources, and competing stakeholder priorities.
  • A proactive, curious mindset and interest in AML, financial crime, fintech, and emerging technologies such as AI, with the ability to take ownership in a fast-changing environment.

 

Why you should join SumUp:

🌎 Opportunity to work with a truly global, multicultural team from our homely, Dublin hub just steps from Harcourt Street Luas and charming Iveagh Gardens. This involves an office-first setup

🌈 Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: be part of a workplace that values and promotes diversity, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone's perspectives are respected and embraced

🚀 Enrolment onto our VSOP programme: you will own a stake in SumUp's future success

📚 A dedicated annual L&D budget of €2000 for your individual development, which can be used to attend conferences and/or advance your career through further education

🏖 Generous time off: 25 days paid leave, plus bank holidays and special leaves

🏥 Well-being support: health insurance for you and your family, and subsidised gym membership when you stay active

🚲 Easy commute perks: participate in the Bike-to-Work or TaxSaver Commuter Ticket scheme

💼 Financial growth: retirement savings match—SumUp tops your contributions up to 5%

🌴 Break4me: 1-month sabbatical after 3 years of service

🔗 Referral Bonus: earn additional rewards by referring talented individuals to join the SumUp team

 

SumUp is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer that proudly pursues and hires a diverse workforce. SumUp does not make hiring or employment decisions on the basis of race, colour, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age or any other basis protected by applicable laws or prohibited by Company policy. SumUp also strives for a healthy and safe workplace and strictly prohibits harassment of any kind.

 

About us:

Be empowered to do more that matters.

At SumUp, we're on a mission to empower small businesses across the globe by providing simple and affordable tools that allow them to thrive. Today, over 4 million businesses in 36 markets rely on SumUp as their financial partner to manage payments, finance and customer relationships.

title: Business Systems Administrator
description:
Business Data & Systems Administrator Cork
 9 month temporary contract
 About Your New Employer Join a leading global technology organisation supporting its Enterprise business across Europe, the Middle East, India and Africa.
 Work within an established Business Solutions & Systems team that supports strategic projects and important operational activities.
 About Your New Job As a Business Data & Systems Administrator, you will support the smooth running of enterprise data and systems across the business. You will work with internal teams, regional sales teams, finance, account managers and external partners.
 Your responsibilities will include:
 Processing requests to create, amend, deactivate and deduplicate customer master data records in line with established governance processes.
 Maintaining accurate records and ensuring changes are properly approved and reflected across relevant systems.
 Updating Tableau dashboards daily and investigating any data or reporting issues.
 Monitoring data flows between customer data management, CRM and ERP systems, escalating sync failures and data mismatches where required.
 Carrying out data quality checks, validation exercises and data-cleansing activities using Excel and other tools.
 Responding to partner and stakeholder queries by email and through internal query systems, ensuring timely and accurate responses.
 Supporting monthly claim audits with the Finance team by investigating discrepancies and reconciling data across systems.
 This role involves a high level of administration and repetitive tasks. It would suit someone who is organised, detail-focused and comfortable following established processes without losing concentration or motivation.
 What Skills You Need Previous experience in data administration, systems administration, business operations or a similar role.
 Experience working with large enterprise systems, such as CRM, ERP, MDM or CDM platforms.
 Strong Excel or Numbers skills, with experience managing and analysing large data sets.
 Excellent attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records.
 Good analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to respond professionally to partner and stakeholder queries.
 The ability to work autonomously while also contributing effectively within a wider team.
 Experience with Tableau, SQL or other reporting and data tools would be an advantage.
 A degree in Business, Data Administration, Information Systems, IT or a related discipline would be beneficial.
 What's on Offer Salary starting at €35,000
 9-month contract with a 39-hour working week, Monday to Friday.
 Hybrid working arrangement, with Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays office-based in Cork and potential remote working on Mondays and Fridays, subject to approval and operational requirements.
 The opportunity to work with a collaborative team in a well-established environment with clear processes and strong support.
 Exposure to enterprise systems, data governance, reporting and cross-functional business operations.
 What's Next If you are organised, detail-oriented and comfortable working with data, systems and high-volume queries, apply now by clicking the “Apply Now” button. If this role is not quite right but you are looking for a similar opportunity, please get in touch. We have a range of temporary, contract and permanent positions available.

title: Graduate Programme, Accountancy - Cork (Sept 2027)
description:
Why Start Your Career at S&W? 
 Starting your career is about more than just a job. It's about the people you learn from, the relationships you build and the experiences that shape you. Whether that's passing an exam, achieving a personal milestone or celebrating success with your colleagues, you'll be part of a team that's invested in your growth, celebrates your achievements and supports you to be yourself.
 At S&W, you'll be given meaningful responsibility from the start, alongside the support and guidance needed to help you succeed. You'll learn from experienced colleagues, develop valuable professional skills and build confidence as your career progresses.
 As a growing accountancy and advisory firms, we offer a balance of opportunity and support. You'll learn from people at every level of the business, gain exposure to a variety of clients, industries and experiences, and develop the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to build a successful career.
 The Accountancy Team at S&W 
 Our Business Outsourcing Services team helps businesses manage their finances, meet their reporting requirements and improve the effectiveness of their finance functions. Working with clients of different sizes, sectors and stages of growth, you'll gain first-hand experience of how businesses operate while helping them navigate day-to-day challenges and achieve their ambitions.
 What sets S&W apart is the breadth of experience you'll gain from the start. You'll work closely with a diverse range of businesses, gaining exposure to accounting, technology and advisory projects that go beyond traditional compliance work. This breadth of experience, combined with structured training and support, will help you build a strong foundation for a successful career in accountancy and business advisory.
 What Will You Be Doing? 
 As part of our Business Outsourcing Services team, you'll work closely with clients and their finance teams, supporting them with everything from statutory accounts and management reporting to VAT, bookkeeping and cloud accounting solutions. By combining technical expertise with practical advice, you'll help businesses operate more effectively and make better-informed decisions.
 Alongside your work, you'll study towards the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) or Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI) qualification, combining professional training with hands-on experience across a diverse range of clients and industries. This blend of technical learning and practical responsibility will help you develop a deep understanding of accounting, finance and business, providing a strong foundation for a successful career in accountancy and advisory services.
 Your work will include:
 Working with a diverse range of clients, supporting the delivery of statutory accounts, management accounts, bookkeeping, VAT returns and cloud accounting solutions.
 Building an understanding of our clients, their businesses and the challenges and opportunities they face.
 Preparing financial information and contributing to the delivery of high-quality client service.
 Developing expertise in cloud accounting platforms and digital finance technologies.
 Supporting clients with accounting queries, providing practical advice and helping to identify effective solutions.
 Using technology and automation to help clients improve efficiency and enhance their finance processes.
 Supporting software implementation, system optimisation and finance transformation projects.
 Managing priorities across a portfolio of clients while developing strong organisational, commercial and relationship-building skills.
 To Be Successful in This Role 
 You'll be someone who:
 Is curious, eager to learn and open to new challenges
 Enjoys working with others and building positive relationships
 Has a keen eye for detail and enjoys solving problems
 Is proactive and looks for ways to make a positive contribution
 Takes ownership of their development and is motivated to achieve their goals
 You'll also need to:
 Be committed to working towards the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) or Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI) qualification
 Have some accountancy experience, as part of your education or work experience
 Have obtained or be predicted a minimum 2:2 degree, in any discipline
 Minimum 400 Leaving Certificate points (or equivalent)
 Leaving Certificate O2 or H5 in Maths and English (or equivalent)
 Your Learning & Development 
 We'll support you throughout your qualification journey with a leading UK training provider, dedicated study time and practical experience that complements your learning.
 You'll join as part of a cohort and benefit from a strong support network that includes experienced colleagues, a buddy and our Learning & Development team. From your first day, you'll have people around you to guide you, answer questions and help you make the most of every opportunity.
 As a Colleague at S&W, You'll Have Access to Benefits That Include 
 Fully funded training towards professional qualifications
 Competitive salary
 Private medical insurance
 Life assurance
 Pension contribution
 Generous holiday package
 Option to purchase additional holiday
 Cycle to work scheme
 Season ticket loan
 Eye care support
 Shared parental leave
 Our Commitment to Inclusion 
 We are proud to value the differences that a diverse workforce brings, representative of society and our clients. At S&W we have a wide range of highly active employee resource groups and we’re delivering multiple diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives across the organisation. It is our commitment to provide a workspace where all colleagues, regardless of identity, background, or circumstance, feel respected as individuals and feel that they can achieve their full potential and work in a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment.
 We are happy to make any reasonable adjustments to accommodate for your needs throughout the application process. Please let your Recruiter know.
 IMPORTANT NOTES FOR COMPLETING YOUR APPLICATION 
 When you click on the 'I'm interested' button, you'll be taken to your profile page. We're currently updating it, but in the meantime:
 We can only accept one application to any of our programmes in a recruitment season. If you're unsuccessful, you'll need to wait until the following recruitment season to reapply.
 Under the Resume (CV) section, uploading a document is mandatory; however, it will not be formally reviewed.

Are you ready to apply your engineering or quantity surveying skills to one of the most ambitious and impactful infrastructure transformations in Ireland?
Do you have, or are you about to get, a degree in Electrical/Telecoms, Civil/ Structural, Mechanical / Energy Engineering or as a Quantity Surveyor?
If so, the ESB Technical Graduate Programme is your opportunity to work at the forefront of Ireland’s clean energy transition, designing, building, and maintaining the electricity network that connects homes, businesses, and communities across the country.
With over 1000 engineers, quantity surveyors and related technical professionals, ESB is dedicated to investing in engineering related expertise and developing critical skills to support Ireland’s future growth and development.
ESB’s Technical Graduate Programme is designed for STEM graduates with less than two years’ experience, offering structured development, real responsibility, and the opportunity to contribute to our Net Zero by 2040 strategy. At ESB, we believe our people are the driving force behind everything we do - today and into the future. That’s why investing in your growth, development and potential isn’t just part of our strategy, it’s at the very heart of it.
The programme has a wide variety of opportunities:
You’ll work alongside experienced engineers, quantity surveyors and technical professionals on projects that matter.
What You’ll Work On:
Delivering energy infrastructure projects for Ireland, with opportunities to be involved at every stage of the project lifecycle
Designing, planning and building the electricity network of the future
Helping to shape ESB's generation fleet on site, ensuring the safety, reliability and resilience of our thermal and renewable energy facilities
Supporting Ireland's largest private telecoms network, helping keep ESB's infrastructure connected and operating safely
Supporting ESB’s customers to optimise their energy use & develop sustainable energy solutions
Our bespoke Early Career Technical Talent Programme includes:
Structured, timely learning and development through formal as well as on-the-job opportunities
Work assignments giving appropriate breath of learning to facilitate career progression
Performance targets set to challenge & develop you while you contribute to ESB’s strategy
Mentoring & career support to enable you to find the right career in the company
Social networking to develop peer supports & relationships across ESB
In addition:
As an employee on our Technical Graduate Programme, you will enjoy our many benefits including a competitive salary and bonus, performance related promotions and a comprehensive benefits package built on the four pillars of reward, career, community, and wellbeing.
Location
Nationwide
What We Look For:
A Masters, Honours or Ordinary degree (or near completion in 2027) in Electrical/Telecoms, Civil/Structural, Mechanical/Energy Engineering or Quantity Surveying, with a minimum Second Class Honours Grade 1 (2.1) result
Excellent analytical skills combined with the ability to learn quickly
Proven ability to deliver results in a fast-paced team environment
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Flexibility regarding work location (for your development you may need to change work location during the programme)
Your CV should be no longer than 2 pages and clearly outline the following:
Details of ALL your qualifications including titles, institutions, years of commencement and (projected) completion with your results to date
Your relevant modules and academic projects
All your work experience
Any relevant external interests / pursuits
A contact telephone number (with voicemail enabled)
A valid email address to reach you on
Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Statement
ESB is committed to being an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all sections of society and ensure that no one is discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion or belief, ethnicity or nationality, disability, age, citizenship, marital status, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation or gender identity, or any other basis as protected by law.
Applicants who anticipate requiring assistance or reasonable accommodations for any part of the application or interview process may contact, in confidence, recruitment@esb.ie.
About ESB
Join us in our mission to achieve a net-zero electricity system by 2040. ESB is Ireland’s leading energy utility, with activities spanning electricity generation, transmission and distribution, energy supply, energy services and international consultancy. Operating in Ireland, Northern Ireland and Great Britain, we invest over €1 billion each year to deliver a new energy future based on reliable, affordable zero-carbon electricity.

title: Consultant Insurance Services
description:
About Northern Trust 

 As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. 

 Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. 

 With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. 

 About The Role : 
 The Consultant Insurance Services post, reporting through Northern Trust Services and part of the Enterprise Financial Planning & Analysis function, will aid in the strategic planning, development, organization, execution, implementation, data gathering and application of the Northern Trust suite of corporate insurance programs. The individual will manage/maintain property lists, tracks assets, and communicate with NT partners with insurance lease provisions, vendor service agreements (collaborating with Procurement as necessary) and insurance compliance  with local regulatory bodies and requirements. He/she will serve as a local point of contact to collect underwriting data, compare insurance coverage terms and conditions, review quotes and policies for accuracy, identify coverage gaps and provide evidence of insurance per client’s requests. They will work with insurance brokerage representatives and intermediaries and may be called upon to explain insurance terms and concepts to local partners. The candidate will be called upon to strengthen the group’s internal governance processes relative to claim reporting practices and respond to regulatory, client and audit requests. The ideal candidate will manage the function’s insurance dashboard and may assume escalating responsibilities based on performance, aptitude, and business needs. 
   
 This individual will also assist the Trust Real Estate Insurance risk manager on insurance program renewals, program maintenance and policy placement. 
   
 Responsibilities / Duties : 
 Assist with the insurance renewal activities with insurance broker
 Maintain insurance schedule and updates underwriting data for changes
 Collaborate with internal (Northern Trust Finance) and external parties to ensure insurance coverages are invoiced timely and policies updated in the document repository
 Advise insurers of incidents and potential claims pursuant to policy provisions
 Review property reports, verify insurance coverage for accuracy, and confirm inclusion on Master Global insurance programs as needed
 Maintain insurance dashboard
 Submit funding requests, assist with premium allocations and process policy endorsements in software applications (Yardi)
 
 Skills/ Experience Required : 
 General understanding of the insurance industry
 Excellent analytical, organizational, and oral and written communication skills
 Ability to prepare clear, comprehensive, written and verbal reports for senior management
 Ability to appropriately prioritize and execute projects in a timely manner
 Ability to analyze and interpret contract language, including insurance policy provisions
 Ability to analyze complex issues, review alternatives, and develop sound recommendations
 Ability to work well independently and in a team environment
 Possess working knowledge of MS office (MS Word, MS Excel, and Powerpoint) applications Power BI and Python experience a plus
 Ability to manage a wide variety of tasks from start to finish
 ARM or CPCU insurance designation (or the International equivalent) a plus
 Experience with analytics, visualization, document management, AI, and automation software applications
 Travel :  As needed (less than 10% per year)

 Work Authorization 

 Applicants must have the right to work in Ireland at the time of application and for the duration of employment.

 Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide employment permit sponsorship for this role. This includes Critical Skills Employment Permits, General Employment Permits, Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permits, Stamp 1G permissions, and other employment permits under Irish immigration frameworks.

 Working with Us 

 As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve. 

 Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities. 

 Reasonable Accommodation 

 Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com , or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.

Allianz has established a specialist subsidiary company for Reinsurance P&C business in Dublin, Allianz Re Dublin Dac (‘the Company') . The Company's premises are at Allianz House, Elmpark, Merrion Road, Dublin 4.

The Opportunity 

Allianz Reinsurance is seeking a Reinsurance Finance Analyst (P&C) to join their finance team. The roles requires a finance professional (reinsurance/insurance) with a structured, analytical mindset and the ambition to help shape how finance processes work, not simply operate them. The role sits at the intersection of reinsurance accounting, business understanding, and process improvement, with a strong focus on challenging existing ways of working and building better, more scalable solutions. 

The role holder will collaborate and contribute as part of a global team, working closely with internal and external stakeholders including cedents, retrocessionaries, vendors, banks and local authorities. A key part of the role is to understand the underlying reinsurance transactions, connect commercial substance with accounting, tax and reporting requirements, and translate this into robust, efficient and well-controlled processes. 

This position is suited to someone who enjoys change, takes ownership, asks thoughtful questions and is motivated by making things better. The role is within a continuously growing reinsurance company and provides strong opportunities to develop across finance, reinsurance and transformation

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Support the delivery of accurate, well-controlled accounting and reporting outputs for reinsurance business under different accounting and regulatory regimes, including IFRS 17 and Solvency II. 

  • Understand how the commercial and technical characteristics of reinsurance transactions are reflected in accounting, tax, regulatory and reporting treatments across different regimes. 

  • Analyse reinsurance structures, data flows and operational processes to ensure that accounting and reporting processes reflect the economic substance of the underlying business. 

  • Challenge existing processes, identify weaknesses or inefficiencies, and drive practical improvements that increase quality, transparency, control and scalability. 

  • Take ownership of complex topics from problem definition through to implementation, working independently while keeping colleagues and stakeholders appropriately involved. 

  • Contribute to finance transformation initiatives, including process documentation, data analytics, automation and the sensible use of AI or digital tools where they support better outcomes. 

  • Collaborate and contribute in a global team, managing relationships with internal and external stakeholders including Allianz Group, Allianz Re SE, cedents, retrocessionaries and local authorities. 

  • Support management reporting for local committees and Board meetings, translating complex technical matters into clear, decision-useful information. 

  • Support day to day activities as part of a reinsurance finance team. 

Key Requirements / Skills & Experience 

Essential: 

  • Relevant experience in reinsurance/ non life insurance finance is essential, preferably gained in accounting, while strong candidates from actuarial, controlling or financial reporting will also be considered. 

  • Experience with IFRS 17, Solvency II,  and reinsurance accounting  is strongly preferred. 

  • Strong technical and quantitative background, with the ability to understand complex reinsurance structures, data flows and financial impacts. 

  • Strong analytical mindset, with the ability to question existing processes, identify root causes and develop practical solutions. 

  • Comfortable working with data and tools (including AI) such as Excel; experience with Power BI, automation or workflow tools would be an advantage. 

  • Highly motivated, self-organised and comfortable taking responsibility in an environment where priorities, processes and requirements continue to evolve. 

  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to explain technical topics clearly and work constructively across teams, functions and locations. 

Desirable: 

  • At Allianz Reinsurance, we are committed to embracing innovation and the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to drive innovation and business success. We are seeking candidates who demonstrate curiosity, adaptability and have a proactive approach to learning and development. An awareness of AI-powered tools, data-driven decision making and data analysis will be highly valued. 

 

 

Regulatory Notice: 

Appointment to this role will be subject to the requirements provided for by the Central Bank of Ireland. Please refer to the Central Bank of Ireland’s Guidance on Minimum Competency Code: Minimum Competency | Central Bank of Ireland as well as F&P Standards and the Corporate Governance Requirements: Fitness & Probity | Central Bank of Ireland. This includes the requirements provided for by the Central Bank Individual Accountability Framework Act 2023. The successful candidate will be provided with the relevant Conduct Standards (including Additional Conduct Standards) training, where required. Full details are available via the Central Bank website: Individual Accountability Framework  | Central Bank of Ireland. 

Allianz Re Dublin Dac. is regulated by the Central Bank of Ireland.

title: IT Business Analyst
description:
McDermott Laboratories Limited 
 Viatris is a global healthcare company uniquely positioned to bridge the traditional divide between generics and brands, combining the best of both to more holistically address healthcare needs globally. With a mission to empower people worldwide to live healthier at every stage of life, we provide access at scale, currently supplying high-quality medicines to approximately 1 billion patients around the world annually and touching all of life's moments, from birth to the end of life, acute conditions to chronic diseases. 
 
 We have been included on number of award lists that demonstrate the impact we are making. 
 
 Our global portfolio includes best-in-class, iconic brand-name products as well as global key brands; generics, including branded and complex generics; and other offerings across a wide range of therapeutic areas. We are committed to helping create healthier communities worldwide through education, outreach and better access to treatment. 
 For those driven to live their lives with purpose, Viatris helps employees realise their full potential by creating a collaborative culture that fosters courage and resilience. Viatris is more than just a place to work. This is a place to make a difference in the world. 
   
 Our Global Device Development organization is an innovative, technically strong, and fully integrated team focused on delivering high-quality, safe, and effective device and combination products to meet evolving patient healthcare needs worldwide. 
   
 The IT Business Analyst position will assist in pursuing solutions that address the emerging needs of the manufacturing business in Europe and provide day-to-day support to the sites. As part of the regional team the IT Business Analyst will also assist with implementing global IT projects in the region and ensure the harmonization of best practices across the European manufacturing sites. 
   
 Every day, we rise to the challenge to make a difference and here’s how the IT Business Analyst will make an impact. 
   
 Key responsibilities for this role include: 
  
 ·       Understand Viatris’ business, pain points, needs, and strategic plans around manufacturing area.
 ·       Able to manage complex process analyses for all areas of operations within the site. Including manufacturing/packaging, quality, warehouse, and plant maintenance processes.
 ·       Facilitates process to gather requirements in support of efforts led by a Solutions Leader or Project Manager. Evaluates information gathered from multiple sources, reconciles conflicts, decomposes high-level information into details, differentiates between actual and required user needs.
 ·       Participates in global IT projects at a plant site, as well as in projects that are strictly local in nature.
 ·       Skilled in general business analysis and validation techniques. Elicits requirements using interviews, analysis of documents, requirements workshops, surveys, site visits, business process descriptions, use cases, scenarios, and workflow analysis and other relevant techniques, e.g., Value Stream Mapping.
 ·       Maintains current understanding of trends and issues in the IT industry, including current technologies in consideration by corporate IT.
 ·       Provides day-to-day support related to the installed application portfolio at a site. Collaborates with other IT teams to resolve day-to-day issues, as needed, such as the Run team.
 ·       Proactively connects, collaborates, and maintains communication with external and internal customers to analyze information needs and functional requirements and deliver project methodology artifacts as needed (following Viatris’ project methodology)
 ·       Provides support and/or direction to project and program manager(s) in overcoming hurdles and moving projects forward by proactively mitigating open issues and project risks. Maintains consistent communication channels between all vested parties (steering committee, business sponsors, IT stakeholders, project team, etc.). Supports organization change management efforts in areas of responsibility.
 ·       Acts as gate keeper/local system owner for Global applications installed at the site. Ensures GxP and SOX compliance as appropriate.
 ·       Function as a coordinator between SAP end users and the IT support organization, ensuring that business needs are fully documented and understood, and assist the IT organization in prioritizing requirements, developing, and testing solutions, and delivering enhanced SAP functionality to the business.
 ·       Play an active role in application integration implementations for EU sites
 The minimum qualifications for this role are: 
 ·       Must understand overly complex technology projects and concepts as they relate to high-level business objectives, and ability to present those concepts to both IT and non-IT audiences in a concise and easily understandable manner.
 ·       Minimum of a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) and minimum of 2 years of experience. However, a combination of experience and/or education will be taken into consideration.
 ·       Functional knowledge of the following SAP operations modules: Materials Management, Warehouse Management, Production Planning and Quality Management.
 ·       Ability to develop a tactical partnership with business customers.
 ·       Strong understanding of highly technical custom software solutions.
 ·       Ability to drive complex conceptual discussions and develop system requirements. This includes the ability to generate innovative ideas to resolve problems.
 ·       Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group of executives, managers, and subject matter experts.
 ·       Strong understanding of Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) or Manufacturing Execution System (MES) applications.
 ·       Strong understanding of IT/OT applications’ System Development Life Cycle and related CSV activities.

title: Attack Surface Research Analyst
description:
Job Description: 
 
 Job Title: Attack Surface Research Analyst 
 Corporate Title: Up to Vice President  
 Location:  Chester or Dublin 
 
 Company Overview :
 
 At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection.  We do this by driving Responsible Growth and delivering for our clients, teammates, communities and shareholders every day.
 
 Being a Great Place to Work is core to how we drive Responsible Growth.  This includes our commitment to being a diverse and inclusive workplace, attracting and developing exceptional talent, supporting our teammates’ physical, emotional, and financial wellness, recognizing and rewarding performance, and how we make an impact in the communities we serve.
 
 At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.  Join us!
 
 Location Overview: 
 
 Chester 
 Find us in the city of Chester, a destination renowned for its culture, history, and beauty. Working at Bank of America Chester offers a far-reaching global career for a world-renowned organisation, whilst being ideally situated against the backdrop of the rolling North Wales hills and the banks of the serene River Dee.
 
 Central Park 
 Overlooking the spectacular Iveagh Gardens with access to all amenities in the beating heart of central Dublin is our Park Place office. Travel options include the LUAS, Dublin Bus networks as well as the Dublin Bikes station, positioned just outside our front doors. As part of our commitment to supporting staff travel to and from work in the most sustainable way possible, we also provide tax saver tickets as part of our award-winning benefits package which means getting to work has never been easier
 
 Role Description: 
 
 The Cyber Security Assurance, Attack Surface Research (ASR) role maintains and performs queries across a wide array of asset enumeration and research toolsets, spanning on-premises and cloud platforms, to effectively map, measure, and report on the topography of the Bank’s network endpoints and other assets for vulnerability risk.
 
 In addition to core investigative matters, the role is responsible for ensuring the stability and enhancement of the backend infrastructure used to create high quality queries, datasets, and visualizations from various enterprise platforms and security data sources. Individuals in the role will routinely ad-hoc investigate infrastructure and vulnerability asset data in support of partner Information Security teams, to help correctly ascertain and communicate vulnerability risk to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.
 
 The role requires a highly collaborative, analytical and detail-oriented mindset, with a focus on ensuring conclusions and/or insights reflect innovative thinking as well as accurate information gathering under time pressure to fully answer three core questions as quickly as possible.
 
 •     Do we have it?
 •     Are we vulnerable?
 •     Is it exploitable?
 
 Persons in this role operate as part of a team developing methods to quickly reference systems of record (SORs), systems of origin (SOOs) and other available data stores to provide a comprehensive, reliable and timely view of the Bank’s Attack Surface, both as it relates to vulnerability exploitation risk as well as other concerns.
 
 Responsibilities: 
 Create SQL and Python scripts within Qualys, Tanium and BladeLogic to query datasets, to support Attack Surface Review.
 Perform hands-on analysis of large-scale datasets to correlate map, measure, and report on the overall vulnerability attack surface of the Bank.
 Leverage Python, SQL, and other languages/platforms to automate data ingestion, transformation, enrichment, and quality validation (ETL)
 Develop and maintain visualizations and reports in Power BI or MS-Reporting Services (SSRS) MS-Integration Services (MSIS) that support operational teams, cyber leadership, and stakeholders across Information Security and broader risk teams.
 Possesses network architecture experience sufficient to reasonably speak to the Bank’s data network and architecture in a timely manner to major inquiries as both an individual and as part of projects by the larger team.
 Clearly communicate findings through written analysis and live discussions, including executive level summaries
 
 What we’re looking for: 
 Deep analytical, problem solving, and conceptual thinking skills

title: Equity Research Analyst
description:
Overview 

 Susquehanna is a global quantitative trading firm powered by scientific rigor, curiosity, and innovation. Our culture is intellectually driven and highly collaborative, bringing together researchers, engineers, and traders to design and deploy impactful strategies in our systematic trading environment. To meet the unique challenges of global markets, Susquehanna applies machine learning and advanced quantitative research to vast datasets in order to uncover actionable insights and build effective strategies. By uniting deep market expertise with cutting-edge technology, we excel in solving complex problems and pushing boundaries together. 
  
 As an Analyst on Susquehanna’s Research team, you will partner with our senior analysts and traders to identify investment opportunities in the equity or options market. Research analysts provide real-time opinions on breaking news and in-depth analysis of future volatility events. You will be responsible for finding opportunities that other market participants may not be capitalizing on, either by discovering new information or considering existing knowledge from a different perspective. Analysts are embedded in a sector-focused trading desk and the analysis you provide will directly impact trading decisions. 
  
 At Susquehanna we place a high value on education and development. You will experience this dedication to training first hand as you work collaboratively with the research analysts and traders on your desk to gain the practical exposure needed to perform your daily responsibilities. You will also learn about options and the decision-making strategies that our traders employ. This role provides the unique opportunity to combine the quantitative aspects of finance with creative problem solving in order to develop trade ideas in a fast paced proprietary trading environment. 
    
 What you’ll be doing: 
 Identifying and analysing upcoming volatility events 
 Providing real-time opinions on breaking news 
 Forecasting dividends 
 Evaluating special situations such as mergers and acquisitions and other corporate actions 
 Collaborating with derivative traders on investment ideas 
 Traveling to company events and conferences as required 
 Performing stock valuation analysis 
 
 What we're looking for 

 Minimum of a Bachelor's degree 
 3 years’ + experience in financial markets or progress towards CFA qualification an advantage 
 Strong written, analytical, and financial research skills 
 Demonstrable interest in, and some knowledge of, macroeconomic environment and political events 
 Ability to prioritize and complete multiple tasks in a fast paced, dynamic environment 
 Familiarity with a trading environment and derivative products preferred 
 Must be a self-starter, a quick learner, an effective communicator, and resourceful in solving problems 
 Willingness to work additional and flexible hours when necessary 
   
 If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to recruiting@sig.com . Any resume or referral submitted in the absence of a signed agreement will not be eligible for an agency fee.

title: Accounts Payable & Cost Analyst
description:
About us  
 At Davy, it’s the unique talents of all our people that have been the foundations of our success for 100 years. As we continue to grow, so do you. Because you are not just part of our team – you are a key player in shaping our future.  
 At Davy, you are the difference.   
 Established in 1926, the Davy Group sits at the heart of wealth and capital in Ireland, providing a broad range of services to high-net-worth individuals, self-directed investors, small-to-medium enterprises, credit unions, corporations, and domestic & international institutional investors.  
 Our culture is shaped around three values, which are at the heart of everything we do: client success, one Davy, and building a proud legacy. Sharing the same goals, we work together to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients. As part of a team of over 900, you will be encouraged to learn and to grow, both professionally and personally.  
 
 About the role 
 An exciting opportunity has arisen to join Davy as an Accounts Payable & Cost Analyst in our Finance Department. The Accounts Payable & Cost Analyst is responsible for ensuring the efficient and controlled processing of supplier transactions, maintaining strong governance across the purchase-to-pay process, and delivering insightful cost analysis to support budget management and business decision-making.
 The role combines operational finance responsibilities with analytical and business partnering activities, ensuring supplier payments are processed accurately and on time while identifying, investigating, and resolving cost variances. The postholder will work closely with budget owners and operational teams to improve financial awareness, enhance controls, and drive continuous process improvements across finance processes.
 In the role, the successful candidate will:
 Accounts Payable & Governance 
 Manage the end-to-end accounts payable process, ensuring invoices are processed accurately and in line with company policies and procedures.
 Review and set up new suppliers, ensuring all required documentation, approvals, and due diligence checks are completed.
 Maintain supplier master data and ensure information remains accurate and up to date.
 Ensure compliance with internal controls, delegated authorities, procurement policies, and governance requirements.
 Process and validate supplier invoices, matching invoices to purchase orders and approvals where applicable.
 Investigate and resolve invoice queries, discrepancies, and supplier issues in a timely manner.
 Prepare and execute supplier payment runs in accordance with payment schedules and approval processes.
 Reconcile supplier statements and resolve outstanding balances.
 Support internal and external audit requirements relating to accounts payable activities.
 Cost Analysis 
 Analyse expenditure across departments and cost centres to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and anomalies.
 Produce regular cost reporting and variance analysis against budgets and forecasts.
 Investigate budget variances, identifying root causes and providing recommendations for corrective action.
 Challenge cost assumptions and provide insight into spending patterns.
 Support budgeting and forecasting processes by providing accurate expenditure analysis and commentary.
 Identify areas where costs can be controlled, reduced, or better managed.
 Prepare management information and financial analyses to support decision-making.
 Assist with month-end activities, including accrual reviews, prepayments, expenditure validation, and reporting.
 Process Improvement 
 Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and controls across accounts payable and cost management processes.
 Review existing workflows and recommend process enhancements to reduce manual activity and eliminate recurring issues.
 Support the implementation of system improvements, automation initiatives, and digital finance solutions.
 Develop and maintain process documentation and standard operating procedures.
 Promote best practice financial processes across the organisation.
 Drive initiatives that improve service delivery to suppliers and internal stakeholders.
 Stakeholder Management 
 Build effective working relationships with managers, procurement teams, and suppliers.
 Act as a trusted finance contact for operational teams.
 Support non-finance stakeholders in understanding financial information and governance requirements.
 Communicate financial issues, risks, and opportunities clearly and effectively.
 
 Requirements 
 About you 
 We are looking for somebody who has the following background and skills: 
 Experience working within Accounts Payable or Finance Operations.
 Experience processing invoices and supplier payments.
 Experience performing financial analysis and investigating financial variances.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
 Ability to interpret financial data and explain findings to non-finance stakeholders.
 Strong organisational and prioritisation skills.
 Good stakeholder management and communication skills.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial systems.
 Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
 Desirable 
 AAT qualified, part-qualified ACCA/CIMA, or equivalent.
 Experience with ERP systems such as SAP.
 Benefits 
 What we offer  
 At Davy, our people are our biggest investment. In today’s fast-moving world, we know it’s important to feel secure and empowered. That’s why Davy benefits support you through all of life’s stages, offering health and wellness, flexible working options, flexible benefits allowance, learning and development opportunities, through to assisted retirement planning.   
 Health and Wellbeing   
 Psychological safety, emotional wellbeing and support are a priority at Davy. We offer a comprehensive Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) and mental health first aid. Our Sports & Social teams promote physical wellbeing and social connection.  
 Reward and Recognition   
 We offer a competitive remuneration package to include salary, bonus, pension and a host of additional benefits to protect you and your family when it matters most.  
 Growth and Development   
 Our award-winning L&D function supports you and your growth at Davy. We offer a comprehensive range of professional and personal development opportunities. Our culture supports learning, and we encourage you to explore more at Davy.  
 Positive Workplace   
 Our workplace is inclusive, diverse, and offers everyone a sense of belonging. We are flexible and continue to support a hybrid working model. You will get to be your best at Davy.
 Values and Culture   
 Exceptional client outcomes delivered by a world class team, underpinned by our core Davy values – One Team, Client Success, and Proud Legacy.
 Important Information  
 Davy is an equal opportunities employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace. We value diversity in both background and experience, and even if you don’t meet all of the requirements outlined in the job description, we still encourage you to apply. We review all applications received. As part of our commitment to creating an accessible environment, we want to ensure that everyone has an equal opportunity to participate in the interview process. If you require any reasonable accommodations, please let us know, and we will do our best to make the necessary arrangements.  
 Appointment to this role is subject to the candidate's eligibility to work in Ireland. 
 Where agency assistance is required, our Recruitment Team will engage directly with suppliers. Unsolicited CVs / profiles supplied to us by recruitment agencies will not be accepted for this role. 
 Davy Group is a member of the Bank of Ireland Group.

People & Culture Administrator – 12 months FTC 
 Because people are more than just your day job. Connect, our way.
 People and Culture at Primark
 Our team has created a workplace of inspiration and growth. Be a part of building an inclusive and empowering culture, where every colleague’s unique abilities are recognised and celebrated. Collaborate with a team committed to the wellbeing of our workforce, and define what it means to work at Primark.

 What You’ll Do as a People & Culture Administrator – 12 months FTC 
 In your role, you’ll collaborate with different people across a range of skillsets and departments. Here’s a flavour of your day-to-day:
 Coordinate end-to-end onboarding and offboarding activities, including induction planning, new starter inductions, employment documentation, and exit interviews to ensure a seamless colleague experience.
 Manage core People Administration processes, including colleague movements, organisational charts, absence management, service ticket resolution, people records, and employee queries.
 Support performance and people lifecycle activities by maintaining accurate documentation and assisting with end-of-year performance cycle preparation.
 Oversee payroll and finance administration, including payroll reviews, purchase order processing, invoice tracking, and payroll data validation.
 Enhance colleague experience by supporting recognition initiatives, People & Culture projects, and fostering strong stakeholder relationships across the business.
 Produce accurate people data and reports while maintaining confidentiality, driving process improvements, and supporting the delivery of the People & Culture strategy.
 

 What You’ll Bring   
 Here at Primark, we want everyone to feel valued – so please bring your authentic self to work, of course with some other key experience and abilities for this role in particular:
 Previous experience in a similar P&C/HR administration role, with knowledge of Workday or other P&C systems being an advantage.
 Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office and other business software applications.
 Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment while using initiative and managing priorities independently.
 Excellent attention to detail, accuracy, and a proactive approach to work.
 Strong planning, organisation, and coordination skills.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, strong interpersonal skills, a positive attitude, and a P&C qualification would be desirable.
 

 What You’ll Ge t  
 The work you do shapes the impact we have. We’re focused on providing you with the culture to reach your potential. Your wellbeing is our top priority.   
 Let’s talk lifestyle: 27 days of leave, plus bank holidays and if you want, you can buy 5 more. Because Primark is all about tailoring to you, we offer Tax Saver Tickets, fitness centre, and a subsidised cafeteria.
 Does this sound like you? Great, because we can’t wait to see what you’ll bring. You’ll be supported within a team of equally capable people, celebrating who you are and aiding you reach your potential. At Primark, we’re excited about our future - and we’re excited to develop yours.  
 About Primark  
 At Primark, people matter. They’re the beating heart of our business and the reason we’ve grown from our first store in Dublin in 1969 to a £9bn+ turnover business and over 80,000 colleagues and over 440 stores in 17 countries today. Our values run through everything we do. In essence, we're Caring and always strive to put people first. We're also Dynamic, bravely pushing the boundaries to stay ahead. And finally, we succeed Together.  
 Our Values: 
 Every person impacts the culture at Primark. Our values: Caring (we always strive to put people first), Dynamic (we bravely push the boundaries to stay ahead) and Together (we learn more, laugh more and achieve more as a team) outline how we work with each other, our suppliers, and our partners. We want to continue to create amazing cultures across Primark and need everyone to play their part in making this happen by living our values.
