We invite you to grow your career with us, experience our caring culture, and enjoy work-life balance. Here, there’s no limit to what you can achieve.
 
 
Financial Accountant 
 

 FINANCIAL ACCOUNTANT                                                       
 Key roles 
 The Financial Accountant will play a pivotal role within the financial team. 
 Specific responsibilities (including but not limited to) 
 Full ownership of the General Ledgers. 
 Responsible for the accuracy of all financial data. 
 Assist the Head of Finance in the supervision and oversight of Accounts Assistant roles. 
 Review processes and drive efficiencies. 
 Oversee the Accounts Assistant roles when required. 
 Manage the preparation and completion of the month-end process. 
 Ensure accuracy and completeness of the day-to-day key financial reporting outputs. 
 Partnering with key stakeholders to ensure all revenue and costs are transacted into the Finance system prior to month-end deadlines.

 Ad hoc duties and projects as requested by the business. 
   
 Qualifications/skills

 People person who has the skill set to ensure the ethos of Sedgwick Ireland ‘caring counts’ is embedded within the team.

 Personal attributes 
 High levels of motivation and enthusiasm.

 A positive attitude, co-operative, willing to comply with company policies and procedures and work constructively with colleagues.

 Capable of working well in a team environment – guide / mentor Accounts Assistants.

 Proactive approach.

description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Abbott in Ireland 
 Abbott has maintained a strong presence in Ireland since 1946 and celebrates its 80th anniversary in the country in 2026. The company supports the Irish healthcare sector with a broad portfolio spanning diagnostics, diabetes care, medical devices and nutritional products. Today, Abbott employs more than 6,500 people across ten sites located in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford and Sligo.

 About Abbott 
 Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

 Abbott Ireland Nutrition Division Cootehill Cavan 
 Abbott Nutrition produces a range of infant formulae in all pack sizes under the brand name “Similac”. To complement the range of “Similac” infant formulae, the facility also manufactures a range of follow-on formulae under the brand name of “Gain”. The essential ingredient is liquid skim-milk and this is combined with carbohydrate, vegetable oils, vitamins and minerals. The product is blended, pasteurised, dried and packaged at the site and once packaged, is distributed to Europe, South East Asia, the Middle East, Latin America and Canada.

 Established in 1975, Abbott Nutrition in Ireland is the largest powder manufacturing facility for the production of infant formulae within the Abbott Corporation worldwide.  Approximately 1,000 dairy farms in Ireland and Northern Ireland supply quality milk to the Cootehill facility which processes 500,000 litres per day. This secure supply together with Ireland’s reputation as a green, clean environment is of significant strategic importance to Abbott Nutrition.

 *Please note any offer of employment for this position is conditional upon the successful completion of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening, conducted by a medical practitioner designated by the Company. 

 This is an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Project Engineer - Continuous Improvement on a 2 year fixed-term contract 

 We are looking for a motivated and ambitious Project Manager to further their career by joining a Global Leader in the Nutritional Manufacturing industry. 

 The primary purpose of this role is to lead and support continuous improvement initiatives across the Abbott Nutrition Cootehill site, while sharing best practices across the wider Abbott Nutrition Network. You will play an important role in helping to cultivate a culture of sustainable change through the creation and embedding of Lean methodology and the supporting framework, to deliver business transformation.  

 Responsibilities 
 •    Champion the use of Lean, Continuous Improvement and Six Sigma across the site. 
•    Use Lean Six Sigma, change management tools and methodologies to ensure project success, including Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping and DMAIC. 
•    Identify opportunities to optimise processes and ways of working to improve efficiency, quality and cost performance. 
•    Support delivery and financial reporting of the site Margin Improvement Program, and develop a sustainable year-on-year pipeline of improvement opportunities. 
•    Develop and execute Lean initiatives to drive productivity, standardisation and operational excellence across departments.
•    Support the identification and implementation of digital and data-driven solutions to improve operational performance and ways of working, including the use of tools such as Power BI and Power Apps where appropriate. 
•    Lead cross-functional improvement projects, engaging stakeholders at all levels and driving sustainable change across the organisation. 
•    Support departments in achieving key performance indicators through the application of Lean principles and continuous improvement practices. 
•    Assist with the site's Ideas to Action programme, promoting employee engagement, recognition and the sharing of best practices. 
•    Support the delivery of Lean capability training, including Root Cause Analysis, Kaizen, Lean Six Sigma, Value Stream Mapping and 6S Housekeeping Standards. 
•    Undertake other Operational Excellence and site improvement projects as required.

 Education Required 
 •    A 3rd level qualification in Technology, Business, Engineering or a related discipline or 5+ years relevant work experience in a high volume and dynamic production environment.
•    Lean Six Sigma Green Belt qualification, with knowledge of Lean Six Sigma tools such as DMAIC, Root Cause Analysis, 5S and Standard Work, is preferable.

 Knowledge/Skills 
 •    The post holder will have strong attention to detail, project management and planning skills.
•    Demonstrated ability to identify improvement opportunities and lead or support Continuous Improvement projects through to implementation and sustainable results, with a proactive and can-do approach.
•    Ability to build on the site's Behaviour-Based Continuous Improvement culture through engagement, data analysis, best practice identification and implementation.
•    Ability to effectively interact, influence and communicate across all levels.
•    Experience using data and digital tools to support continuous improvement activities. Knowledge of Power BI, Power Apps or similar tools would be advantageous.
 
 Connect with us at www.abbott.com and on LinkedIn , Facebook , Instagram , X and YouTube .

Job Details: 
 
 Job Description:  The Role and Impact 
As a Design Verification Engineering Intern, you will contribute to designing or verifying the functional logic of silicon designs to ensure they meet specifications and performance standards. In this role, you will support the development of internal logic design blocks, verification plans, test benches, and environments to achieve architectural coverage and uncover bugs. You will gain practical experience collaborating with architecture and design teams, applying technical skills, and exploring career opportunities in a dynamic and innovative environment. 

 Business Group 
The Central Engineering Group (CEG) drives Intel's innovation by delivering scalable solutions across diverse technology domains. This group supports Intel's silicon development and engineering operations, ensuring functional accuracy, efficiency, and optimization in design processes. Joining this team offers access to cutting-edge methodologies and collaboration opportunities that contribute to Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry. 

 Key Responsibilities 
 Assist in design and development of custom RTL Logic design blocks for IPU IPs.
 Assist in the development and execution of verification plans to ensure design specifications are met. 
 Support the creation and modification of test benches and verification environments to achieve required coverage. 
 Apply simulation and emulation techniques to analyze power, performance, and functionality. 
 Collaborate with architecture and design teams to identify and debug issues, and contribute to root cause analysis. 
 Participate in corrective measures and solutions for design challenges to ensure functional correctness. 
 Gain hands-on experience with tools and methodologies central to verification processes.
 
 
 Qualifications: The candidate must be currently doing a Level 8 or Level 9 college course in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or an equivalent course.

 Strong analytical & problem-solving skills. 
 Self-motivated with ability to work independently and manage stakeholders. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
 Demonstrated team dynamics / ability to work as part of a high performing team. 
 Ability to deal with ambiguity in defining activities and direction. 
 Good planning & organization skills. 
 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Practical experience or knowledge with hardware programming languages such as Verilog, System Verilog, VHDL. Scripting languages like Python.

 Take the first step in your career journey by joining Intel's Central Engineering Group, where you will gain hands-on experience, expand your technical knowledge, and contribute to groundbreaking designs that shape the future of technology.

Junior Legal Applications Engineer - ALG Solutions
As a Junior Legal Applications Engineer, you will join a well-established team who are delivering innovative legal solutions using legal technology and AI for the firm and its clients.
You will learn how technology is transforming legal service delivery and play a part in that journey. You will get hands-on experience working with diverse legal technology platforms, actively contribute to building and maintaining internal applications, and play an integral role in delivering legally focused, but technology-enabled projects.
Collaboration is at the heart of this position: you will work side by side with legal applications experts, lawyers, IT professionals, and external suppliers to help build solutions that make a real difference to how legal services are delivered by the firm.
This role provides training and mentorship from experienced team members and the opportunity to build skills in automation, workflow design, data analysis and low-code / no-code solution development. It is an excellent opportunity to begin a career in innovation and technology and join a team at the forefront of innovation in legal service delivery.
This is an entry‑level position designed for candidates who have recently completed a degree in Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, or a related analytical field and who are seeking to begin their career in legal technology.
This role reports to the Applications Development Manager.
Role and responsibilities
Appplication support and maintenance
Assist in the basic administration, configuration and routine maintenance of legal and AI technology applications.
Log issues, gather relevant information and support senior colleagues in resolving first‑level technical queries.
Carry out scheduled system checks, updates and maintenance activities under supervision.
Maintain accurate records of configuration changes, updates and support activity.
Escalate technical or operational issues appropriately to senior team members or suppliers.
Assist in creating reports and dashboards related to application usage and performance.
Technical development assistance
Contribute to the design and development of internal applications using a variety of technologies.
Support testing activities and assist senior colleagues in developing prototypes.
Stay informed about emerging trends in legal technology, learn from these, and share insights with the team.
Contribute to promoting the adoption of legal technology tools across the firm.
Legal workflow and process support
Support senior team members in developing legal workflows across all the firm’s practice areas.
Assist in mapping legal and business processes and identifying opportunities for improvement or automation.
Help prepare materials that explain how legal technology tools support legal service delivery.
Project support
Contribute to project activities including planning, development and delivery of technology‑led solutions.
Help gather project requirements and assist with implementing updates or enhancements.
Support go‑live activities by helping coordinate tasks and assisting in preparing documentation.
Help draft and update documentation including user guides and ‘how-to’ guides.
Prepare materials for presentations, demonstrations and training sessions.
Support stakeholder communication by drafting updates, summaries and progress notes for senior colleagues.
Skills, experience and characteristics required
Interested in the business operation of law firms, their legal service delivery processes and how technology can support the delivery of their services.
Knowledge of development concepts, automation tools, or collaboration platforms gained through university projects, internships, or outcome-oriented self-directed learning.
Strong ability to quickly learn how to use AI tools and other legal technology platforms and apply these in practice.
Very familiar with Microsoft Office (especially Excel) and ideally experience with using other Microsoft tools (Power Platform, Power BI etc.)
A keen interest in (and ideally practical experience of) leveraging technology to address real‑world challenges in the delivery of legal / professional service offerings.
Knowledgeable of at least one programming or scripting language (for example Python, JavaScript) and an ability to further develop programming / low-code / workflow skills.
Strong professional communication and presentation skills, and the ability to collaborate effectively, build relationships, and work with various stakeholders across the business.
Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritise effectively.
Strong self‑motivation with strong attention to detail and a positive, proactive approach to learning.
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment and enthusiastic about developing new skills.
Qualifications
Educated to degree level in Engineering, Physics, Economics or a related analytical field.
Academic, internship or project experience which demonstrates an interest in solution development, automation or data technologies.
What we offer
At A&L Goodbody ( ALG ) we pride ourselves on the high calibre of our employees. We place strong emphasis on career development and enabling our people to excel in their careers. Our work environment is friendly, professional and collaborative. In addition to working with a highly regarded team we offer:
A competitive remuneration package
Access to the firm’s marquee training and development programmes, delivered through the ALG School of Business and Law
Discretionary performance bonus
Pension and health insurance contributions, wellbeing contribution, life assurance, subsidised gym, restaurant and coffee shop.
Hybrid working policy
The Firm
ALG is a leading Irish law firm with five international offices in Dublin, Belfast, London, New York and San Francisco. ALG is a full-service, independent, corporate law firm with over 1,000 employees, and a client base spanning across the strong international and domestic business community in Ireland.
ALG has a reputation for leading the way in continuously developing its service to clients and internally to its business. This is delivered through the use of new processes, ways of working, innovative use of technology and marketing-leading business service teams.
Learn more about us  here  or see a sample of our recent  notable awards .
Accessibility
If you require any accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact us and we will work with you to ensure the best possible candidate experience.
We value a diverse and inclusive workforce and are an equal opportunities employer.

title: Internship - Finance
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Abbott Undergraduate Internship   Programme   
 

 Unlock Your Potential at Abbott   

 Looking for an opportunity to apply your academic knowledge, gain hands-on experience, and make a real impact? Abbott's Undergraduate Internship   Programme   offers students the chance to work on meaningful projects, collaborate with industry experts, and contribute to innovations that help people live healthier lives.   
 

 As an Abbott intern,   you'll   gain practical experience in a global healthcare   organisation , develop sought-after skills, and build a strong professional network. Whether your interests lie in Engineering, Science, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, IT, or other STEM disciplines,   you'll   be supported to learn, grow, and reach your potential.   
 

 Many of our interns go on to secure Graduate opportunities, Professional Development   Programme   positions, and long-term careers across Abbott's sites in Ireland and around the world.   
 

 What You Can Expect   

 As an Abbott intern,   you'll   gain hands-on experience while working on meaningful projects that contribute to healthcare innovation. Depending on your area of study and placement, you may support engineering, manufacturing, scientific, quality, supply chain, business, or technology initiatives that make a real impact.    
 

 What's   in it for you?   

 Apply your academic learning in a real-world environment.   

 
 Gain valuable hands-on experience with a global healthcare leader.   

 
 Contribute to   meaningful projects that help   people live healthier   lives.   

 
 Learn from experienced professionals and receive ongoing mentorship.   

 
 Develop technical, professional, and leadership capabilities.   

 
 Build your network across Abbott's Ireland operations.   

 
 Gain exposure to diverse functions, projects, and career paths.   

 
 Benefit from 6, 9, or 12-month internship opportunities aligned to your academic   programme .   

 
 Explore future opportunities through Abbott's Graduate   Programmes   and long-term career pathways.   

 

 Placement length and location will vary depending on business requirements and academic   programme   requirements.   

   

 About Abbott   

 Abbott is a global healthcare   leader   developing life-changing technologies that help people live healthier lives. With more than 122,000 colleagues serving people in over 160 countries, we deliver innovative solutions across diagnostics, medical devices, nutrition, and medicines.   

 In Ireland, Abbott employs more than 6,200 people across ten sites, providing interns with the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in world-class STEM and business environments while contributing to healthcare innovation.   
 

 Employment offers are subject to the successful completion of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening.   
 

 Why Choose Abbott?   

 At Abbott,   you'll   gain hands-on experience, work on meaningful projects, and develop skills that will support your future career.   You'll :   

 Contribute to healthcare innovations that improve lives.   

 
 Learn from experienced professionals and industry experts.   

 
 Build valuable skills and expand your professional network.   

 
 Gain exposure to opportunities across Abbott's Ireland network, with flexibility to be based at different Abbott locations.   

 
 Explore future career opportunities within Abbott.   

 

 Our internship   Programme   provides real-world experience, broad exposure, and   a strong foundation   for future career growth.   
 

 Area of Opportunity   

 Depending on business needs and your area of study, you may have the opportunity to gain experience in the following area: 
   

 Finance   

 Gaining exposure to financial planning, reporting, analysis, and process improvement activities while supporting business decisions that help drive Abbott's continued growth and success.   
 

 Specific assignments will be aligned to business requirements, site needs, and individual development opportunitie s   
 

 What You'll Bring   

 At Abbott,   we're   looking for students with   the curiosity , drive, and ambition to make a difference. Successful candidates will:   

 Be available for a 6, 9, or 12-month placement aligned with their academic   program me .   

 
 B e pursuing an undergraduate or postgraduate qualification in   Finance, Business, or   another   relevant STEM discipline. 

 
 Be on track to achieve, or have achieved, a minimum   2.1 degree   classificatio n.   

 
 Bring   strong communication , teamwork, and analytical skills.   

 
 Demonstrate initiative, curiosity, and   a desire   to learn.   

 
 Have   a passion for innovation, STEM, and healthcare.   

 
 Thrive in a collaborative environment and be willing to take ownership of their work.   

 

 Have flexibility to be based at any Abbott Ireland location, providing opportunities for broader exposure, diverse experiences, and professional growth.   

 
   

 Closing Date: 19 September 2026   

 Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing   basis   and interviews   will   take place before the closing date. As positions may be filled early, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid   missing out on   this opportunity.   
 

 Learn more about our health and wellness benefits, which provide the security to help   you and   your family live full lives:     Abbott in Ireland | Benefits   

 Connect with us at   www.abbott.com   and on ,   Facebook ,   Instagram ,   X   and   YouTube . LinkedIn ,   Facebook ,   Instagram ,   X   and   YouTube .   
 

 Join Abbott and Help Build the Workforce of Tomorrow   

 Become part of the next generation of innovators, engineers, scientists, and future leaders helping shape the future of healthcare.   

 #EarlyCareers #STEMCareers #LifeAtAbbott #FutureTalent

Job Description:
It’s never been a more exciting time to join Vistra.
At Vistra our purpose is progress. We believe that our clients have the power to change the world and to do great things for global progress, and we exist to remove the friction that comes from the complexity of global business – to help our clients achieve progress without friction.   But progress only happens when people come together and take action. And we’re absolutely committed to building a culture where our people can do just that.
We have an exciting opportunity for you to join our team as a UK Payroll Associate for our iiPay business, part of our award winning Global payroll division. Reporting to the Senior Manager, UK & European Payroll Operations,  this full-time, permanent position can be based in our UK, Hungary, Romania or Poland offices and offers local coverage, allowing you to make a significant impact on our payroll business and its growth.
All our roles can be performed remotely with occasional visits to the office as requested by your manager. Where we have office locations, our team members are welcome to work remotely, on a hybrid basis or fully office based as they wish.
Our highly motivated and engaged team members are at the heart of our success! This role requires owning and delivering the UK payrolls for a range of international clients. Working closely with a variety of clients to professionally deliver a quality UK payroll service.
Key responsibilities:
The successful candidate requires minimum 2 years of UK Payroll experience and the ability to demonstrate a proven track record in the following areas:
Payroll delivery and service level management
Delivering accurate and compliant UK payroll processing for a group of assigned clients and payrolls, co-ordinating the client’s requirements and managing the process.
Scheduling and time management
Managing and delivering client payrolls against the agreed schedule - communicating directly with clients to meet or exceed the client deadlines and expectations. Escalating issues within the client and iiPAY teams to meet and exceed agreed service level agreement.
Operational excellence
Individually and as a team member strive to improve the systems, processes and payroll delivery environment to maximise the efficiency and accuracy of our client contracts. iiPAY team members must be focused on maintaining a high customer satisfaction rating.
Communication
Managing and maintaining clear and informative communications to clients, implementation team and client account managers.
Country legislation knowledge
Take responsibility for being the primary operations contact point for the UK, developing and maintaining detailed knowledge of the statutory processes and legislative deadlines.
Working closely with the implementations team to take-on new payrolls and clients. Project delivery
Owning or contributing to specific company projects such as improving and/or changing systems, processes or functions within the business.
Escalation and problem resolution
Owning, managing and resolving client escalations, seeking help and advice where needed. Working with the payroll provider management team to enhance and develop the processes and outcomes for our partner network.
Attributes/Technical Skills:
Has worked in a multi-client payroll environment, managing a diverse range of payrolls and client relationships.
Proven track record of delivering UK payrolls whilst adhering to strict service level agreements. Competent with all UK complexities, including different terms and conditions and treatment of elements.
Experience of different pension schemes, salary sacrifice schemes and auto enrolment.
To be fully compliant with all UK legislation, statutory monthly and yearly requirements
Is experienced in working with international clients both small and large (FTSE & Fortune 500) and has the ability to communicate clearly and gain trust with your client contacts.
Is a highly motivated and driven professional, with excellent communication skills and a track record of delivering high levels of customer satisfaction.
Extremely organised and takes pride in standards of work.
Can demonstrate the ability to interact effectively with iiPay’s clients and be assertive
Has intermediate to high Excel skills and is capable of effectively and efficiently manipulating data within an Excel workbook.
Relevant experience:
Experience of working within a regulated (ISAE 3402 / SSAE 16) service delivery environment.
If you are excited about working with us, we encourage you to apply or have a confidential chat with one of our Talent Acquisition team members. Our goal is to make this a great place to work where all our people can thrive. We hope you join us on this exciting journey!

 Citi has had a presence in Ireland since 1965, it was one of the first foreign banks to open an office in the country and is the Citibank Europe Plc Headquarters.  

 Team/Role Overview 
 The Securities & Derivatives Settlements Analyst is an entry level position responsible for processing orders and transactions originating from trading desks and branch offices in coordination with the Operations - Transaction Services team. The overall objective of this role is to assist in the clearance, settlement and investigation of client securities and derivatives transactions.

 What you'll do

title: GCM Operations Analyst
description:
GCM Treasury Operations Analyst 
 Who we are: 
 American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance, life insurance, retirement solutions, and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide for retirement security.
 
 Get to know the business 
 Corporate function provides a wide range of services to the organization such as finance, internal audit, communications, security and human resources. Treasury sits within the Finance area. The Dublin Treasury Operations Centre consists of various multi-regional functions including Cash Management, GCM Operations, Global Bank Administration, Payment Operations and other areas including Global Risk & Compliance.
 
 About the role 
 What you need to know: 
 
 Responsible for daily activity on trade blotters for each product type covered by GCM traders.
 Monitoring trade matching confirmations, payment execution, settlement, failing trade management, and reconciliation of transactions
 Daily cash management of GCM accounts, including cash pool balances and currency rebalancing.
 The role will involve a combination of teamwork and close collaboration within a small team, as well as independent management of items
 Oversight review and reporting of reconciliation breaks related to GCM activity.
 Work with Kyriba Business Enablement team to ensure GCM payments, access profiles, configurations and reporting are fit for purpose.  
 Maintain good relationships with our transactional global banking partners, provide advisory support to other teams on GCM products and partner with Treasury Compliance team to ensure all activities and duties are carried out within the respective global standards and policies
 Ensure procedure documentation and Standard Operating Procedures are proactively maintained and kept up to date
 From time to time be flexible to support US Market hours but working to demonstrate how delivery can be maintained in standard business hours
 What we’re looking for: 
 
 Experience in a Treasury/Cash Management role and the trade life cycle of financial instruments
 Knowledge of FX, Derivative, Repo, Stock Repurchases and Margin settlement.
 Prior experience with Treasury Management systems and electronic banking systems, preferably Kyriba
 Proven ability to multi-task, and independently and effectively manage and prioritize a varied workload
 BA degree in Accounting, Finance or a Business-related field is preferred
 Must possess strong interpersonal skills (both verbal and written)
 Proficient in Microsoft office specifically Excel and Word and Powerpoint
 English fluency is required
 Strong analytical skills and be able to work independently and with a team
 Ability to investigate, troubleshoot and resolve items to completion and implement change to prevent reoccurrence
 Must be able to communicate information clearly and concisely to stakeholders as needed, in both written and verbal format
 Ensure all Treasury systems, GCM related Audit, SOX and ORM related activities and duties are carried out in line with Treasury’s Risk and Compliance requirements.
 
 
 A look at our benefits 
 At AIG, we have a 100-year legacy of working to make the world a better place. And that begins with our employees. We’re proud to offer a competitive salary along with annual performance related bonus and a range of employee benefits and resources that help you protect what matters most; a company funded health care scheme, a competitive holiday allowance with an additional two company days per year, automatic enrolment into a generous defined contribution pension scheme, smarter travel options such as bike to work and tax saver travel scheme, staff discounts and wellbeing initiatives. We provide a variety of leaves for personal, health, and family needs. We also offer volunteer days, for example, the “Giving Back” program allows you to take up to 16 hours a year to volunteer in your community.
 
 We also believe in fostering our employees’ development and offer a range of learning opportunities for employees to hone their professional skills to position themselves for the next steps of their careers. AIG also has a tuition reimbursement program for eligible employees to enhance their education, skills, and knowledge in areas that relate to their current position or future positions to which they may transfer or progress.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 We are an Equal Opportunity Employer 
 It has been and will continue to be the policy of American International Group, Inc., its subsidiaries and affiliates to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide equal opportunity to all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, age, gender, gender expression, national origin, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected categories. At AIG, we believe that diversity and inclusion are critical to our future and our mission – creating a foundation for a creative workplace that leads to innovation, growth, and profitability. Through a wide variety of programs and initiatives, we invest in each employee, seeking to ensure that our people are not only respected as individuals, but also truly valued for their unique perspectives.
 
 #LI-AIG
 
 At AIG, we value in-person collaboration as a vital part of our culture, which is why we ask our team members to be primarily in the office. This approach helps us work together effectively and create a supportive, connected environment for our team and clients alike. 
 
 Enjoy benefits that take care of what matters 
 At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what’s most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family.
 
 Reimagining insurance to make a bigger difference to the world 
 American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a global leader in commercial and personal insurance solutions; we are one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. It is an exciting time to join us — across our operations, we are thinking in new and innovative ways to deliver ever-better solutions to our customers. At AIG, you can go further to support individuals, businesses, and communities, helping them to manage risk, respond to times of uncertainty and discover new potential. We invest in our largest asset, our people, through continuous learning and development, in a culture that celebrates everyone for who they are and what they want to become.
 
 Welcome to a culture of inclusion 
 We’re committed to creating a culture that truly respects and celebrates each other’s talents, backgrounds, cultures, opinions and goals. We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging through learning, cultural awareness activities and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). With global chapters, ERGs are a cornerstone for our culture of inclusion. The talent of our people is one of AIG’s greatest assets, and we are honored that our drive for positive change has been recognized by numerous recent awards and accreditations.

title: Event Driven Research Analyst
description:
Overview 

 Susquehanna is a global quantitative trading firm powered by scientific rigor, curiosity, and innovation. Our culture is intellectually driven and highly collaborative, bringing together researchers, engineers, and traders to design and deploy impactful strategies in our systematic trading environment. To meet the unique challenges of global markets, Susquehanna applies machine learning and advanced quantitative research to vast datasets in order to uncover actionable insights and build effective strategies. By uniting deep market expertise with cutting-edge technology, we excel in solving complex problems and pushing boundaries together. 
  
 As an analyst on Susquehanna’s Research team, you will partner with our senior analysts and traders to identify investment opportunities in the equity or options market. Research analysts provide real-time opinions on breaking news and in-depth analysis of future events. You will be responsible for finding opportunities that other market participants may not be capitalising on, either by discovering new information or considering existing knowledge from a different perspective. Analysts are embedded in a strategy-focused trading desk and the analysis you provide will directly impact trading decisions. 
   
 At Susquehanna, we place a high value on education and development. You will experience this dedication to training as you work collaboratively with the research analysts and traders on your desk to gain hands-on exposure. You will also learn about options and the decision-making strategies that our traders employ. This role provides the unique opportunity to combine the quantitative aspects of finance with creative problem-solving in order to develop trade ideas in a fast-paced, proprietary trading environment. 
   
 What you’ll be doing 
 Evaluating and tracking special situations such as mergers, acquisitions, and other corporate actions 
 Identifying and analysing upcoming events 
 Providing real-time opinions on breaking news 
 Collaborating with traders on investment ideas 
 Traveling to company events and conferences as required 
 Performing stock valuation analysis 
 
 What we're looking for 

 Minimum of a bachelor's degree 
 Minimum 1 year Experience 
 CFA or part-qualified CFA Candidate preferred 
 Strong written, analytical, and financial research skills 
 Ability to prioritize and complete multiple tasks in a fast-paced, dynamic environment 
 Prior exposure to fundamental company research and event driven analysis an advantage 
 Familiarity with a trading environment and derivative products preferred 
 A self-starter, quick learner, effective communicator, and problem solver 
 Willingness to work additional and flexible hours when necessary

 Unlock Your Potential at Abbott

Company Description
ORIX Aviation is an aircraft leasing company established in 1991, currently with over 200 aircraft owned, managed, and committed on lease to more than 50 airlines across greater than 30 countries. ORIX Aviation is also a 30% shareholder in Avolon, one of the world’s largest aircraft lessors. ORIX Aviation has offices in Dublin and Dubai and works closely with a team of aviation specialists in ORIX Corporation in Tokyo. The team consists of 100+ aviation professionals across the three locations. ORIX Aviation is an S&P ranked aircraft servicer and has earned a “strong” ranking - the highest possible ranking - with a stable outlook. ORIX Aviation is positioned to grow both its owned book aircraft as well as managed aircraft in the coming years. ORIX Aviation believes in the power of diversity and is an equal opportunities employer.
Position
Lead the Powerplant function across engine maintenance strategy, shop visit oversight, cost validation, maintenance forecasting, technical risk management, and transaction support. The role is responsible for providing senior technical direction on engine-related matters, protecting asset value, and supporting commercial decisions across the aircraft and engine portfolio.
Lead the planning, coordination, and oversight of major engine maintenance events across the managed fleet.
Develop, review, and challenge engine shop visit workscopes, maintenance strategies, and operator or MRO recommendations.
Assess shop visit proposals to ensure technical necessity, lease alignment, cost control, and protection of asset value.
Review and validate shop visit costs, invoices, maintenance reserve claims, and related supporting documentation.
Maintain engine maintenance forecasts and exposure assumptions in coordination with airlines, MROs, OEMs, and internal stakeholders.
Provide senior technical input to aircraft and engine transitions, including due diligence, delivery readiness, redelivery planning, and execution risk management.
Support LOIs, lease agreements, lease amendments, lease placements, sales, and trading transactions, including review and validation of engine-related rates and assumptions.
Identify, assess, and communicate technical risks that may affect asset value, maintenance exposure, lease economics, transition execution, or transaction outcomes.
Develop and agree practical mitigation actions for engine maintenance, technical, commercial, and transition-related risks.
Act as a senior technical interface with Trading, Marketing, Pricing, Asset Management, Risk, Legal, and Technical teams.
Maintain market awareness through engagement with operators, OEMs, MROs, appraisers, and wider industry contacts.
Provide guidance and oversight to more junior Powerplant or technical team members on data, maintenance, records, and transaction-related matters.
Translate complex technical findings into clear, decision-ready recommendations for commercial, asset management, and senior leadership stakeholders.
Requirements
5-10 years of relevant powerplant, airline, MRO, OEM, leasing, or technical asset management experience preferred.
Relevant university degree or technical qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Aircraft Maintenance, or a related discipline.
Strong understanding of engine maintenance, shop visit management, lease-related maintenance obligations, and aircraft technical records.
Experience reviewing shop visit workscopes, invoices, reserve claims, engine rates, and maintenance exposure assumptions.
Strong commercial awareness with the ability to assess the impact of technical matters on asset value, lease economics, and transaction execution.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical matters clearly to senior internal stakeholders.
Advanced Microsoft Excel capability and confidence working with technical, utilisation, maintenance, and financial data.
Proactive, well-organised, detail-focused, and able to manage competing priorities across maintenance, transactions, and portfolio management.
Aircraft leasing experience desirable.
Other information
Working with ORIX Aviation
Outside of an attractive and competitive remuneration package, and based in a modern office block situated in a desirable location, other benefits of the ORIX Aviation culture include:
A flexible hybrid working model,
A Social Committee who arrange multiple social events; everything from meals out and pub quizzes to family fun days and social drinks
Participation in company sports teams such as tag rugby, tennis and football
Access to on-site gym and subsidised external gym and sport club memberships
Annual fundraising for charities and community organisations
Opportunity to get involved in ORIX Aviation’s committees which include Wellness, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion, ECO and Sports & Social
Secondment opportunities to Dubai
ORIX Aviation is an equal opportunities employer and accepts applications from people of all backgrounds and disciplines. ORIX Aviation supports inclusion in the workplace and will endeavor to provide reasonable accommodations as requested by candidates throughout the interview process. We encourage applicants with additional accommodation requirements to contact us at [email protected] .

 Analyse complex processes and problems and identify areas of improvement and risk.

Kepak Technical Industrial Placement Programme 2027 - Ireland Role Purpose 
 The Technical Industrial Placement programme is designed to give university students unparalleled insight, training and support around Health, Safety and Environment in a fast-faced food production environment. We are looking for passionate and driven individuals to join the team on our Technical Placement.
 
 These are some of the Key Responsibilities from our Technical Graduate programme, our Placement students will be getting exposure to similar things, just not all to the same depth as the Graduates. 
 Kepak Health & Safety Industrial Placement Programme 2027 
 We are seeking to recruit for the Industrial Placement Programme.
 Duration: Flexible depending on the course you are undertaking. 
 The Programme: 
 Our Health & Safety (H&S) and Environment placement programme is to help us to develop our H&S leaders of the future, and allows dynamic, motivated, hardworking, and passionate Graduates an opportunity to start their career with one of Ireland & UKs leading meat businesses. 
 You can expect: 
 To be fully immersed into our Culture from day 1, working alongside key industry experts and Kepak leaders
 Gain an in depth understanding of our brands and products, and our relationships with customers and consumers, and how they underpin our financial performance
 To learn key aspects of our business, whilst you develop your skills and knowledge
 The opportunity to develop personally and professionally through exposure to key projects, tasks and development activities that challenge you, all supported by a detailed learner journey and training plan
 A dedicated mentor and development program to support you both on the programme and into a role that best fits your skills
 Kepak is one of Europe’s leading food companies operating 12 manufacturing sites across
 Ireland and the UK with sales offices in Europe, US and Asia. The group has a turnover of €1.5bn and employs over 4,500 people. Our company purpose “ Meat at our heart, innovation our driver and nutrition our future ” is underpinned by our values of “ Responsibility, Ambition, Passion for Food and Teamwork” .
 ROLE PURPOSE: 
 Reporting to the Site health and Safety Manager, the H&S Placement role will be responsible for the development and implementation of Health and Safety management systems within the Site and for ensuring that advice and support is available for all business Unit Managers in order for them to fulfil their own responsibilities.
 Liaising closely with Group H&S support services to ensure site management system is aligned with Group safety strategy.

 Policies and Procedures

 Enforce policy by identifying breaches and reporting to the Site Manager and the Group Health and Safety Manager

title: Silicon Architecture Undergraduate Intern
description:
Job Details: 
 
 Job Description:  The Role and Impact 
As a Silicon Architecture Undergraduate Intern, you will play a vital role in supporting the design and optimization of cutting-edge silicon architectures. Working closely with experienced engineers, you will contribute to modeling, analyzing, and validating architectural features to ensure their performance and efficiency for Intel's advanced technologies. This hands-on opportunity allows you to make meaningful contributions to real-world projects while building a strong foundation for your career in silicon engineering. 

 Business group 
The Central Engineering Group (CEG) is Intel's innovation hub, dedicated to driving excellence in silicon design and development across Intel's product portfolio. The group focuses on delivering high-performance, efficient architectures that power next-generation technologies. By joining CEG, you will collaborate with a team of experts to support Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry and enable impactful advancements in computing and connectivity. 

 Key Responsibilities 
- Assist in the development, modeling, and simulation of silicon architecture features to evaluate their functionality and performance. 
- Perform analysis of architectural designs and provide insights to optimize efficiency, scalability, and power consumption. 
- Collaborate with engineers to validate architectural components and ensure alignment with system-level requirements. 
- Contribute to the creation of technical documentation and reports summarizing findings and recommendations. 
- Participate in team meetings and brainstorming sessions to support innovative solutions for complex engineering challenges.
 
 
 Qualifications: The candidate must be currently doing a Level 8 or Level 9 college course in Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Computer Science or an equivalent course.
  
   You must also be available for six to eight months in 2027 with a preferred starting date between January and June.     
  
 Required competencies 
- Familiarity in programming languages such as Python, C, C++, or similar, and familiarity with simulation tools. 

 Preferred Qualifications 
 - Understanding of computer architecture fundamentals or networking systems, including performance and evaluation techniques. 
- Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and communicate technical ideas effectively.

Diversity - Innovation - Caring - Global Collaboration - Winning Spirit - High Performance
At Boston Scientific, we’ll give you the opportunity to harness all that’s within you by working in teams of diverse and high-performing employees, tackling some of the most important health industry challenges. With access to the latest tools, information and training, we’ll help you in advancing your skills and career. Here, you’ll be supported in progressing – whatever your ambitions.
Advancing possibilities for a brighter tomorrow
Boston Scientific is seeking a highly motivated Graduate Supply Chain Analyst   on a defined-term (23months) basis to join our Clonmel team .
Job Purpose:
Start your career where your ideas, curiosity and supply chain skills can make a meaningful difference. As a Supply Chain Graduate at Boston Scientific, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues, contribute towards our Delivering Excellence strategy and build hands-on experience in a collaborative environment.
As a  Supply Chain Graduate at Boston Scientific, you will support the Supply Chain department in the day-to-day coordination and execution of supply chain activities. Provide operational and administrative support across systems and processes, assist with report creation and data analysis based on business requirements, and help maintain accurate and efficient supply chain operations. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support process improvements, resolve operational issues, and contribute to departmental and business objectives
This is an opportunity to apply what you learned during your studies, develop your technical and problem-solving capabilities and gain valuable experience while contributing to improve patients' lives.
Key Responsibilities
Provide operational and administrative support to the Supply Chain function across planning, purchasing, inventory, logistics and related activities.
Assist with the preparation, analysis and maintenance of supply chain reports, KPIs and dashboards to support business requirements and decision-making.
Support supply chain digitalisation initiatives, including the development and implementation of digital tools, automated reporting and data-driven solutions to improve efficiency and visibility.
Analyse supply chain data to identify trends, exceptions and opportunities for improvement, escalating issues and supporting appropriate corrective actions.
Support inventory management and material planning activities to help maintain product availability and optimise inventory levels.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Planning, Procurement, Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering and Logistics to support day-to-day operational requirements.
Participate in new product introductions, product transfers and technology transfer activities, supporting supply chain requirements and gaining exposure to end-to-end processes.
Support the maintenance and continuous improvement of supply chain systems, master data, standard operating procedures and process documentation.
Ensure activities are completed in accordance with applicable quality, regulatory, environmental and company requirements.
Participate in supply chain projects and cross-functional initiatives aligned with departmental and site objectives.
Develop knowledge of end-to-end supply chain processes, systems and best practices through practical experience, training and collaboration with experienced team members.
Education & Experience:
Hons Bachelor Degree (Level 8) in supply chain, business, procurement or related discipline is essential.
Graduated within the past two years or currently in the final year of university.
Relevant work experience or completion of a co-op program, ideally with AI and machine learning coursework.
Eligibility to work in Ireland.
Strong communication and teamwork skills, with the initiative to contribute in a collaborative environment.
Strong systems aptitude and an interest in developing digital solutions.
Enthusiastic, proactive approach to learning and problem-solving.
Interest in medical technology, manufacturing, product development or continuous improvement.
Strong analytics, data science and statistical skills.
Boston Scientific Ireland Graduate Programme cosing date is 22nd November 2026.
As a leader in medical science for more than 40 years, we are committed to solving the challenges that matter most – united by a deep caring for human life. Our mission to advance science for life is about transforming lives through innovative medical solutions that improve patient lives, create value for our customers, and support our employees and the communities in which we operate. Now more than ever, we have a responsibility to apply those values to everything we do – as a global business and as a global corporate citizen.
So, choosing a career with Boston Scientific isn’t just business, it’s personal. And if you’re a natural problem-solver with the imagination, determination, and spirit to make a meaningful difference to people worldwide, we encourage you to apply and look forward to connecting with you!

As a Business Customer Service Representative within the MD&A Service Desk, you'll be part of the EE Onsite Team, a key managed service offering within the BT Business Mobile portfolio. In this customer-facing role, you'll work closely with customers to provide high-quality support and mobile service management, ensuring their mobile environments remain efficient, compliant and optimised. Acting as a trusted partner, you'll help resolve queries, manage mobile assets and deliver services in line with agreed customer requirements and service standards.
You'll combine strong customer service skills with technical knowledge to build effective relationships, solve problems and deliver a great customer experience. The role offers the opportunity to work independently within customer environments while collaborating with internal BT teams to ensure successful service delivery.
Occasional UK travel may be required for training purposes or to visit customer sites to support account configuration activities and service delivery requirements.
What you'll be doing
Delivering a high-quality mobile fleet management service from our customers Basingstoke office, supporting one of our  corporate mobile contracts.
Acting as a key point of contact for customers, building strong relationships and providing an excellent service experience.
Collaborating with BT, EE and customer stakeholders to ensure seamless service delivery and successful outcomes.
Managing a range of provisioning, service request and incident management activities across customer and BT systems.
Resolving customer queries efficiently while ensuring services are delivered in line with agreed contractual and compliance requirements.
Taking ownership of your workload, working proactively and independently to put customers at the heart of everything you do.
Essential skills/experience
Experience delivering excellent customer service in a customer-facing environment, with the ability to build strong relationships and manage stakeholders effectively.
Strong problem-solving skills, with experience handling provisioning, incidents or service requests while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
Ability to work independently, use initiative and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment with a customer-first mindset.
Desirable skills/experience

Holiday purchase scheme

With execution momentum building and a clear path to growth, the opportunity now is to scale what works, accelerate performance and fully realise our potential. This is about delivering against ambitious financial outcomes while transforming how we operate – creating a business that is simpler, faster, more innovative and easier to do business with.
If you want to be part of the team shaping the turnaround of a multi-billion-pound business – and building a stronger, more competitive BT for the future – this is your moment.

description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: About Abbott 
 Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

 Abbott in Ireland 
 Abbott has maintained a strong presence in Ireland since 1946 and celebrates its 80th anniversary in the country in 2026. The company supports the Irish healthcare sector with a broad portfolio spanning diagnostics, diabetes care, medical devices and nutritional products. Today, Abbott employs more than 6,200 people across ten sites located in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford and Sligo.

 Abbott Rapid Diagnostics is part of Abbott’s Diagnostics family of businesses, bringing together exceptional teams of experts and industry-leading technologies to support diagnostic testing which provides important information for the treatment and management of diseases and other conditions. IDEM is an over a billion-dollar business unit that now support significate growth for Abbott in COVID-19 related products in over 70+ countries.

 Main Purpose of the Role 
 The Regional Financial Analyst will be responsible for financial analysis, forecasting, and insights to influence strategic decision-making and support organizational objectives for the Informatics organization within RMDx. Prepares financial plans and forecasts based on performance expectations. Recommend alternative courses of action, influence pricing strategy, and partner with sales and commercial excellence teams to achieve financial goals.

 Main Responsibilities 
Responsible for the review and analysis of assigned projects that may include:

 • Financial statements analysis for business unit and international markets
 • Preparation, review and analysis of requests for capital expenditures and Purchase Orders
 • Evaluate new business opportunities, potential new markets, new products, and spending initiatives by modeling alternative financial scenarios (e.g. revenues, profitability etc).
 • Gross Margin/COGS Analysis
 • Profit plan preparation
 • Long-range planning analysis
 • Balance Sheet Reconciliations/Cash Flow Analysis
 • Review and analysis of profitability
 • Journal Entry Preparation
 • Pricing analysis
 • Applies educational and advanced knowledge of accounting and financial principles and requirements to support business needs.
 • Maintain controls to ensure integrity of assets and compliance with applicable policies, procedures, guidelines and internal controls.
 • Projects can be varied and complex; may refer to established precedents to develop solutions; use of innovative thinking is required. Plans/leads projects and analyzes results to present recommendations to leadership.
 • Works under minimal supervision. Independently determines and develops approach to solutions. Work is reviewed upon completion for adequacy in meeting objectives.

 Education and Experience 
 • BSc in a related discipline, such as Accounting, Finance or related field
 • Minimum of 4 years' experience in accounting or financial planning and analysis within a manufacturing, operations, medical device, pharmaceutical or healthcare environment.
 • Strong organisational, communication, and problem-solving skills. 
 • A collaborative mindset and commitment to continuous improvement

 Why Abbott? 
 At Abbott, you'll have the opportunity to work on meaningful projects that help shape the future of healthcare while developing your skills in a global, innovative organisation. Join a team that values collaboration, diversity, growth, and making a lasting impact on people's lives around the world.

 Learn more about our health and wellness benefits, which provide the security to help you and your family live full lives:  Abbott in Ireland | Benefits

description:
At Forvis Mazars, we’re not just one of the leading professional services firms in Ireland — we’re a launchpad for ambitious graduates ready to make an impact. With over 1,000 professionals across Dublin, Cork, Galway, and Limerick, and a global network spanning 100+ countries, we offer the scale, support, and opportunities to help you thrive.   
   
 Why join us?  
  
 Our next-generation graduate programme is built around you. We understand that no two people are the same, so we tailor your training, mentoring, and career development to match your strengths, interests, and goals.  
  
 Here, you’ll be more than just a number. You’ll be empowered to lead, innovate, and grow — personally and professionally. If you're looking for a career where your voice matters and your work makes a difference, this is the place for you. 
 
 The position  
  
 As a consulting associate, you will work with a range of interesting clients primarily in the public and financial services sectors, whilst undergoing professional training and rotating across a number of our consulting service areas such as strategy, organisation development, change and transformation, culture, people consulting, finance decision support, financial services regulatory consulting, privacy and sustainability (ESG). 
  
 Every day is different for a consultant. You will be assisting a wide variety of clients with their business’s challenges and developing tailored pragmatic solutions. Service rotations will help you to identify areas most suited to your abilities and we will support you with dedicated mentoring, coaching, technical upskilling and professional development so that you are set up for success.
We’re looking for bright, motivated individuals from a wide range of backgrounds—whether  that’s engineering, business, law, science, or a related field. What matters most is your eagerness to learn, collaborate, and apply your skills effectively. We’ll equip you with the technical and business know-how you need—but your energy, curiosity, and attitude are what will set you apart.  
   
 What we’re looking for   
 You’re working towards or have recently completed an honours degree in any discipline.  

 You act with integrity and always strive to do the right thing.  

 You’re a strong communicator who enjoys meeting people and exploring new ideas.  

 You value respect, inclusivity, and supporting those around you.  

 You thrive in team environments and enjoy working with others.  

 You’re organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage your time effectively.  

 You’re comfortable with technology and have solid computer skills.  

 You think critically and enjoy solving problems with logic and creativity.  

 You have excellent organisational skills, computer literacy and attention to detail

At Forvis Mazars, we’re not just one of the leading professional services firms in Ireland — we’re a launchpad for ambitious graduates ready to make an impact. With over 1,000 professionals across Dublin, Cork, Galway, and Limerick, and a global network spanning 100+ countries, we offer the scale, support, and opportunities to help you thrive.    
   
 Why join us?   
   
 Our next-generation graduate programme is built around you. We understand that no two people are the same, so we tailor your training, mentoring, and career development to match your strengths, interests, and goals.   
   
 Here, you’ll be more than just a number. You’ll be empowered to lead, innovate, and grow — personally and professionally. If you're looking for a career where your voice matters and your work makes a difference, this is the place for you.
Supported by our corporate secretarial management team, you will: 
 Take ownership of a portfolio of clients and being responsible for ensuring that clients are meeting their statutory obligations by 

 Maintaining company secretarial records to include updating minute books and statutory registers  

 Keeping up to date with annual return filings, and producing documentation in respect of the annual approval and circulation of financial statements and other minutes, as required 

 Preparing and filing statutory forms at the Companies Registration Office 

 Deal with queries and requests from clients, auditors, solicitors and internal staff 

 Assist clients to set up Irish entities through completion of company formations and branch registrations 

 Ensure the company secretarial database is up to date at all times 

 Take on responsibility for billing clients and for debtors’ collection 

 Stay on top of filing, archiving and general administrative duties 

 You will also have the opportunity to get involved in regular departmental training sessions to assist in your development and progression as a corporate governance professional.  
   
   About you   
   
 We’re looking for bright, motivated individuals from a wide range of backgrounds—whether that’s engineering, business, law, science, or a related field. What matters most is your eagerness to learn, collaborate, and apply your skills effectively. We’ll equip you with the technical and business know-how you need—but your energy, curiosity, and attitude are what will set you apart.  
   
 What we’re looking for   
 You’re working towards or have recently completed an honours degree in any discipline.  

 You act with integrity and always strive to do the right thing.  

 You’re a strong communicator who enjoys meeting people and exploring new ideas.  

 You value respect, inclusivity, and supporting those around you.  

 You thrive in team environments and enjoy working with others.  

 You’re organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage your time effectively.  

 You’re comfortable with technology and have solid computer skills.  

 You think critically and enjoy solving problems with logic and creativity.  

 You have excellent organisational skills, computer literacy and attention to detail

title: Science/Engineering Graduate - Dundalk
description:
Job Description
 
 Job Title: Graduate Program - Dundalk
 
 Location: Dundalk Co. Louth, Ireland
 
 
 Duration: 3 Years
 
 
 Program Overview: The Dundalk Graduate Program is a comprehensive 3-year rotational program designed to provide recent graduates with hands-on experience in various departments in a cutting-edge biotechnology manufacturing facility. Participants will have the opportunity to work on real-world projects, collaborate with industry experts, and develop the skills necessary to excel in their careers.
 
 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 
 Over the course of the three-year programme, you will bring energy, knowledge, innovation and leadership to carry out the following:
 Operate as part of the Engineering, Operations and MS&T teams, on a yearly-rotation basis, supporting the daily and long-term goals of the teams.
 Participate in troubleshooting meetings and root cause analysis workshops in support of manufacturing activities.
 Compile data and trends on batch performance (yield & cadence) and adherence to critical product quality measurements.
 Author technical memos, quality notifications and strategies for manufacturing investigations and improvements.
 Develop and deliver CAPA’s from associated quality management systems.
 Writing/revising/ rolling out accurate operational procedures, training materials and maintenance procedures for various Quality systems; ensure all work is carried out in line with same.
 Peer review documentation, ensuring Right First Time KPIs are achieved.
 Participate in daily team meetings and ensure effective communication of testing progress, deviations etc.
 Ensure that all Quality Systems within the department are adhered to on a daily basis.
 Complete all documentation in compliance with GMP and GxP standards.
 Provide support with audit/inspection requirements to ensure department compliance/readiness.
 Collaborating with others by sharing your skill-set and expertise
 Drive continuous improvement, perform root cause analysis on system failures e.g. FMEA, Fishbone diagrams, 5 why's etc.
 Drive compliance with Global Policies, Procedures and Guidelines, regulatory requirements and execute current Good manufacturing Practices (cGMP) in the performance of day-to-day activities and all applicable job functions, including maintenance of accurate records.
 Lead and support projects aimed at improving processes at our site in Dundalk.
 Be an active participant in the sites culture workstreams.
 
 This programme will be completed fully on site (Dundalk, Co. Louth) 
 
 The ideal person will have: 
 Working towards an Engineering or Science 2:1 qualification or relevant discipline
 
 So, if you are ready to: 
 
 Invent solutions to meet unmet healthcare needs, Impact the future by driving one of the world’s leading healthcare companies, and inspire your team to reach their full potential and push the boundaries of science and technology, please apply today. 
 
 
 
 PQ20 
 
 Required Skills: 
Chemical Engineering, Data Analysis, Engineering Design, Engineering Standards, Estimation and Planning, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Equipment, Manufacturing Scale-Up, Problem Solving, Process Improvements, Professional Engineering, Project Management, Self Motivation, Teamwork, Technical Writing

title: Program Management Intern, Summer 2027 – Dublin, Ireland
description:
Our Purpose 
 
 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 
 
 Title and Summary 
 
Program Management Intern, Summer 2027 – Dublin, Ireland 
Why join Mastercard’s internship program? 

Mastercard's internship program offers more than hands-on work. It provides an opportunity to build skills, expand your network, and make a meaningful impact while working on projects that support business priorities. It provides an opportunity to build skills, expand your network, and make a meaningful impact while working on projects that support business priorities. 

We are hiring for two Program Management Intern openings, each supporting a different technology team. Please indicate clearly on your CV or cover letter which opportunity they are most interested in.

Technical Program Management:

Team profile

The Build Factory & Modernization team supports global data-centre and product deployments. The team coordinates technical delivery across engineering and partner teams, ensuring that dependencies are managed, progress is visible and the required components are ready for launch.

Role description

As a Technical Program Management Intern, you will support the planning, execution and delivery of a technical workstream from inception through completion. You will work across teams to coordinate engineering delivery, monitor dependencies and help address gaps or blockers that could affect successful delivery.

Your responsibilities may include:

Supporting the development and maintenance of integrated project schedules
Tracking data-centre deployments, product integrations, scope, timing and delivery
Coordinating work and dependencies across engineering and partner teams
Monitoring delivery progress and providing clear, data-supported updates
Identifying gaps, dependencies and blockers that may affect delivery
Supporting project delivery within established frameworks and processes
Reviewing metrics and identifying improved ways to provide program visibility
Developing knowledge in areas such as software engineering, data centres, security or operations
Turning complex or unstructured information into clear communications and instructions
Requirements

Requirements:

Availability: Must be available between 21st June until 27th August 2027
Undergraduate or master’s student with an expected graduation date between Dec 2027-July 2028

Currently studying:

Project Management or Program Management, Systems Analysis, Computing or Computer Science, Engineering or another relevant technical discipline

You should also have:

An interest in infrastructure, data-centre projects or new software-product deployments
An interest in supporting projects involving multiple stakeholders in a global organization
Strong technical aptitude and problem-solving skills
The ability to communicate complex infrastructure or technical information to non-technical and senior stakeholders
Clear and confident written and verbal communication skills
Curiosity and a willingness to build expertise in a technical domain
Availability to work onsite in the Dublin Tech Hub office at least three days per week

Program Management: 

Team profile

The Technology Regulatory Execution team supports the coordinated delivery of Mastercard’s technology regulatory obligations. The team works across functions to align priorities, dependencies and outcomes, while supporting effective governance, reporting and execution.

Role description

As a Program Management Intern, you will support program managers with the planning, execution and monitoring of strategic initiatives and projects. You will work with stakeholders across the organization to coordinate activities, track progress and help ensure that key deliverables are completed on time.

Your responsibilities may include:

Maintaining project schedules, milestones, action items and deliverables
Supporting leadership updates, presentations, dashboards and management reporting
Coordinating meetings, documenting decisions and following up on agreed actions
Monitoring program risks, issues and dependencies
Analyzing project and program data to identify actionable insights
Maintaining accurate documentation and governance records
Supporting process improvements that strengthen program efficiency and consistency
Learning how technology initiatives contribute to broader business and organizational priorities

Requirements

Availability: Must be available between 21st June until 27th August 2027
Undergraduate or master’s student with an expected graduation date between Dec 2027-July 2028

Currently studying: Project Management, Program Management, Business or a related discipline, with a demonstrated interest in technology, Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics, commonly referred to as 
Systems Analysis, Computing or Computer Science

You should also have:

An interest in supporting projects involving multiple stakeholders in a global organization
An interest in technology and how technology programs support business and regulatory objectives
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
The ability to understand technical topics and communicate them clearly to non-technical or senior stakeholders
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively with different teams
Availability to work onsite in the Dublin Tech Hub office at least three days per week 
 
 Corporate Security Responsibility 
 
All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
 Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

 Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

 Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

 Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.
