title: Procurement Project Specialist &#8211; Hybrid
description:
Procurement Project Specialist – (€280/Daily)

  • Long Term Day Rate Contract with high likelihood of extension
  • Hybrid working – 2-days on-site
  • Join a major €30M infrastructure project connecting Ireland like never before
  • Join at mobilisation and shape the supply chain from day one

The next chapter of Ireland’s connectivity is being built now.

A major new project is underway to connect some of Ireland’s biggest cities and regions through a resilient national fibre network — creating the infrastructure to support the country’s growing demand for connectivity.

Making that happen is no small undertaking. It’s a complex, multi-party infrastructure build bringing together engineering, third-party infrastructure, civils, fibre deployment and specialist suppliers.

And this is where you come in.

Joining at mobilisation, you’ll help build the supply chain that makes the project possible — finding the right suppliers, running tenders, negotiating the right deals and putting the commercial arrangements in place to keep the project moving.

Your decisions will have a direct impact on what gets delivered, who delivers it and how successfully the project moves from plan to reality. You’ll work closely with Project Managers, Engineering and Commercial teams, with the opportunity to shape procurement from the ground up rather than inherit an established process.

 

Why You’ll Love This Role

  • Work on a National Project: Help build a fibre network connecting some of Ireland’s biggest cities and regions.
  • Shape It from the Start: Join during mobilisation and build the procurement approach from the ground up.
  • Work Across the Project: Source across multiple workstreams, from infrastructure and civils to fibre deployment and specialist suppliers.
  • Own Key Supplier Decisions: Help select the suppliers and agree the commercial terms that will support delivery.
  • Work Closely with Delivery Teams: Partner directly with Project Managers, Engineering and Commercial teams to make sure procurement keeps pace with the project.

What You’ll Do

  • Set the Plan: Identify what needs to be sourced and when.
  • Run Tenders: Manage RFQs and RFPs from scope through to supplier selection.
  • Secure the Deal: Benchmark prices, negotiate terms and manage commercial risk.
  • Build the Supply Base: Find and develop the suppliers and subcontractors needed for delivery.
  • Keep Procurement Moving: Work with project teams to manage requirements, priorities and supplier dependencies.
  • Set Up Delivery: Put the right suppliers and agreements in place for the next stage of the project.

What You’ll Have

  • Procurement Experience: Strong experience at Procurement Specialist, Senior Procurement Specialist, Procurement Manager or similar level. Your current or most recent role should be procurement-focused.
  • Tendering & Negotiation: Experience managing sourcing projects from initial requirement through tender, negotiation and award.
  • Project & Stakeholder Experience: Comfortable working with suppliers, project teams and senior stakeholders in a fast-moving project environment.
  • Relevant Sector Experience: Infrastructure, utilities, construction, engineering or telecommunications would be beneficial. CIPS would be an advantage, but strong procurement experience is the priority.

 

For more information, contact kendra.greasley@archer.ie
For additional opportunities, visit the Archer Recruitment website.

title: Protect yourself from recruitment scams
description:

Protect yourself from recruitment scams
We are seeing an increase in fraudulent activity involving individuals falsely claiming to represent Bank of America. These scams often include fake job offers, interviews, or requests for financial or personal information. We take these matters seriously and want to ensure you stay informed and protected throughout your job search.
Please keep the following in mind:
Bank of America will never ask for payment or request personal banking information at any stage of the recruitment /career process.
All official recruitment communications will come from a verified Bank of America email address ending in @bofa.com. Be cautious of messages from personal or non-company email addresses.
Do not engage with or respond to suspicious emails or messages. If you're unsure about the legitimacy of a communication, verify the sender’s email address and contact us directly. Hover over the sender’s email address and confirm it ends with @bofa.com—be alert for misspellings or added words.
If you receive a suspicious email, text, or phone call using Bank of America's name, please forward it to the Abuse mailbox .
Interviews
Bank of America does not utilize video chat rooms (e.g., Google Hangouts) to conduct interviews.
Bank of America will only use our approved interview platforms, HireVue, Teams, Webex or Zoom.
Your vigilance helps protect you and supports the integrity of our hiring process.
Recognizing fraudulent communications
Phishing emails often: Do not address you by name.
Create a sense of urgency to prompt quick action.
Contain links that lead to suspicious websites or malicious attachments.
Include grammatical or spelling errors.
Stay informed

description:
Line of Service 
Assurance 
 Industry/Sector 
Not Applicable 
 Specialism 
Assurance 
 Management Level 
Manager 
 Job Description & Summary 
Our FS Risk & Regulation team works with banks and other regulated financial institutions on the financial (prudential) risk issues that affect how they manage capital, liquidity, regulatory reporting, stress testing, recovery and resolution.

This role is for someone with strong banking prudential risk expertise who wants to use that knowledge in varied, client-facing work, rather than in a purely internal control, policy or reporting role. You will work across a small number of client projects at any one time, using your technical knowledge to understand the issue, analyse the facts, develop clear outputs and help clients progress practical actions.

The work is varied and technical. One project may involve reviewing a bank’s regulatory reporting process, another may involve assessing liquidity risk governance or economic capital modelling, and another may require interpreting new prudential requirements and setting out what needs to change. You will need to be organised, comfortable with competing priorities, able to manage multiple deliverables and able to maintain quality across different topics and deadlines. 
 
 About the Role: 
 Work on concurrent client projects or workstreams, often covering different prudential risk topics, with responsibility for organising your work, tracking actions and delivering agreed outputs. Your focus will be on the execution and delivery of the projects.
 Review client information such as policies, procedures, governance packs, regulatory returns, risk reports, committee materials, models, calculations and management information to understand how the current approach works.
 Use your financial (prudential) risk knowledge to identify issues, gaps, inconsistencies or areas where the client’s approach may not meet regulatory requirements, supervisory expectations or good practice.
 Analyse numerical information, including capital, liquidity, stress testing, regulatory reporting and balance sheet data, and explain what the figures show, what assumptions have been used and where further challenge may be needed.
 Prepare clear deliverables such as findings papers, gap analyses, impact assessments, remediation plans, framework documents, process maps, management reports and materials for senior stakeholders.
 Attend meetings and working sessions with client teams across Risk, Finance, Treasury, Regulatory Reporting and senior management to gather information, test understanding, discuss findings and agree next steps.
 Keep project teams informed on progress, risks and dependencies, and escalate where timelines, scope, data availability or competing priorities need to be managed.
 Review the work of junior team members, provide clear feedback and help them build technical knowledge, structured analysis and excellent delivery discipline.
 Contribute to internal technical materials, market updates, proposals and points of view on emerging prudential risk topics.
 
 
 
 
 Who we are looking for: 
 
 You may have specialist knowledge in any one of the areas below, with a desire and willingness to learn the others:
 At least 4+ years of experience working in a related area such as capital management, liquidity, risk or liquidity management, regulatory reporting, recovery and resolution, stress testing and credit risk.
 Capital management: capital planning, capital adequacy, balance sheet management and optimisation. Understanding of the CRR and RWA calculations.  
 Credit risk: credit risk frameworks, credit risk appetite, portfolio monitoring, credit risk data and MI, impairment and provisioning approaches, credit risk model outputs, and the use of credit risk parameters such as PD, LGD and EAD in regulatory capital, stress testing and management reporting.
 Liquidity management: LCR, NSFR, ILAAP, contingency funding planning, intraday liquidity, liquidity governance and risk appetite. Knowledge of the LCR Delegated Act and the CRR.
 Stress testing: internal and regulatory stress testing (supporting the ICAAP, ILAAP, and recovery plan), liquidity stress testing, scenario design, modelling methodologies, assumptions, governance, documentation, and use of results.
 Recovery and resolution: recovery planning, wind-down planning, resolution planning, resolvability assessments, dry runs, and related regulatory submissions.
 Regulatory reporting: COREP, LCR/NSFR, ALMM, STE, resolution reporting, data quality, governance and control frameworks.
 Numerical and analytical capability: ability to read, interpret and challenge data, calculations, assumptions, modelling and outputs, and management information. Quantitative skills or experience with modelling approaches would be a plus.
 Business Acumen - use a broad range of tools and techniques to extract insights from current trends in the market and utilise this information to assist your clients in making innovative business decisions.
 Relationship management - ability to read situations and modify behaviour to build quality, diverse relationships.
 Creative - demonstrate an ability to contribute to new ideas and propose innovative solutions to problems. 
 Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.
 Enthusiastic team player and manager with a passion to coach and encourage others to achieve their potential.
 Leadership – demonstrate strong commitment and experience to developing yourself, your team members, your clients and your business.

title: Legal Counsel - Infrastructure & Projects
description:
Join us, be part of more.   
   
 We’re so much more than an energy company. We’re a family of brands revolutionising how we power the planet. We're energisers. One team of 21,000 colleagues that's energising a greener, fairer future by creating an energy system that doesn’t rely on fossil fuels whilst living our powerful commitment to igniting positive change in our communities. Here, you can find more purpose, more passion, and more potential. That’s why working here is #MoreThanACareer. We do energy differently - we do it all. We make it, store it, move it, sell it, and mend it.   
   
 About your team:   
   
 We’re the pride of Ireland. Bord Gáis Energy have been powering the nation’s homes and businesses for almost 40 years. But now, we’re so much more than just gas and electric. Through our unique combination of household heroes and energy assets, we’re at the heart of the energy transition in Ireland, strengthening the country’s energy security and helping customers get ready for a net zero future.
 
 An exciting opportunity has arisen to join Centrica’s Legal Infrastructure team for a Legal Counsel - Infrastructure & Projects as the team grows to support significant infrastructure investment across Ireland and the UK.
  
 As Centrica’s Irish infrastructure portfolio expands across generation, storage, renewables, grid and emerging energy technologies, this new role will support projects central to Ireland and the United Kindgom’s energy security, decarbonisation and infrastructure development.
  
 Location 
 This role is ideally based in Dublin, where the successful candidate will work closely with colleagues supporting Centrica's growing infrastructure portfolio in Ireland.
  
 We are also open to considering applications from candidates based elsewhere in Ireland or the UK, provided you are able to travel regularly to Dublin and our Reading, UK, office as required. While we welcome applications from a wider geographical area, there is a strong preference for the successful candidate to be based in or near Dublin.
  
 About the Role 
 As part of Centrica’s Legal Infrastructure team, you will be supporting major infrastructure and energy projects across their lifecycle, working closely with project, engineering, procurement, commercial and operational teams across both Ireland and the wider Centrica group.
  
 Key responsibilities include:
 Advising on the development, delivery and operation of major infrastructure and energy projects.
 Drafting, reviewing and negotiating construction, engineering, consultancy and project-related documentation.
 Supporting procurement, governance, regulatory, planning, environmental and consenting workstreams.
 Advising on construction, project delivery, land, property, infrastructure rights and dispute-related matters.
 Supporting investment approvals, board papers and strategic decision-making processes.
 Managing external legal advisers and supporting effective management of legal spend, precedents, guidance and training materials.
 Monitoring legal and regulatory developments and helping to build knowledge and capability across the Legal Infrastructure team.
 Supporting the development of legal colleagues by sharing infrastructure and construction law expertise and best practice.

 Here’s what we’re looking for: 
 Qualified solicitor or barrister in Ireland, the UK or another recognised common law jurisdiction, eligible to practise in Ireland.
 The responsibilities associated with this position would be suited to an individual with 1 to 4 years of post-qualification experience in private practice, industry or both; however, BGE welcomes applications from all candidates interested in opportunities at this level.
 Experience in infrastructure, construction, energy, engineering or major projects.
 Strong drafting, negotiation, legal risk and commercial advisory skills.
 Able to manage stakeholders and competing priorities independently in a fast-paced environment.
 Collaborative, adaptable and keen to broaden legal expertise and expand AI use.
 Experience in energy, utilities, infrastructure, NEC/FIDIC or other construction contracts.
 Exposure to procurement, planning, environmental, property or land rights matters.
 
 Why this role? 
 In this role you will work on significant energy infrastructure projects supporting Ireland and the United Kingdom’s energy security and net zero ambitions.
 Gain full lifecycle project exposure across generation, storage, renewables and emerging technologies.
 Develop broad expertise across construction, procurement, planning, property, governance and commercial contracting.
 Be part of Centrica’s Legal Infrastructure team, working with senior stakeholders and experienced colleagues across Ireland and the UK, with strong professional development opportunities across the group.
 
 Why should you apply?    
  
We’re not a perfect place – but we’re a people place. Our priority is supporting all of the different realities our people face. Life is about so much more than work. We get it. That’s why we’ve designed our total rewards to give you the flexibility to choose what you need, when you need it, making sure that you and your family are supported not only financially, but physically and emotionally too. Visit the link below to discover why we’re a great place to work and what being part of more means for you.  
  
 https://www.morethanacareer.energy/bordgais  
   
 If you're full of energy, fired up about sustainability, and ready to craft not only a better tomorrow, but a better you, then come and find your purpose in a team where your voice matters, your growth is non-negotiable, and your ambitions are our priority.    
 
 Help us, help you. We would love for you to share any information about yourself throughout our recruitment process so that we can better understand you and help shape your journey.

title: Associate Auditor - Audit Services
description:
About Northern Trust: 
 
 Northern Trust, a Fortune 500 company, is a globally recognized, award-winning financial institution that has been in continuous operation since 1889.
 
 Northern Trust is proud to provide innovative financial services and guidance to the world’s most successful individuals, families, and institutions by remaining true to our enduring principles of service, expertise, and integrity. With more than 130 years of financial experience and over 22,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service.
 
 
 Role 
 
 The Associate Auditor is responsible for performing and documenting routine audit examinations across Northern Trust Corporation. Reporting directly to an Audit Team Lead, the role is accountable for completing audit activities in line with established budgets, timelines, and departmental standards. The Associate Auditor also contributes insights and recommendations to improve operational efficiency and to enhance the design and operating effectiveness of the internal control environment.
 
 The key responsibilities of the role include: 
 
 Performs review of various departments by understanding the key risks and controls within the function being reviewed. Develops and executes test steps, documents results and evaluates results to assess the quality of the control and/or control environment

 Responsible for staying current on regulatory rules and changes within the industry

 Manages and performs special projects as assigned

 Participates in meetings with business unit to discuss audit results

 Communicates with partners at all levels, developing and presenting recommendations on operations and controls for the business unit

 Utilizes understanding of various Corporate units to ensure operations, services, and systems have proper audit controls in place (i.e., design of the control environment)

 Evaluates corporate management, business processes, business controls and operating practices during audits and consulting/monitoring engagements

 Applies analytical skills to review information and determine potential control weaknesses

 Develops a thorough understanding of the Northern Trust Audit Methodology and adheres to all applicable Department Standards

 Completes and compiles a high quality summary of findings and recommendations for review in a concise and professional manner

 
 Skills/ Qualifications: 
 
 The successful candidate will ideally demonstrate:
 Knowledge of auditing within the financial services industry, including a sound understanding of basic accounting principles, supported by a college or university degree and/or entry‑level auditing experience within a financial institution

 Professional certifications (e.g. CPA, CISA, CIA, ACA, ACCA) and/or an MBA, with demonstrated technical expertise in areas such as accounting, regulatory compliance, or risk management, preferred

 Strong analytical and organisational skills, with the ability to plan, execute, and support audit activities effectively

 Clear and effective report writing capabilities, alongside strong workpaper documentation skills and attention to detail

 
 Working with Us: 
 As a Northern Trust partner, greater achievements await. You will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture in an organization where financial strength and stability is an asset that emboldens us to explore new ideas.
 
 Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to assisting the communities we serve! Join a workplace with a greater purpose.
 
 We’d love to learn more about how your interests and experience could be a fit with one of the world’s most admired and sustainable companies! Build your career with us and apply today. #MadeForGreater
 
 Reasonable accommodation 
 
 Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com .
 
 We hope you’re excited about the role and the opportunity to work with us. We value an inclusive workplace and understand flexibility means different things to different people.
 
 Apply today and talk to us about your flexible working requirements and together we can achieve greater.

description:
At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com .
 
 As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.
 
 
 Job Function: 
MedTech Sales 
 
 Job Sub Function: 
Clinical Sales – Surgeons (Commission) 
 
 Job Category: 
Professional 
 
 All Job Posting Locations: 
Dublin, Ireland 
 
 Job Description: 
 DePuy Synthes is part of the Johnson & Johnson Medical Devices family and the largest, most innovative, and comprehensive orthopaedic and neurological business in the world. We offer an unparalleled breadth and depth of products, services, and programs in the areas of joint reconstruction, trauma, spine, sports medicine, neurological, craniomaxillofacial, power tools and biomaterials.
 At DePuySynthes Spine, we are inspired by the opportunity to work together with our Doctors, Nurses and Hospitals, to advance patient care. We strive to deliver innovative solutions to help with today's healthcare challenges - advancing patient care and delivering clinical and economic value to our healthcare systems throughout the world.

 Our expansive portfolio of spinal care solutions and treatment options are available in key areas including thoracolumbar, cervical, aging spine, interbody fusion, and arthroplasty, with innovation and new technologies central to the future of surgery, as we move more and more to a Digital and MedTech company.

 Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopaedics business to establish a standalone orthopaedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and approvals.
 Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans. In that case, details of any planned changes would be provided to you by DePuy Synthes at an appropriate time and subject to any necessary consultation processes. 

 Johnson & Johnson Medical Devices Ireland has an exciting opportunity to join our DePuySynthes Spine team.
 We are looking for someone, who is Passionate about SPINE , and excited about the opportunity to make a difference to peoples lives!

 The role: 
 In this role as a Spine Sales Specialists, you will be a master of your own destiny, responsible for being that central point of contact for Surgeons and Hospital teams to become a trusted support as they deliver the best possible care for their patients.
 You will maintain an existing customer base but also develop new customers, delivering sales in strategic accounts primarily concentrated in Dublin.

 Area of responsibility: 
 Identify and understand customer challenges and requirements and using the full breath of Johnson & Johnson / DePuySynthes resources, help find solutions.
 Lead in exciting new go-to-market opportunities to build long term meaningful relationships with your customers.
 
 To be in a position to achieve these exciting goals, a minimum standard of proficiencies would be required including:
 Procedural & Product understanding to ensure the provision of In-theatre support to consultants & nursing staff during surgery
 Providing first class service and flawless supply to customers including training, stock checks, timely deliveries and supporting the theatre team to ensure the operation proceeds optimally
 Working collaboratively with your Spine Team Colleagues, Business lead, and J&J teams & functions to maximise the benefits of working in a larger organisation
 Achieve Business goals in line with CREDO Values
 Adherence in full to Johnson & Johnson HCC (Healthcare Compliance) Standards, and standards of Business Conduct
 Job Scope: 
 Field position (Dublin based) Sales coverage and case support within Ireland as required
 Overnight stays may be required along with some international travel occasionally
 Desirable: 
 Proven experience in health sciences / anatomy and / or arthroscopy
 Medical Sales / record of delighting your customers
 
 Qualifications: 

 Crucial: Solid understanding of the Irish Hospital environment, both HSE & Private. Astute commercial drive and acuity.
 Desirable. A degree in medical/science/sports science/business/technology or other relevant qualifications e.g. ODP, RGN, Physiotherapy

 Skills and Aptitudes: 
 Engaging interpersonal skills with a positive outlook to make things better
 Excellent communication and team-working skills
 Dynamic and hard-working individual who is excited by new technologies and their developments in medical devices.
 Proactive - anticipates problems, shows initiative for problem-solving and generating new insights
 Resilient -able to work in an ambitious and fast paced environment.
 
 Benefits: 

 Competitive salary with additional significant commission earning opportunities.
 Company Car, Defined Benefit Pension, Private Healthcare Insurance, Lunch Allowance.
 If joining our unique Spine team within the broadest Healthcare company in the world appeals to you, reach out today to our specialist recruitment team – and help us improve Irish patients' lives for the future.

 Johnson & Johnson is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local law. We actively seek qualified candidates who are protected veterans and individuals with disabilities as defined under VEVRAA and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act.
 Johnson & Johnson is committed to providing an interview process that is inclusive of our applicants’ needs. If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request an accommodation, external applicants please contact us via https://www.jnj.com/contact-us/careers , internal employees contact AskGS to be directed to your accommodation resource.
 
 
  
  
 Required Skills: 
  
  
 Preferred Skills: 
Business Development, Communication, Customer Centricity, Customer Retentions, Execution Focus, Healthcare Trends, Market Knowledge, Market Research, Presentation Design, Problem Solving, Sales, Solutions Selling, Stakeholder Engagement, Strategic Sales Planning, Sustainable Procurement, Team Management, Vendor Selection   
  
 The anticipated base pay range for this position is: 
€65.700,00 - €105.685,00  
  
 Benefits: 
 In addition to base pay, we offer the following benefits*: an annual bonus with set target (% of pay) depending on pay grade / location, where the actual amount is based on the employees’ and companies’ performance of the previous calendar year, or sales commissions. Moreover, we offer vacation days, parental leave for a minimum of 12 weeks, bereavement leave, caregiver leave, volunteer leave, well-being reimbursement, programs for financial, physical and mental health. We also offer service anniversary and recognition awards, and subject to the terms of their respective plans, employees - and in some location’s eligible dependents - can participate in several insurance plans. For more information, visit Employee benefits | Supporting well-being & career growth | Johnson & Johnson Careers.

title: Quantitative Sports Trader
description:
Overview 

 This is a trading and quantitative strategy role focused primarily on trading on prediction markets. You will make fast, informed trading decisions while developing and maintaining the quantitative models, data pipelines, and tools that drive trading performance. The role blends hands-on trading with quantitative research, model development, and product ownership — ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of markets, analytics, and technology.
  
 In this role, you will: 
 Trade using in-house models, data-driven insights, and automated tools to maximize expectancy and meet business objectives. 
 Take ownership of trading strategies and associated models — designing, implementing, and refining logic for execution, pricing, and market-making. 
 Collaborate closely with quantitative researchers and engineers to identify, design, and deploy model enhancements, data features, and trading infrastructure improvements. 
 Perform post-trade analysis of decisions, model performance, and market behavior to inform strategy development and model calibration. 
 Identify opportunities in prediction market dynamics — pricing inefficiencies, liquidity behavior, or reaction times — to strengthen the team’s edge. 
 Drive innovation in trading methodology, tooling, and data usage across the trading and quantitative teams. 
 
 What we're looking for 

 Bachelor’s degree or higher in a technical or quantitative discipline (e.g., Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Physics, Economics). 

 Deep domain expertise and passion for sports such as Football, Soccer or Golf, including understanding of tactical, statistical, and market aspects of the sport and direct experience trading them.  

 Demonstrated ability in Python, including strong experience with data manipulation (Pandas, NumPy), statistical analysis, and automation. 

 Experience integrating data and models into production trading workflows is a strong plus. 

 Exceptional quantitative reasoning, analytical, and problem-solving skills. 

 Experience trading or modelling in fast-moving, competitive markets (prediction markets, exchanges, or similar). 

 Ability to operate across both trading and quantitative research, bridging analytical insight with execution. 

 Comfort taking product ownership — defining priorities, implementing features, and improving workflows end-to-end. 

 Strong communication skills, both for collaboration and articulating decision rationale. 

 Flexibility with working hours to align with global game/match/tournament schedules.

title: Office Fit Out Operative
description:
Fit-out Operative Required – Baldonnell, Dublin 

 About Your New Employer 
Our client is a well-established interiors and fit-out company with a strong presence across Dublin. They specialise in commercial interiors, furniture installation, relocation, and fit-out services, working with a range of office and commercial clients.
Due to continued growth, they are currently seeking an experienced Fit-out Operative to join their team based in Baldonnell, Dublin.
This is a semi-mobile role, with regular travel to offices and commercial sites across Dublin. When you are not working on-site, you will be based in the warehouse supporting the day-to-day operation.

 About Your New Job 
As a Fit-out Operative, you will be responsible for carrying out furniture moves, repairs, installations, and general fit-out duties at client offices across Dublin.
You will also spend time working in the warehouse, preparing furniture and equipment for jobs, organising stock, and ensuring materials are ready for delivery and installation.
The ideal candidate will be practical, reliable, physically capable, and comfortable working both independently and as part of a team.
Your main responsibilities will include:
 Travelling to offices and commercial sites across Dublin to carry out furniture moves, repairs, installations, and general fit-out works.
 Moving, assembling, dismantling, and positioning office furniture.
 Carrying out basic furniture repairs and maintenance where required.
 Loading and unloading furniture, equipment, and materials safely.
 Operating a forklift safely and efficiently within the warehouse and on-site where required.
 Supporting the warehouse team with receiving, storing, organising, and preparing stock.
 Preparing furniture and equipment for upcoming fit-out and relocation projects.
 Keeping the warehouse clean, organized, and safe.
 Ensuring tools, equipment, and materials are maintained and available when required.
 Working professionally when attending client offices and commercial premises.
 Following all health & safety procedures and company guidelines.
 Carrying out general warehouse and fit-out duties as required.
 
 What Skills You Need 
To be successful in this role, you should have:
 Previous experience in a fit-out, furniture installation, warehouse, construction, maintenance, or similar role.
 A valid forklift license – essential.
 Good practical and mechanical aptitude with the ability to carry out basic repairs and furniture assembly.
 The ability to safely lift and move furniture and other materials.
 A full clean driving license would be an advantage due to the semi-mobile nature of the role.
 Good communication skills and a professional manner when dealing with clients.
 The ability to work independently and as part of a wider team.
 A flexible approach to working between the warehouse and various client sites across Dublin.
 Reliability, punctuality, and a strong work ethic.
 A good understanding of health & safety procedures.
 
 What’s on Offer 
 Competitive salary depending on experience.
 24 days annual leave.
 Pension plan.
 Life insurance.
 Health insurance.
 Full-time, Monday–Friday position.
 A varied role combining warehouse and on-site work.
 Opportunity to work across a range of commercial fit-out and office projects throughout Dublin.
 Long-term career opportunity with an established and growing company.
 
 What’s Next 
If you’re an experienced Fit-out Operative, Furniture Installer, Warehouse Operative, or skilled general operative looking for a varied role based in Baldonnell with regular work across Dublin, we’d like to hear from you.
Apply now for more information.
Please send your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your experience and suitability for this role to Mlyons@sigmar.ie or call 086 771 8859 for a confidential discussion.

title: 360 Excavator Operator
description:
360 Excavator Operator – Dublin 

 About Your New Employer 
Our client is a well-established civil engineering and groundworks contractor delivering a range of infrastructure and construction projects across Dublin and the surrounding areas. With a strong reputation for quality workmanship, safety, and professionalism, they continue to secure major projects and are now looking to recruit an experienced 360 Excavator Operator to join their growing team.
This is an excellent opportunity to secure long-term work on a busy construction site, with the potential to be offered a permanent position for the right candidate.

 About Your New Job 
As a 360 Excavator Operator, you will play a key role in the day-to-day running of site operations, ensuring excavation and groundwork activities are completed safely, efficiently, and to a high standard. You will work closely with the site management team and groundworkers to support the successful delivery of the project.

 Your main responsibilities will include: 
 Operating a 360 Excavator safely and efficiently on a busy construction site.
 Carrying out excavation works for foundations, drainage, utilities, and other civil engineering activities.
 Digging trenches and preparing ground in accordance with site drawings and specifications.
 Backfilling, grading, levelling, and reinstating ground as required.
 Loading dumpers and moving materials safely around site.
 Working in close proximity to underground and overhead services while following all safety procedures.
 Assisting groundworkers and other site personnel when plant operation is not required.
 Carrying out daily pre-start inspections and basic maintenance checks on the excavator.
 Reporting any defects or maintenance issues to site management promptly.
 Following site instructions from the Foreman and Project Manager.
 Maintaining a clean, organised, and safe working environment at all times.
 Adhering to all Health & Safety regulations, company procedures, and wearing the appropriate PPE.
 
 What Skills You Need 
To be successful in this role, you should have:
 Previous experience operating a 360 Excavator on construction or civil engineering projects.
 A valid CSCS 360 Excavator Ticket (essential).
 Safe Pass (essential).
 Manual Handling certification (essential).
 Experience working around drainage, utilities, and groundworks is highly desirable.
 A strong understanding of safe excavation practices and health & safety procedures.
 The ability to work independently while also contributing as part of a site team.
 Good communication skills, reliability, and a strong work ethic.
 Own transport is advantageous but not essential depending on location.
 
 What's on Offer 
 Competitive hourly rate, depending on experience.
 Long-term contract on a major construction project in Dublin.
 Opportunity to secure a permanent position with a growing civil engineering contractor.
 Full-time Monday to Friday hours with overtime opportunities available.
 Immediate start for the right candidate.
 A safe, professional, and supportive working environment with ongoing project opportunities.
 
 What's Next 
If you're an experienced 360 Excavator Operator looking for your next long-term opportunity in Dublin, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply today with your up-to-date CV to mlyons@sigmar.ie or call or Whatsapp Michael on 086 771 8859 for more details

title: Medical Science Liaison/Medical Advisor – GI Oncology
description:
Medical Science Liaison/Medical Advisor – GI Oncology   
 50% Field – 50% Office based 
 Location: Dublin, Ireland 
 Competitive salary & excellent company benefits 
   
 About AstraZeneca 
 AstraZeneca is a global, science-led, patient-focused biopharmaceutical company that focuses on the discovery, development and commercialisation of prescription medicines for some of the world’s most serious diseases. But we’re more than one of the world’s leading pharmaceutical companies
  
 Business Area 
 Taking a forward-looking approach we look at the world through a different lens. We go above and beyond to find solutions that impact patients – harnessing science with technology and connecting the entire healthcare ecosystem.
  
 We live in a hybrid space – one foot in the scientific world, the other partnering with the business. This is a place for strong communicators, resilient and fast-paced, who bring new ideas to the table then make them a reality.
  
 We are currently looking for a Medical Science Liaison/Medical Advisor to play a leading role in our Oncology team.
   
 MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSABILITIES 
 The role is responsible for being the first point of contact for any medical/scientific aspect or issue related to the assigned oncology products and therapy area by engaging in Scientific Exchange with AstraZeneca teams, Key External Experts, Health Care Professionals, and Clinical Investigators. The role engages with external experts to identify medical unmet needs, evidence gaps and gain insight, and delivers presentations in a non-promotional scientific context as determined by the global / local Medical Affairs plans. For this position, the successful candidate will have hybrid responsibilities (50% field based; 50% office based with medical affairs responsibilities).
   
 MAIN ACCOUNTABILITIES 
 The role broadly includes the following key components:
 Build and maintain robust expertise in your therapeutic area by continuous education, active monitoring of the scientific literature and by participation in national and international congresses and AstraZeneca events 
 Develop and implement the local medical plan to address unmet medical needs in priority disease areas and ensure alignment with the brand plan in the local market 
 Be a core member of the cross-functional team and drive the implementation of initiatives and projects such as medical education and communication, scientific exchange, mapping and insight gathering and evidence generation within a specific therapy area, ensuring they are medically and scientifically accurate and compliant 
 Build, enhance and maintain the engagement with key opinion leaders 
 Help set up and provide medical-scientific training and further education in your therapeutic area for AZ personnel 
 Proactively contribute medical & clinical expertise and insights to the brand strategy, for the successful launch and life cycle management (LCM) of new & growth products
 Organisation and execution of scientific events such as symposia, other educational initiatives for healthcare professionals 
 Providing scientific input into the scoping & horizon scanning meetings, rapid reviews & health technology assessment (clinical section) in collaboration with the market access team 
 Organisation of and conducting of local advisory board meetings 
 Develop and maintain contacts with Scientific Societies/Communities including attendance at relevant national and international congresses 
 Interact with other Medical team members from other countries or other TAs in order to exchange best practice and further shape the role 
 Ensure compliance with all local regulatory requirements and AstraZeneca Local and Global Policies and Guidelines 
 Review promotional and scientific documents for content accuracy and compliance 
   
 Other responsibilities may include: 
 Respond to medical and scientific queries along with the Medical Information / Patient Safety team 
 Discuss with Investigators and review proposals for independent studies (ESR Externally Sponsored Research) and follow the relevant process for managing externally sponsored research 
 Management of early access medicine requests as per local policy 
 Support the market access team in scientific communication with health care authorities 
 
 Essential for the role 
 Minimum: Life Sciences Degree. MD, pharmacist or PhD preferable. 
 Strong understanding of oncology therapeutic area or ability to acquire this knowledge rapidly 
 Professional experience of working in healthcare related industries 
 High-level of scientific knowledge and ability to analyse and process clinical and scientific data 
 Strong communication and presentation skills, including communicating complex technical, scientific, or medical information to various audiences 
 Excellent project management ability 
 Experience in liaising with healthcare professionals 
 Quick self-learner, ability and willingness to work in a team and independently 
 Driving license, and willingness to drive within Ireland 
 
 Desirable for the role 
 Experience working in the pharmaceutical industry, preferentially within Medical Affairs 
 Experience in engaging with health care regulatory authorities 
 Experience in pre-launch, peri-launch and post-launch phase of a product as part of its life cycle management 
 Knowledge of the local regulatory and market access requirements related to medical affairs activities 
 Knowledge of the legal and ethical framework and the procedural guidelines that apply to the promotion and approval of medicinal products in Ireland 
 
 Why AstraZeneca 
 At AstraZeneca we’re dedicated to being a Great Place to Work. Where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and unleash your entrepreneurial spirit. There’s no better place to make a difference to medicine, patients and society. An inclusive culture that champions diversity and collaboration, and always committed to lifelong learning, growth and development. We’re on an exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare. 
   
 So, what’s next?   
 Are you already imagining yourself joining our team? Good, because we can’t wait to hear from you.
   
 Where can you find more? 
 Our Social Media, Follow AstraZeneca on LinkedIn 
 Follow AstraZeneca on Facebook 
 Follow AstraZeneca on Instagram

08-Oct-2026 
 Closing Date 
21-Oct-2026 
 
Our mission is to build an inclusive and equitable environment. We want people to feel they belong at AstraZeneca and Alexion, starting with our recruitment process. We welcome and consider applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of characteristics. We offer reasonable adjustments/accommodations to help all candidates to perform at their best. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential.
Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all.

Role

• Experience with monitoring tools (e.g., Azure Monitor, Log Analytics).
• Excellent problem-solving and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications
• Microsoft Certified: Azure Database Administrator Associate or equivalent.
• Experience with hybrid cloud or multi-cloud environments.
• Familiarity with data warehousing and ETL processes.
• Experience with scripting languages (PowerShell, Python).

description:
Your New Employer 
 Your new employer is a well-established multidisciplinary engineering consultancy with a strong reputation for delivering high-quality building services solutions across Ireland.
 Based in Dublin, you will join an experienced engineering team working on major projects across the commercial, residential, healthcare, education, industrial and public sectors. The company offers a collaborative working environment with strong opportunities for professional development and career progression.
 
 Your New Role 
 As Mechanical Engineer, you will be involved in the design and delivery of mechanical building services projects from initial concept through to construction and handover.
 Working alongside senior engineers, technicians and other engineering disciplines, your responsibilities will include:
 Designing mechanical building services, including HVAC, ventilation, heating, cooling, water services and drainage systems.
 Completing heating and cooling load calculations, equipment selections and system sizing.
 Producing mechanical specifications, technical reports, schedules and design documentation.
 Reviewing and coordinating mechanical drawings and BIM models.
 Working closely with electrical, structural and civil engineering teams to produce coordinated designs.
 Attending client, design-team and project coordination meetings.
 Liaising with architects, contractors, suppliers and other project stakeholders.
 Reviewing technical submittals and responding to RFIs and design queries.

 Supporting projects throughout the construction, commissioning and handover stages.
 Ensuring designs comply with Irish Building Regulations, relevant standards and client requirements.
 
 What You'll Need to Succeed 
 A degree in Mechanical Engineering, Building Services Engineering or a related discipline.

 Experience designing HVAC, heating, ventilation, water services and drainage systems.
 Strong knowledge of Irish Building Regulations and relevant mechanical engineering standards.
 Experience using software such as AutoCAD, Revit, IES, Hevacomp or similar design packages.
 The ability to produce calculations, specifications, schedules and technical reports.
 Previous experience working within an engineering consultancy would be highly advantageous.
 Strong communication and coordination skills.
 The ability to manage technical responsibilities across multiple projects.
 A proactive approach to problem-solving and project delivery.
 
 What You'll Get in Return 
 You will receive a competitive salary and benefits package along with the opportunity to work on a varied portfolio of high-profile engineering projects.
 You will benefit from structured career development, support towards professional chartership and the opportunity to learn from experienced engineers within a respected multidisciplinary consultancy. The position also offers long-term progression and the chance to take on increasing technical and project responsibilities as your experience develops.

title: Consultant, Workday Reporting and Data
description:
About Northern Trust 

 As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. 

 Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. 

 With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. 

 Job Description 
 
 At Northern Trust, data drives all of our decision-making, and HR is no exception. The HR Technology Capabilities team pioneers Northern Trust’s approach to talent strategy and organizational growth. As a member of the team, you will play an important role in helping our HR department address the people-related data and analytical needs of internal clients across the globe.
 
 Supporting the team as a Consultant for Workday reporting, you will be pivotal to the digital transformation of our HR function to develop business intelligence products and reports to enable HR processes and drive human capital decisions. You will be working with different HR COEs to develop reporting solutions across all functional areas of HR, such as compensation, time, talent, etc. This is an exciting opportunity to be a part of HR’s digital transformation and pioneer a team of report writers and data scientists to drive a data culture.
 
 The key responsibilities of the role include: 
 Work closely with stakeholders to deliver report solutions and anticipate report needs.

 Perform reporting change requests related to business process flow and security based on business requirements.

 Respond to HR data requests on an ad hoc basis by gathering, analyzing, and reporting relevant data from various sources.

 Demonstrate an understanding of confidentiality requirements relating to HR and Financial data.

 Identify opportunities to streamline HR processes and drive productivity through reporting solutions.

 Train and guide junior report writers and data stewards on workday reporting capabilities.

 Facilitate data extraction, collection, and other strategies that will help optimize efficiency and data quality.

 
 Skills/ Qualifications 
 Intermediate to advanced knowledge in complex report development in Workday for HR (advanced report, discovery boards, composite reports, trending reports, calculated fields)

 A strong understanding of data needs for analysis and business management

 Strong analytical skills with the ability to pinpoint problems in data records based on analysis

 
 The successful candidate will benefit from having: 
 Experience with Prism Analytics or Core HCM

 3 to 5 years of work experience in any area of HR

 
 Work Authorization 

 Applicants must have the right to work in Ireland at the time of application and for the duration of employment.

 Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide employment permit sponsorship for this role. This includes Critical Skills Employment Permits, General Employment Permits, Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permits, Stamp 1G permissions, and other employment permits under Irish immigration frameworks.

 Working with Us 

 As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve. 

 Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities. 

 Reasonable Accommodation 

 Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com , or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.

title: Supplier Quality Engineer
description:
Supplier Quality Engineer Location: Galway
Permanent - Full-Time
Sector: Medical Devices
 The Opportunity We are seeking a Supplier Quality Engineer to join a leading organisation in the medical device sector. This is an excellent opportunity for a quality professional to play a key role in ensuring supplier performance, product quality, and compliance with stringent regulatory and quality management system requirements.
 Working closely with suppliers and cross-functional teams, you will support supplier qualification, auditing, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives to ensure the consistent delivery of high-quality components and services.
 Key Responsibilities Manage supplier quality activities for components, ensuring compliance with applicable quality standards, regulatory requirements, and internal procedures.

 Maintain and update the Approved Supplier List (ASL), supporting supplier selection, assessment, and qualification.

 Apply quality engineering tools and methodologies, including Statistical Process Control (SPC), process capability studies, and IQ/OQ/PQ.

 Lead 8D investigations and drive supplier corrective and preventive actions to address quality issues and prevent recurrence.

 Review supplier non-conformances and customer complaints, ensuring appropriate investigation and resolution.

 Conduct supplier audits, follow up on audit findings, and ensure timely closure of corrective actions.

 Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Factory, Sourcing, CME, AME, and R&D, to resolve quality issues and support business objectives.

 Support the timely delivery of conforming components through appropriate acceptance criteria, AQL sampling, and incoming inspection processes.

 Contribute to CAPA activities, supplier transfers, and ongoing process improvement initiatives.

 Help maintain supplier compliance with FDA, EU MDR, and internal Quality Management System (QMS) requirements.

 Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline.

 Minimum of two years’ experience in Quality Engineering or Supplier Quality within a relevant technical or manufacturing environment.

 Working knowledge of plastic injection moulding and assembly processes.

 Strong communication and problem-solving skills, with a good standard of written and spoken English.

 Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail, and a dependable approach to managing priorities.

 Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.

 Desirable Skills Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.

 Experience with supplier audits, corrective action investigations, process validation, and continuous improvement methodologies.

 What’s on Offer? The opportunity to contribute to product quality and supplier performance within the medical device industry.

 A collaborative, cross-functional working environment.

 A competitive salary and benefits package, with compensation reflecting relevant skills, qualifications, experience, and location.

 Eligibility for a discretionary annual bonus and potential participation in long-term incentive plans, subject to applicable company terms and role eligibility.

 Apply Now If you have experience in Supplier Quality and are interested in contributing to quality and compliance within a regulated manufacturing environment, we would welcome your application.

title: Sr. Analyst, Payroll AMR
description:
Logitech is the Sweet Spot for people who want their actions to have a positive global impact while having the flexibility to do it in their own way.
 
 
 Global Payroll Senior Analyst 
  
 Position Summary: 
 ●      Department: Controllership Finance – Global Payroll Team
 ●       Location: Cork, Ireland - On site 2 days a week 
 ●      Contract Type: Full Time / Permanent
 ●      Region Coverage: AMR 

 About the Role: 
 As an integral member of Logitech Finance, you will work in a fast-paced, dynamic Global Payroll team processing payrolls across the Americas region — covering the United States, Canada, and Latin America. You will play a key role in ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely payroll delivery, while helping to drive continuous improvement across our payroll operations.
   
 Your Contribution: 
 Be Yourself. Be Open. Stay Hungry and Humble. Collaborate. Challenge. Decide and Do.
 In this role you will:
   
 ●      Ensure the accurate and timely processing of Logitech’s end-to-end payroll for the AMR region (USA, Canada, and LATAM).
 ●      Collaborate with payroll partners to collect and validate all payroll inputs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, allowances, and deductions. Conduct rigorous pre- and post-payroll reconciliations to eliminate anomalies or duplicate records before finalization.
 ●      Ensure the accurate and timely completion of payroll fiscal close procedures, including journal entries and balance sheet reconciliations. Work with the broader Finance team to identify and resolve payroll accounting exceptions.
 ●      Understand the full payroll cycle through to GL bookings and present meaningful flux analysis to stakeholders.
 ●      Stay current on and ensure strict compliance with federal, state/provincial, and local payroll regulations, tax laws, social security, and benefits requirements across all AMR jurisdictions.
 ●      Ensure compliance with payroll internal controls, maintaining robust documentation and proactively identifying and remediating any control gaps or weaknesses. Assist in facilitating internal and external audit engagements.
 ●      Partner with key stakeholders including People Services, HRIS, Compensation & Benefits, Stock Admin, and Finance to troubleshoot issues and work collaboratively to develop optimum processes and service delivery.
 ●      Drive the payroll Global Finance Transformation roadmap, focusing on eliminating manual workflows and implementing scalable, automated payroll solutions.
 ●      Collaborate with internal and external partners to drive automation and enhance service delivery.

 Your Skills & Experience: 
 Beyond core technical payroll knowledge, we are seeking an innovative, highly data-literate payroll professional who actively identifies opportunities to leverage modern tools, AI, and emerging technologies to automate workflows and transform end-to-end payroll operations.
 For consideration, you must bring the following skills, experience and behaviours to our team:
  
 ●      Experience: 3+ years of proven experience in a senior analyst payroll role, specifically working with Americas payroll (US required; Canada and LATAM experience is a major plus).
 ●      Education & Certification: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field—or an equivalent payroll certification.
 ●      Regulatory Compliance: Solid understanding of US/Canadian payroll taxes, statutory deductions, and labour regulations.
 ●      Hands-on experience processing payroll and running reports in Workday and/or Dayforce (Ceridian).
 ●      Spreadsheet Skills: Advanced proficiency in MS Excel and Google Sheets (must be comfortable using Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and managing large data sets).
 ●      Familiarity with how HRIS data flows into downstream payroll and Finance/GL systems.
 ●      Strong ability to perform pre- and post-payroll reconciliations, investigate gross-to-net variances, and flag data errors before finalization.
 ●      Experience supporting month-end close procedures, including preparing journal entries and assisting Finance/FP&A teams with cost analysis.
 ●      Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills to partner effectively across HR, Finance, and external vendors.
 ●      Ability to stay organized and solve problems independently in a fast-paced, global team environment.
 ●      Customer service focus with the ability and sound judgment to handle highly sensitive information.
 ●      Process improvement mindset: have a passion for reengineering payroll processes in implementing a first-class payroll service.
 ●      Strong interest in applying emerging technologies—such as AI, ML, and RPA—to re-engineer enterprise payroll workflows, eliminate manual touchpoints, and unlock value-added insights for workforce planning.
  
  
 ABOUT LOGITECH
 With a fast-moving, innovative culture and a strong balance sheet, Logitech is a world leader in products that connect people to the digital experiences they care most about. Video conferencing, remote work, content creation, and gaming are long-term secular trends driving our business — and today all of them have accelerated, making Logitech more relevant to customers than ever.
 Logitech is the sweet spot for people who are passionate about products, making a mark, and having fun doing it. We're small and flexible enough for every person to take initiative — and big enough for those actions to have a global impact.
 Across Logitech we empower collaboration and foster play. We help teams collaborate/learn from anywhere, without compromising on productivity or continuity so it should be no surprise that most of our jobs are open to work from home from most locations. Our hybrid work model allows some employees to work remotely while others work on-premises. Within this structure, you may have teams or departments split between working remotely and working in-house.

Logitech is an amazing place to work because it is full of authentic people who are inclusive by nature as well as by design. Being a global company, we value our diversity and celebrate all our differences. Don’t meet every single requirement? Not a problem. If you feel you are the right candidate for the opportunity, we strongly recommend that you apply. We want to meet you!
 
We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits packages and working environments that are designed to be flexible and help you to care for yourself and your loved ones, now and in the future. We believe that good health means more than getting medical care when you need it. Logitech supports a culture that encourages individuals to achieve good physical, financial, emotional, intellectual and social wellbeing so we all can create, achieve and enjoy more and support our families. We can’t wait to tell you more about them being that there are too many to list here and they vary based on location.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, age, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.

If you require an accommodation to complete any part of the application process, are limited in the ability, are unable to access or use this online application process and need an alternative method for applying, you may contact us toll free at +1-510-713-4866 for assistance and we will get back to you as soon as possible.

title: Automation Engineer
description:
Job Title: Automation Engineer
 Location: Waterford, Ireland
 Contract Type: 18-Month Fixed-Term Contract
 Shift Pattern: Standard Days
 
 About the role 
 As an Automation Engineer within the Waterford Automation & Manufacturing Systems team, you will play a critical role in supporting and advancing the site's automated manufacturing capabilities across PFS, LYO, Filling, and Packaging operations. You will be responsible for both the operational support of existing automation infrastructure and the delivery of capital improvement projects — ensuring systems are reliable, compliant, and continuously evolving in line with Sanofi's Digital Lighthouse ambitions.
 
 You will work across a broad technology stack including PLCs, SCADA, MES, Historian, and IIoT platforms, operating within a GMP-regulated environment where patient safety and product quality are paramount.
 
 Ready to get started?
 
 Join a global network that powers how Sanofi delivers — seamlessly, purposefully, and at scale. In Manufacturing & Supply, you’ll help reimagine how life-changing treatments reach people everywhere, faster.
 
 About Sanofi:  
 We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives. 
 
 Main responsibilities 
 Operational Support & System Maintenance 
 Provide day-to-day automation support for manufacturing equipment and systems across PFS, LYO, Filling, and Packaging operations
 Troubleshoot and resolve automation-related issues on Siemens S7/TIA Portal, Wonderware, iFix, and Zenon SCADA platforms to minimise production downtime
 Maintain and administer OSIsoft PI Historian and Ignition platforms, ensuring data integrity and availability for operational and quality reporting
 Manage and support Windows Server environments (including virtualised/VM infrastructure) underpinning site automation systems
 Maintain site OT network infrastructure, ensuring cybersecurity controls and network segmentation are upheld in line with site standards
 Capital Projects & Continuous Improvement 
 Lead and contribute to automation capital projects from concept through to commissioning and handover, including URS development, design review, FAT/SAT, and qualification activities
 Identify and implement automation improvements that drive efficiency, reduce waste, and support the site's Digital Lighthouse and Industry 4.0 roadmap
 Collaborate with Engineering, Operations, Quality, and global Automation teams to deliver projects on time, within budget, and to specification
 Support the integration of MES (Manufacturing Execution Systems) with automation layers to enhance data flow, traceability, and paperless manufacturing
 Computer System Validation (CSV) & GxP Compliance 
 Author and execute validation documentation (URS, FS, DS, IQ, OQ, PQ, Validation Strategy) in accordance with Sanofi's Computerised Systems Validation GOP and GAMP 5 guidelines
 Ensure all automation systems are maintained in a validated state and are inspection-ready for regulatory audits (FDA, EMA, HPRA)
 Manage change control, deviation investigations, and CAPAs related to automation systems in compliance with site GMP procedures
 Support the site's Business Quality Representative (BQR) process for GxP digital solutions
 Data & Digital 
 Leverage OSIsoft PI and Ignition platforms to develop dashboards, reports, and analytics that support operational decision-making and continuous improvement
 Contribute to IIoT and Industry 4.0 initiatives, supporting the site's Digital Lighthouse strategy through data connectivity, real-time monitoring, and smart manufacturing capabilities
 Participate in the evaluation and implementation of new digital technologies aligned with Sanofi's global automation standards
 
 About you 
 Essential Requirements 
 Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Control Systems Engineering, Automation, Mechatronics, or a related discipline
 Significant hands-on automation engineering experience in a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical or life sciences manufacturing environment
 Demonstrated experience with Siemens S7 / TIA Portal PLC programming and commissioning
 Proficiency with one or more SCADA platforms: Wonderware (AVEVA), iFix (GE), or Zenon (Copa-Data) 
 Experience with OSIsoft PI Historian and/or Ignition (Inductive Automation) platforms
 Working knowledge of Windows Server administration and virtualised (VM) environments in an OT context
 Understanding of OT/IT network architecture , including industrial networking protocols (Ethernet/IP, Profinet, Modbus TCP)
 Solid understanding of Computer System Validation (CSV) principles and GAMP 5 methodology
 Familiarity with GMP regulations and pharmaceutical manufacturing standards (FDA 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11)
 Desirable Requirements 
 Experience with MES platforms (e.g., Werum PAS-X, Rockwell PharmaSuite, or equivalent)
 Exposure to fill/finish, lyophilisation (LYO), or packaging equipment automation
 Experience with IIoT platforms and Industry 4.0 / smart manufacturing initiatives
 Knowledge of machine vision systems or robotics integration
 Project management experience in a capital projects environment
 
 Why choose us? 
 Transform lives worldwide by delivering life-changing treatments anywhere, anytime.  

 Grow, thrive, and make an impact in a workplace that empowers you to bring your best self every day, with pride.  

 Help deliver 30+ new product launches by 2030, ensuring patients get treatments faster than ever.  

 Develop new skills, explore cross-functional roles, and work in an environment that values growth and discovery.  

 
 #LI-EUR 
 
 
 Pursue progress , discover extraordinary Better is out there. Better medications, better outcomes, better science. But progress doesn’t happen without people – people from different backgrounds, in different locations, doing different roles, all united by one thing: a desire to make miracles happen. So, let’s be those people.

 Watch our ALL IN video and check out our Diversity Equity and Inclusion actions at sanofi.com !

Security and clearance eligibility: Fortinet networking and security capability, together with eligibility to obtain SC and NPPV3 clearance and undertake regular travel to police sites.
Desirable Skills / Experience
Experience working with police, blue-light, government or similarly secure and regulated customers.
Current CCNP certification, or equivalent practical networking knowledge gained through experience.
Existing SC and NPPV3 clearance.
Candidates do not need to meet every desirable skill to apply. Transferable experience is welcomed.
Our Package
Tailored benefits make a real difference. That’s why we offer a comprehensive range to support your growth, wellbeing, and everyday life.
You can design the package to suit you and your lifestyle. Your core benefits include:
• 10% on target annual bonus
• 25 days Holiday
• Access to an online private GP 24/7 for you and your immediate family
• Market-leading paid carers leave with up to 2 weeks off
• Equalized maternity, paternity, and adoption leave – 18 weeks’ full pay and 8 weeks’ half pay
• Discounted EE and BT products, including mobile and broadband
• Market leading Pension scheme – 5% from you and 10% from us
• Holiday purchase scheme
You can select additional benefits, including healthcare, dental, gym memberships and more when you’re ready.
Ready to connect for good and help shape the future? Apply now.
Join us at a pivotal moment for BT Business. We are executing a multi-year transformation to restore growth, modernise at scale and unlock new markets beyond connectivity. Our ambition is clear – return to sustainable revenue and EBITDA growth, strengthen our market position, and deliver meaningful shareholder value through disciplined execution and bold reinvention.
We are fundamentally reshaping the business – simplifying our portfolio, digitising our customer experience and building market-leading capability across cyber, AI and managed services, all powered by the UK’s leading fixed and mobile networks. This is a shift from a legacy connectivity provider to a modern, solutions-led, AI-first business that can truly differentiate in a competitive and fast-moving market.
With execution momentum building and a clear path to growth, the opportunity now is to scale what works, accelerate performance and fully realise our potential. This is about delivering against ambitious financial outcomes while transforming how we operate – creating a business that is simpler, faster, more innovative and easier to do business with.
If you want to be part of the team shaping the turnaround of a multi-billion-pound business – and building a stronger, more competitive BT for the future – this is your moment.

title: Architectural Technologist
description:
Architectural Technologist 
 
 About Your New Employer 
 
 Join a well-established Dublin-based architectural studio with decades of experience delivering innovative, high-quality projects across the residential, commercial and interiors sectors.
 You will join a collaborative and design-led team working on a diverse portfolio of residential developments.
 
 The practice offers:
 The opportunity to work on large-scale residential projects from concept through to completion.
 A supportive and experienced team environment where your technical skills will be developed and valued.
 Exposure to all stages of project delivery, including design development, technical detailing, construction and site coordination.
 Excellent opportunities for professional growth and career progression.
 The chance to work closely with experienced Associates, architects, consultants and contractors.
 
 About Your New Job 
 
 As an Architectural Technologist, you will contribute to the delivery of residential projects throughout the full project lifecycle. Working closely with the Associate and wider project team, you will take responsibility for key technical packages and support the successful delivery of projects from design through to completion.
 
 Your responsibilities will include:
 Preparing and developing technical drawings, construction details and project information.
 Supporting the delivery of large-scale residential projects from concept and planning through to construction and completion.
 Coordinating architectural information with structural, MEP and other specialist consultants.
 Ensuring designs and technical information comply with Irish Building Regulations, planning requirements and relevant standards.
 Working with architects, clients, consultants and contractors to resolve technical queries and design issues.
 Assisting with the preparation of tender and construction documentation.
 Reviewing drawings and technical information to ensure accuracy, coordination and buildability.
 Attending site inspections and meetings to monitor project progress and assist with resolving construction issues.
 Managing assigned technical packages and contributing to project programmes and delivery deadlines.
 Reporting project updates, risks and technical issues to the Associate.
 Supporting the development of less experienced team members where appropriate.
 
 This role would suit an Architectural Technologist with 3 to 5 years’ experience who is looking to broaden their project experience, take ownership of key technical responsibilities and develop towards a more senior position.
 
 What Skills You Need 
 
 3 to 5 years’ experience working as an Architectural Technologist, ideally within an architectural practice or similar consultancy environment.
 Experience working on residential projects, preferably large-scale developments.
 Good knowledge of Irish Building Regulations, planning processes, construction methods and technical detailing.
 Experience preparing technical drawings, construction information and project documentation.
 Strong proficiency in Revit and experience coordinating multidisciplinary project information.
 An understanding of project delivery from design development through to construction and completion.
 Good communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
 The ability to manage assigned tasks and technical packages while working to project deadlines.
 A proactive and collaborative approach, with the ambition to develop your project leadership skills.
 
 What’s on Offer 
 
 A competitive salary of €45,000 to €55,000, depending on experience.
 The opportunity to work on major residential projects from concept through to completion.
 The chance to take responsibility for key technical packages and develop your project management skills.
 Comprehensive health insurance.
 A supportive team environment with access to experienced senior professionals.
 Ongoing training and clear opportunities for career progression.
 The opportunity to develop towards a Senior Architectural Technologist or project leadership position.
 
 What’s Next 
 
 Apply now by clicking the “Apply Now” button or contact me at thyland@sigmar.ie / 01 474 4690.

 Excellent training and career progression

 Assembly and integration of complex mechanical and electrical equipment

 Integration and qualification of advanced semiconductor and microscope technology

 Professional-level English communication skills

 Commitment to relocating to the Netherlands for a minimum of two years

 Interested in an International Career Move? If you're an Engineer looking to gain experience with cutting-edge technology, develop your technical expertise and progress your career in the semiconductor industry, we'd love to hear from you.
 Apply today for a confidential discussion about the opportunity and relocation package.
